👉 Mẹo: câu hỏi quan hệ hiếm khi nói thẳng từ "best friend". Bắt các chi tiết định tuổi và bối cảnh như "first day of school", "just like when we were girls" để suy ra vai vế ngang hàng.

questions.prompt: A receptionist is checking the client list of a clinic. How many clients are Americans?
questions.explanation:
Right, let me check tomorrow's client list before I go home. Nine o'clock, Mrs. Schneider — she's German. Ten thirty, Mr. Lopez from Spain. Then after lunch we have Mr. Miller — he's the American gentleman, the only one this week actually. And finally Madame Dubois from France at four. So that's four clients tomorrow, and I must remember Mr. Miller prefers to pay in dollars.

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án A – One.
• Vì sao đúng: "Mr. Miller — he's the American gentleman, the only one this week actually" — chỉ đúng một khách người Mỹ.
• Two sai: hai cái tên nước ngoài khác được nhắc là Mr. Lopez from Spain và Madame Dubois from France, đều không phải người Mỹ.
• Three sai: tổng số khách ngày mai là bốn ("that's four clients tomorrow"), không có con số ba nào gắn với khách Mỹ.
👉 Mẹo: câu "how many" theo quốc tịch — đừng đếm tổng số người. Nghe cụm giới hạn "the only one", "just one of them" là ra đáp án ngay.

questions.prompt: Listen to Anna talking about her routine. Where does Anna go for a walk every morning?
questions.explanation:
My mornings are the same all year round. I get up at six, make myself a pot of tea, and spend half an hour reading before anyone else wakes up. Then I put on my trainers and go for my walk around the college — it is quiet at that hour, and the old buildings look beautiful in the morning light. By the time I get back home, I feel ready for anything the day may bring.

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án C – college.
• Vì sao đúng: "Then I put on my trainers and go for my walk around the college — it is quiet at that hour".
• park sai: không được nhắc tới trong bài, chỉ là phương án gây nhiễu.
• neighborhood sai: cũng không được nhắc tới; bài chỉ nói cô đi bộ xong thì về nhà ("By the time I get back home").
👉 Mẹo: câu hỏi "where" trong bài độc thoại thường chỉ có một địa điểm thật. Bám vào danh từ đứng ngay sau động từ của câu hỏi ("go for my walk around the...") thay vì mọi danh từ nơi chốn nghe được.

questions.prompt: Listen to a girl calling the cafe. What did she forget, and where did she leave it?
questions.explanation:
Hello, is that the Riverside Café? I was sitting at your place about an hour ago and I think I left my scarf behind. I've looked everywhere in my bag. Could you check for me, please? I remember taking it off when I sat down — we were at the little table in the corner, by the bookshelf. Yes, the corner table. If you find it, I'll come by this evening to collect it. Thank you so much!

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án B – in the corner.
• Vì sao đúng: "we were at the little table in the corner, by the bookshelf. Yes, the corner table" — cô để quên khăn ở bàn góc.
• on the counter sai: không được nhắc tới trong bài, chỉ là phương án gây nhiễu.
• near the door sai: cũng không được nhắc tới trong bài.
👉 Mẹo: dạng gọi điện tìm đồ thất lạc, vị trí đúng hay được nhắc hai lần liên tiếp để nhấn mạnh ("in the corner... the corner table"). Nghe câu lặp lại là chốt.

questions.prompt: Helen is calling a friend about the place her whole family is standing while seeing her off to college. Where are they standing?
questions.explanation:
Hi! Yes, we've just arrived — the whole family came to see me off, even grandma! Where are we standing? Well, we couldn't park near the main gate, so we're in the residential area behind the campus, you know, where all the little houses are. It's actually quieter here. Dad is unloading my boxes and mum is already crying. Come and find us — the street with the red postboxes!

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án C – Residential area.
• Vì sao đúng: "we couldn't park near the main gate, so we're in the residential area behind the campus, you know, where all the little houses are".
• library complex sai: không được nhắc tới trong bài, chỉ là phương án gây nhiễu.
• university area sai: khuôn viên trường có được nhắc, nhưng chỉ để nói họ KHÔNG đỗ xe được ở đó, và chỗ đứng nằm phía SAU campus ("behind the campus").
👉 Mẹo: chú ý giới từ chỉ vị trí (behind, next to, opposite). Nghe thấy "campus/university" đừng vội chọn phương án có chữ university — "behind the campus" là bên ngoài khuôn viên.

questions.prompt: Listen to a man talking about their train journey. What time did the train depart?
questions.explanation:
What a morning we had! Our train was timetabled for nine o'clock sharp, and we were on the platform early like good tourists. Then came the announcement: a signal problem, everything delayed. Some passengers heard ten o'clock and started queuing for refunds. In the end the train actually left at nine thirty — only half an hour late, which these days almost counts as punctual. We still made our connection, just barely.

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án B – 9:30.
• Vì sao đúng: "In the end the train actually left at nine thirty — only half an hour late".
• 9:00 sai: đó là giờ theo LỊCH in trên vé ("Our train was timetabled for nine o'clock sharp"), tàu không chạy đúng giờ đó.
• 10:00 sai: chỉ là tin đồn giữa hành khách ("Some passengers heard ten o'clock and started queuing for refunds").
👉 Mẹo: với giờ tàu/máy bay, tách ba lớp thông tin: giờ theo lịch (timetabled/scheduled), giờ đồn (some passengers heard), giờ thật (actually left). Chỉ giờ đi kèm "actually" mới là đáp án.

questions.prompt: A man is talking to a shopping assistant. What color top is he going to buy?
questions.explanation:
Woman: Good morning! Are you looking for anything special today?
Man: Yes, I need a new top — something for the office, but not too formal.
Woman: Of course. This green one is very popular at the moment. The colour suits most people, and it's twenty percent off this week.
Man: Hmm, green is a bit bright for me, to be honest. My wife says it doesn't match anything else I own. What about that blue one on the shelf?
Woman: Good choice — that one is pure cotton. But I should tell you we only have it in large, and I think you need a medium.
Man: Ah, that's a shame, it's a lovely colour. What's that darker one hanging at the back?
Woman: The black one? That's the same style as the blue, and we have every size.
Man: Perfect. Black goes with everything anyway. I'll take it in a medium, please.

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án C – Black.
• Vì sao đúng: "Black goes with everything anyway. I'll take it in a medium, please" — động từ mua thật nằm ở câu này.
• Green sai: anh chê màu quá chói và vợ nói không hợp đồ ("green is a bit bright for me... My wife says it doesn't match anything else I own").
• Blue sai: hết cỡ vừa, chỉ còn size lớn ("we only have it in large, and I think you need a medium").
👉 Mẹo: hội thoại mua sắm luôn duyệt đủ 3 món. Món đúng là món đi kèm hành động mua ("I'll take it", "I'll have that one"), không phải món được nhân viên khen nhiều nhất.

questions.prompt: A man is calling his sister. Where will they meet?
questions.explanation:
M: Hi, how are you?
W: Oh! Are you calling from America?
M: No, I've been visiting the London office for a few days. Do you want to meet up? I have to catch a train at three.
W: Yes! There's a park near my flat. The weather's lovely and sunny, and there are lots of people around. Do you want to meet there?
M: Sure. Then I can walk you to your university afterwards — I don't have to be at the station until three.
W: OK, see you soon.

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án B – At the park.
• Vì sao đúng: cô đề nghị "There's a park near my flat... Do you want to meet there?" và anh đồng ý "Sure".
• At the station sai: đó là nơi anh phải đến lúc 3 giờ SAU khi gặp.
• At the university sai: anh chỉ đi bộ đưa cô đến đó sau, không phải điểm hẹn.
👉 Mẹo: cả 3 địa điểm đều xuất hiện — chọn nơi có "meet there" + "Sure".

questions.prompt: A woman is talking about her house. What is she going to change in their house?
questions.explanation:
Woman: I've been thinking about the house again. Something has to change this year.
Man: Here we go. The car? You said the engine sounds tired.
Woman: The car is fine, it just needs a service. And before you ask — no, not the computer either. It's slow, but it works, and the children barely use it now anyway.
Man: Then what?
Woman: The window in the kitchen. It lets the cold in all winter, the frame is cracked, and I'm tired of taping it up every November. I called the fitters this morning — they can replace it next month.
Man: You already called them? So this isn't really a discussion, is it?
Woman: It's an announcement with discussion-flavoured decoration. The window is what we're changing.

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án A – The window.
• Vì sao đúng: "The window in the kitchen... I called the fitters this morning — they can replace it next month", chốt lại "The window is what we're changing".
• The car sai: cô nói xe vẫn ổn, chỉ cần bảo dưỡng ("The car is fine, it just needs a service").
• The computer sai: cô chủ động loại trước ("no, not the computer either. It's slow, but it works").
👉 Mẹo: dạng "what will they change/buy" — người nói thường tự loại trừ bằng "X is fine", "not X either" rồi mới tiết lộ đáp án ở câu khẳng định cuối. Đừng chốt sớm.

questions.prompt: The woman is calling a friend about meeting for dinner. How long does it take to get to the station?
questions.explanation:
Woman: Hi! About dinner on Saturday — I'm trying to work out when to leave home.
Man: It depends how you're coming. Driving?
Woman: No, the train. How long does it take you to get to the station from your side?
Man: From mine, about thirty minutes on the bus. But you're further out, aren't you?
Woman: That's what I'm worried about. Someone told me it takes fifty minutes from my neighbourhood, which sounds like torture.
Man: Fifty? No, that's the old route, before they opened the new road. From yours it's forty minutes now, door to door. I did it last week visiting Tom.
Woman: Forty minutes — that's not bad at all. So if dinner is at seven, I'll leave at six.
Man: Leave ten minutes earlier to be safe. See you Saturday!

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án B – 40 minutes.
• Vì sao đúng: "From yours it's forty minutes now, door to door. I did it last week visiting Tom" — đây là thời gian từ nhà người phụ nữ (người đang hỏi) tới ga.
• 30 minutes sai: đó là thời gian từ nhà NGƯỜI ĐÀN ÔNG, không phải của cô ("From mine, about thirty minutes on the bus").
• 50 minutes sai: là con số cũ theo tuyến đường trước khi mở đường mới ("that's the old route, before they opened the new road").
👉 Mẹo: câu "how long" hay gài số của người khác hoặc số lỗi thời. Xác định rõ đại từ sở hữu ("from mine" vs "from yours") và loại số đi kèm "the old route / it used to be".

questions.prompt: Four people are talking about their exercise preferences. Match each person to the correct information.
questions.explanation:
Speaker A: My weekends belong to the hills. I load the bike onto the car on Friday night, and by eight the next morning I am flying down a forest trail with mud everywhere. My friends think I am mad — the bruises, the repairs, the cold. But nothing else empties my head like picking a line between the trees at speed. I have tried gentler hobbies, honestly. None of them ever made me feel so completely awake.
Speaker B: For me it has to be simple, so I just go for a run before work. No equipment, no bookings, no team — shoes on, door shut, and thirty minutes later I am back, red-faced and happy. In summer I follow the river; in winter I do loops around my block under the streetlights. People keep inviting me to fancy gyms, and I always say the same thing: the pavement is free and it never closes.
Speaker C: My doctor told me to stay active without stressing my knees, so every evening after dinner my husband and I head out on foot and do a slow hour through the neighbourhood. We have done it so long that the neighbours joke they can set their clocks by us. It is gentle, it costs nothing, and we talk more in that hour than in the rest of the day. Not dramatic, I know — but at my age, steady beats spectacular.
Speaker D: Mine started with a birthday gift: one lesson at the stables outside town. Ten years later I am there every Saturday, brushing, saddling, and taking my favourite mare across the fields. Being carried by a living animal is nothing like any machine — you learn to listen with your whole body. It is not a cheap pastime, and my boots are permanently filthy, but walking into that yard is still the best moment of my week.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
A = Mountain biking (keyword "bike... forest trail"). B = Going for a run (keyword "go for a run"). C = Walking (PARAPHRASE: "head out on foot... slow hour through the neighbourhood" — không có chữ walk). D = Horse riding (PARAPHRASE: "stables... favourite mare... carried by a living animal" — không có chữ horse/riding). Nhiễu: Hiking, Swimming — không ai nói.

questions.prompt: There is too much information on the Internet
questions.explanation:
W: So, how did you get on with that research project you were doing online?
M: Honestly, it nearly finished me off. The real problem is that there's simply far more material out there than any one person could ever get through in a lifetime.
W: I'm not so sure about that, actually. I'd say the sheer volume isn't the issue at all. A big library has more than you could read too, and nobody ever complains about that.
M: Fair enough, but a library has been sorted out for you by somebody. Anyway, what I will say is that digging out anything reliable online is a proper skill in itself.
W: Oh, absolutely, I agree with you there. Knowing which search terms to try, and how to spot a dodgy source, is something you genuinely have to be taught.
M: Exactly. My younger cousin just clicks the very first link and believes every word of it.
W: Well, that brings me to something I've been chewing over. I reckon being online all day is actually changing how our brains work, the way we reason things through.
M: Hmm, I don't see it that way. I'll accept that our habits have shifted, of course. But our actual thinking? No, I'd say that's much the same as it's always been.
W: You say that, but I notice it in myself. I can't sit with a long article any more.
M: Maybe you're just tired. What I would definitely sign up to, though, is that teenagers these days simply can't wait for anything at all.
W: Now that I do agree with, completely. Anything that takes more than three seconds to load and they've given up entirely and moved on.
M: Same with films. My nephew watches everything on double speed, which I find slightly horrifying.
W: Guilty as charged, to be honest. I've started doing exactly that myself.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
Key: Quá nhiều thông tin trên Internet = Man · Tìm thông tin cần kỹ năng = Both · Internet ảnh hưởng cách ta tư duy = Woman · Internet khiến giới trẻ thiếu kiên nhẫn = Both

1. There is too much information on the Internet → Man: người đàn ông nêu rõ "The real problem is that there's simply far more material out there than any one person could ever get through in a lifetime." Người phụ nữ phản đối thẳng: "I'm not so sure about that, actually. I'd say the sheer volume isn't the issue at all."

2. Finding information on the Internet requires skills → Both: người đàn ông nói "digging out anything reliable online is a proper skill in itself", người phụ nữ tán thành rõ ràng: "Oh, absolutely, I agree with you there... is something you genuinely have to be taught."

3. The use of the Internet affects the way we think. → Woman: người phụ nữ nêu "I reckon being online all day is actually changing how our brains work, the way we reason things through." Người đàn ông phản đối: "Hmm, I don't see it that way... our actual thinking? No, I'd say that's much the same as it's always been."

4. The Internet makes young people less patient. → Both: người đàn ông nêu "teenagers these days simply can't wait for anything at all", người phụ nữ đồng ý: "Now that I do agree with, completely."

👉 Mẹo: Bẫy nằm ở ý 3 — người đàn ông nói "I'll accept that our habits have shifted" nghe như đồng ý, nhưng ngay sau đó bác bỏ đúng phần cốt lõi (cách tư duy), nên đáp án là Woman chứ không phải Both.

questions.prompt: Finding information on the Internet requires skills
The use of the Internet affects the way we think.
The Internet makes young people less patient.
What does the announcer say about the new novel?
options: It is different from his earlier works
It is less famous than his earlier works
questions.explanation:
Good evening, everyone. Tonight I want to talk about the latest novel by the popular author James Parker. Most of you know him for his soft, romantic stories, and before this book came out, some people even worried that a new direction would make him less famous than before. A few magazines predicted that his loyal readers would simply stop buying. Well, the opposite has happened. The new novel, Shadow in the Night, is completely different from his earlier works, and readers seem to love it for exactly that reason. Instead of gentle love stories, Parker gives us a dark mystery full of secrets and surprising turns. The mood is tense from the first chapter, and several reviewers have said they could not put the book down. Sales in the first month were actually higher than for any of his romantic titles, so the fear that this book would damage his name has disappeared completely.
Of course, the big question now is what Parker should do next. Some fans are begging him to continue with this new style of dark, exciting stories. Others, especially his older readers, hope he will go back to the romantic writing that made him famous in the first place. In my view, neither group should decide for him. What Parker really needs to do is listen carefully to what the critics are saying before he starts his next book. Their reviews point out real weaknesses as well as strengths, and a writer who takes that advice seriously will find the right balance and grow with every book he writes.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
1. Đáp án: It is different from his earlier works — "completely different from his earlier works". Bẫy: "romantic and soft" là phong cách CŨ; "less famous" chỉ là lo ngại ban đầu và đã bị bác bỏ (doanh số cao hơn).
2. Đáp án: He should listen to critics before writing his next work. Bẫy: "continue this genre" là mong muốn của fan mới, "go back to his original genre" là mong muốn của độc giả cũ — người nói gạt cả hai và chốt nên nghe giới phê bình.

questions.prompt: What does the announcer say the writer should do in the future?
options: The writer should continue to write this genre
The writer should go back to his original genre
He should listen to critics before writing his next work

questions.prompt: What does the expert say being professional is all about?
options: To create a good working environment.
questions.explanation:
Good morning, everyone. Today I want to talk about professionalism and how it has changed over the years. If you ask people what being professional is really about, you will hear different answers. Some will tell you it is about creating a good working environment. Others will say it is about making a good impression on clients and colleagues. Those things matter, of course, but I see them as results, not as the starting point. In my view, being professional is, above all, about maintaining a positive attitude. When you stay friendly, open-minded and willing to help, even on difficult days, the good impression and the pleasant working environment follow naturally. A positive attitude is the engine; everything else is what the engine produces.
Now let me turn to how the idea of professionalism has developed. Forty years ago, being professional often meant little more than wearing a smart suit and following strict rules. Some people still believe the meaning has stayed the same all this time, but that is clearly not true. Technology and global business have changed what employers expect. Today, a professional also needs to be flexible, to understand people from different cultures, and to use new tools with confidence. And I want to be clear about one more thing: this process is not finished. Anyone who thinks the definition is now fixed and will not change any more is going to be surprised. Our definition of professionalism is still changing, and the professionals who succeed will be the ones who keep changing with it. Thank you.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
1. Đáp án: To maintain a positive attitude — thái độ tích cực là "engine", còn môi trường làm việc tốt và ấn tượng tốt chỉ là KẾT QUẢ (cả hai đều được nhắc làm bẫy).
2. Đáp án: Our definition of it is changing. Bẫy: "same as 40 years ago" bị phủ định trực tiếp; "will not change anymore" bị phủ định bằng câu "this process is not finished".

questions.prompt: What does the expert say about the definition of professionalism?
options: It is the same as 40 years ago.
Our definition of it is changing.

questions.prompt: Listen to a woman asking about a flight. How much does the flight in the morning cost?
questions.explanation:
Good morning, I'm calling about flights to Edinburgh next Tuesday. Yes, I saw three prices online and got confused. The evening flight is four hundred pounds, which is too much for me. There was also one at three hundred, but I understand that one is fully booked now? Right. So the morning flight it is — three hundred and fifty pounds, you said? Perfect, let's book that one. The morning flight at three fifty.

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án B – 350 pounds.
• Vì sao đúng: "So the morning flight it is — three hundred and fifty pounds, you said? Perfect, let's book that one" — chuyến sáng đúng 350 và đã đặt.
• 300 pounds sai: chuyến đó đã hết chỗ ("There was also one at three hundred, but I understand that one is fully booked now?").
• 400 pounds sai: đó là chuyến TỐI và quá đắt với người nói ("The evening flight is four hundred pounds, which is too much for me").
👉 Mẹo: khi câu hỏi giới hạn rõ đối tượng ("the flight in the morning"), phải ghép giá với đúng chuyến/buổi được hỏi, đừng chộp con số nghe rõ nhất.

questions.prompt: Listen to a friend talking about selling her music player. How much did she sell it for?
questions.explanation:
Guess what — I finally sold my old music player! You remember I first asked sixty dollars for it online? Nobody even wrote to me for two weeks. Then a student offered forty, which honestly felt too little for such a good machine. We met halfway in the end: he paid fifty dollars and walked away happy, and so did I. Now I can put that money towards the new headphones I've been wanting.

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án A – 50 dollars.
• Vì sao đúng: "We met halfway in the end: he paid fifty dollars and walked away happy".
• 60 dollars sai: là giá RAO ban đầu, không ai hỏi mua ("I first asked sixty dollars for it online? Nobody even wrote to me for two weeks").
• 40 dollars sai: là giá người mua trả, bị chê quá thấp ("a student offered forty, which honestly felt too little").
👉 Mẹo: bài mặc cả có công thức 3 bước: giá rao (asked) – giá trả (offered) – giá chốt (met halfway / in the end). Luôn lấy con số ở bước thứ ba.

questions.prompt: Listen to a woman explaining why he was late. What is the main reason he gets late?
questions.explanation:
Poor Daniel had a terrible morning. People at the office joked that he must have overslept again, but no — his alarm worked fine and he was up at six. He even remembered everything: keys, laptop, the presentation folder, all packed the night before. The real problem was at the station. He arrived just as the doors closed, and the next train wasn't for another forty minutes. That's why he walked in an hour late, poor thing.

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án C – Missed the train.
• Vì sao đúng: "The real problem was at the station. He arrived just as the doors closed, and the next train wasn't for another forty minutes".
• Overslept sai: đó là lời trêu ở công ty và đã bị bác bỏ ("People at the office joked that he must have overslept again, but no — his alarm worked fine").
• Forgot something sai: anh nhớ đủ mọi thứ, còn soạn từ tối hôm trước ("He even remembered everything: keys, laptop, the presentation folder, all packed the night before").
👉 Mẹo: câu hỏi "the main reason" luôn dựng sẵn 2 lý do giả rồi phủ định bằng "but no". Đáp án nằm sau "The real problem was..." hoặc "That's why...".

questions.prompt: A mom is calling her son to remind him about picking up groceries. How much is an egg?
questions.explanation:
Hi love, it's mum. Can you stop at the market stall on your way home? I need those big organic eggs for the cake — the special ones the baker uses. Yes, they're pricey: one pound fifty for a single egg, can you believe it. The lady next to her sells them at two fifty and the shop wants three fifty each, so hers are actually the cheapest. Take six eggs, that's nine pounds exactly. Thanks, sweetheart!

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án A – £1.50 (One pound fifty).
• Vì sao đúng: "one pound fifty for a single egg" — đây là giá tại sạp mẹ nhờ con mua, và "hers are actually the cheapest"; kiểm chứng bằng phép tính "Take six eggs, that's nine pounds exactly" (6 × 1.50 = 9).
• £2.50 sai: là giá của người bán ngay bên cạnh ("The lady next to her sells them at two fifty").
• £3.50 sai: là giá trong cửa hàng ("the shop wants three fifty each").
👉 Mẹo: đề hỏi giá một đơn vị hay kèm phép tính kiểm chứng. Nếu nghe được tổng tiền, nhân chia nhanh để xác nhận con số mình chọn.

questions.prompt: Julie is asking her professor about the assignment. When is the work due?
questions.explanation:
Professor, quick question about the essay before you go — when exactly do you need it? I heard some people say Thursday morning and I panicked a little. No? Oh, thank goodness. And it's not Friday either? I see — so we hand everything in on Saturday morning, before ten o'clock, in your office or by email. Saturday morning, got it. That gives me two more evenings than I thought. Thank you so much, Professor!

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án C – On Saturday morning.
• Vì sao đúng: "so we hand everything in on Saturday morning, before ten o'clock" và cô nhắc lại "Saturday morning, got it".
• On Thursday morning sai: chỉ là tin đồn cô nghe được, đã bị thầy phủ nhận ("I heard some people say Thursday morning and I panicked a little. No? Oh, thank goodness").
• On Friday morning sai: cũng bị loại ngay sau đó ("And it's not Friday either?").
👉 Mẹo: bài chỉ nghe một phía hội thoại — các câu hỏi lại kiểu "No? / It's not... either?" chính là dấu hiệu phương án vừa bị loại. Đáp án nằm ở câu "so..." tiếp theo.

questions.prompt: A tour guide is introducing a tourist destination. How many people live in the town?
questions.explanation:
Welcome to Millbrook, everyone! Before we walk into the old town, a few facts. People often guess this is a tiny village, but exactly ten thousand people live here today. The number was smaller a generation ago, and the mayor expects it to keep growing thanks to the new railway link. Most residents work in the pottery workshops you'll see on our left. Now, follow me across the square — and mind the cobblestones!

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án C – 10,000.
• Vì sao đúng: "exactly ten thousand people live here today".
• 8,000 sai: không được nhắc tới trong bài, chỉ là phương án gây nhiễu.
• 9,000 sai: cũng không được nhắc tới; bài chỉ nói dân số trước đây ít hơn ("The number was smaller a generation ago") mà không đưa con số.
👉 Mẹo: với số liệu dân số, bám từ khóa xác nhận "exactly", "today". Các câu kiểu "smaller before / expected to keep growing" chỉ là thông tin nền, không phải đáp án.

questions.prompt: A man is talking about his routine after work. What is the man going to do after work?
questions.explanation:
My colleagues think I rush home after work, but my routine is different. The moment I leave the office, I change into my sports clothes and go running along the river — five kilometres, every single day, rain or shine. It clears my head completely after all those meetings. Only after the run do I cycle slowly home, shower, and cook dinner. My doctor says it's the best habit I've ever built, and I agree.

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án A – Goes running.
• Vì sao đúng: "The moment I leave the office, I change into my sports clothes and go running along the river — five kilometres, every single day".
• Cycles home sai: việc này có thật nhưng xảy ra SAU khi chạy xong ("Only after the run do I cycle slowly home, shower, and cook dinner").
• Meets his client sai: không được nhắc tới trong bài; anh chỉ nói tới các cuộc họp đã qua ("after all those meetings").
👉 Mẹo: câu hỏi trình tự ("after work") — bám mốc thời gian "the moment I...", "only after..." để xếp thứ tự. Đừng chọn một việc chỉ vì nó có xuất hiện trong bài.

questions.prompt: Two friends are talking about their favorite activities. What is the woman's favorite form of entertainment?
questions.explanation:
You know me — my brother reads his thick novels every evening, and my cousin keeps inviting me to play chess with her, which I politely survive about once a month. But my heart belongs somewhere else entirely: the theatre. I go almost every Saturday — plays, musicals, even the small student performances above the pub. There is nothing like the moment the lights go down and the curtain rises. I've kept every ticket since I was twenty.

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án B – Going to the theatre.
• Vì sao đúng: "my heart belongs somewhere else entirely: the theatre. I go almost every Saturday".
• Reading books sai: đó là sở thích của ANH TRAI cô ("my brother reads his thick novels every evening").
• Playing chess with her cousin sai: cô chỉ miễn cưỡng chiều em họ mỗi tháng một lần ("my cousin keeps inviting me to play chess with her, which I politely survive about once a month").
👉 Mẹo: câu hỏi "favorite" — tìm cụm bộc lộ cảm xúc mạnh như "my heart belongs to", "there is nothing like". Sở thích gắn với người khác (my brother, my cousin) luôn là bẫy.

questions.prompt: An expert is talking about the lack of satisfaction at work. What should be the solution?
questions.explanation:
Many employees write to me saying the joy has gone out of their work. Let me clear away two popular wrong answers first. A raise? Money soothes for a month or two, then the same emptiness returns. Quitting for a completely new job sounds brave, but you throw away your reputation and often import the same boredom into a new office. The solution my research supports: request a transfer. Same company, new department — fresh faces and fresh problems, while your history and security stay with you.

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án C – Request a transfer.
• Vì sao đúng: "The solution my research supports: request a transfer. Same company, new department — fresh faces and fresh problems".
• Raise the salary sai: chuyên gia nói tiền chỉ xoa dịu tạm thời ("Money soothes for a month or two, then the same emptiness returns").
• Seek a new job sai: bị loại vì mất uy tín đã tích lũy và thường mang theo chính sự chán nản ("you throw away your reputation and often import the same boredom into a new office").
👉 Mẹo: bài chuyên gia tư vấn luôn "clear away the wrong answers first". Đáp án nằm sau từ hiệu lệnh "The solution is / What actually works is"; mọi ý trước đó đều là phương án bị bác.

questions.prompt: A man is calling his wife. Where will they meet?
questions.explanation:
Man: Hi darling, I've finished at the bank early. Where shall we meet?
Woman: Oh good! I'm still at the market. Shall I just see you at home?
Man: I'd rather not sit around waiting — I'm already in town. What about the garden café near the fountain?
Woman: It's closed on Mondays, remember? We found that out last week.
Man: Ah, you're right. Then let's keep it simple: I'll wait for you outside the shop — the big bookshop on the corner, our usual spot.
Woman: Outside the shop it is. Give me fifteen minutes. If I'm late, start browsing without me!
Man: I always do. See you soon.

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án C – Outside the shop.
• Vì sao đúng: "I'll wait for you outside the shop — the big bookshop on the corner, our usual spot" và cô đồng ý "Outside the shop it is".
• At home sai: người chồng không muốn ngồi chờ vì đã ở trong phố rồi ("I'd rather not sit around waiting — I'm already in town").
• In the garden sai: quán cà phê sân vườn đóng cửa thứ Hai ("It's closed on Mondays, remember?").
👉 Mẹo: nghe cấu trúc đảo ngữ xác nhận "... it is" (Outside the shop it is) — đây là dấu hiệu chốt phương án rất hay gặp trong hội thoại Part 1.

questions.prompt: A man is calling his friend, Maria. When will he see her?
questions.explanation:
Man: Maria! It's been months! When can I finally see you?
Woman: I know, I know. This weekend? Saturday I'm free after ten in the morning.
Man: Saturday's no good for me — I work until evening. What about Sunday?
Woman: Sunday works. But not too late, I have dinner with my parents.
Man: Early then. Eight in the morning? There's that breakfast place by the lake.
Woman: Eight is brutal, let's say nine. Nine on Sunday, the lake café.
Man: Nine on Sunday it is. I'll book the table by the window. So good to hear your voice!

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án A – at 9 am on Sunday.
• Vì sao đúng: "Nine on Sunday, the lake café" và anh xác nhận "Nine on Sunday it is".
• at 10 am on Saturday sai: thứ Bảy anh phải làm tới tối ("Saturday's no good for me — I work until evening").
• at 8 am on Sunday sai: cô chê quá sớm và đẩy lùi một tiếng ("Eight is brutal, let's say nine").
👉 Mẹo: đáp án dạng "ngày + giờ" phải khớp CẢ HAI yếu tố. Chốt được ngày rồi vẫn phải nghe tiếp, vì giờ thường bị dời thêm một lần ở lượt thoại cuối.

questions.prompt: A man is calling his colleague about a meeting with clients. When will the meeting start?
questions.explanation:
Man: Hi Anna, about tomorrow's meeting with the clients — is everything confirmed?
Woman: Almost. They first suggested nine fifteen, but their flight only lands at nine.
Man: That's tight. So we pushed it back?
Woman: Yes. I offered eleven fifteen, but Mr. Chen has a lunch appointment, so that was too late for him.
Man: So where did we land?
Woman: Ten fifteen. It gives them time from the airport, and we finish well before lunch. Meeting room two, projector's already booked.
Man: Ten fifteen, room two. I'll bring the printed contracts. Thanks, Anna — you think of everything.

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án B – at 10.15.
• Vì sao đúng: "Ten fifteen. It gives them time from the airport, and we finish well before lunch" — người kia nhắc lại "Ten fifteen, room two".
• at 9.15 sai: là giờ khách đề xuất ban đầu, nhưng máy bay 9h mới hạ cánh nên quá gấp ("They first suggested nine fifteen, but their flight only lands at nine").
• at 11.15 sai: quá muộn vì ông Chen có hẹn ăn trưa ("I offered eleven fifteen, but Mr. Chen has a lunch appointment").
👉 Mẹo: khi ba mốc giờ chỉ lệch nhau đúng một tiếng (9.15/10.15/11.15), đừng cố nghe con số — nghe LÝ DO loại trừ đi kèm mỗi mốc thì chắc hơn nhiều.

questions.prompt: A customer is calling the hotline of a department store. Which number to press in order to buy a computer?
questions.explanation:
Woman: Thank you for calling Harrison's Department Store. How can I direct your call?
Man: Hello, yes — I want to order a computer I saw in your catalogue.
Woman: Of course, sir. Our automated line handles that. When you call back, listen carefully: press one for clothing and shoes.
Man: Not that, then.
Woman: Press two for furniture and home goods. And for electronics — computers, phones, televisions — you press three.
Man: So for the computer, three?
Woman: Exactly, press three, and the electronics team will take your order. They're open until eight tonight.
Man: Wonderful. Three it is. Thank you very much!

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án C – Three.
• Vì sao đúng: "for electronics — computers, phones, televisions — you press three", nhân viên xác nhận "Exactly, press three, and the electronics team will take your order".
• One sai: phím dành cho quần áo và giày ("press one for clothing and shoes").
• Two sai: phím dành cho nội thất và đồ gia dụng ("Press two for furniture and home goods").
👉 Mẹo: dạng tổng đài liệt kê phím bấm — nghe theo cặp "số + nhóm hàng", rồi xác định món cần mua thuộc nhóm nào (computer thuộc electronics). Đừng cố nhớ mỗi con số rời.

questions.prompt: Four people are talking about doing exercise. Match each person to the correct information.
questions.explanation:
Speaker A: I started going to the gym for one reason only: my job. I sit in meetings all day, and by three o'clock my brain used to switch off completely. Since I began training at lunchtime, the afternoons feel like mornings. I close deals better, I write faster, and my manager has actually commented on it. Fitness for its own sake never tempted me — but as a tool for doing my work better, exercise has become the most useful hour of my day.
Speaker B: I keep at it because I know it is good for me, but I will be honest about how it feels: every session empties the tank completely. Twenty minutes in, my legs turn to stone and the clock stops moving. Afterwards I need the whole evening on the sofa just to become a person again. My sporty friends promise it gets easier with time. Three years in, I am still waiting for that famous lightness they talk about.
Speaker C: What keeps me coming back is the crowd. Tuesday badminton with my colleagues, Sunday football with the cousins — half the time we laugh more than we play. Alone on a treadmill I last ten minutes and give up, but put four friends around me and two hours vanish like nothing. The sport is really just the excuse; the jokes, the teasing and the noisy dinner afterwards are the real workout.
Speaker D: Let me say what everyone thinks and nobody admits: I cannot stand any of it. The sweating, the counting, the machines — all of it. My family drags me out for a game occasionally and I spend the whole time planning my escape. People promise I will learn to love it. I am fifty-two; I know what I love, and it is a good book in a comfortable chair.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
A = Improve work performance (PARAPHRASE: "I close deals better... the most useful hour" — hiệu quả công việc). B = Find exercise tiring (PARAPHRASE: "empties the tank... legs turn to stone" — không có chữ tiring). C = Have fun exercising with others (keyword "friends... laugh more than we play"). D = Hate exercising (keyword "I cannot stand any of it"). Nhiễu: alone, lose weight.

questions.prompt: Young people are more into politics
questions.explanation:
M: Did you catch that debate programme last night? What struck me was the audience. Half of them looked about twenty years old.
W: Funny you should say that, I noticed exactly the same thing while I was watching.
M: It's a real shift, isn't it. Young people genuinely care about this stuff now, far more than my generation ever did at that age.
W: I completely agree with you there. My niece is nineteen and she can argue about housing policy better than I can.
M: And I'd put a lot of that down to social media. I think it has completely rewritten the way politics actually works these days.
W: Hmm, I'm not so sure about that. I mean, the campaigning has moved online, fine, I'll give you that much. But the real deals are still done in back rooms by the same old people. Nothing fundamental has changed.
M: Well, I'd argue the platforms now decide what we even talk about in the first place, and that's a change in itself.
W: Maybe so. What I would say, though, is that ordinary voters understand the issues far better now than they used to, because everything is out in the open.
M: Oh, I don't see it that way at all, to be honest. People have more headlines in front of them, certainly, but that isn't the same thing as understanding. If anything, I'd say most voters are more confused than they've ever been.
W: That seems a bit harsh on people, doesn't it?
M: Perhaps it is, yes. Anyway, one thing I'm genuinely pleased about is how many more women are standing for office these days.
W: Yes, I agree with you on that one. The last council election here had more women candidates than men, which nobody expected.
M: Long overdue, if you ask me.
W: Couldn't agree more, honestly.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
Key: Giới trẻ quan tâm chính trị hơn = Both · Mạng xã hội thay đổi chính trị = Man · Người dân giờ hiểu biết hơn về chính trị = Woman · Nhiều phụ nữ theo đuổi chính trị hơn = Both

1. Young people are more into politics → Both: người đàn ông nêu "Young people genuinely care about this stuff now, far more than my generation ever did at that age." Người phụ nữ tán thành: "I completely agree with you there. My niece is nineteen and she can argue about housing policy better than I can."

2. Social media changes politics. → Man: người đàn ông nêu "I think it has completely rewritten the way politics actually works these days." Người phụ nữ phản đối: "Hmm, I'm not so sure about that... the real deals are still done in back rooms by the same old people. Nothing fundamental has changed."

3. People are now better informed about politics. → Woman: người phụ nữ nêu "ordinary voters understand the issues far better now than they used to, because everything is out in the open." Người đàn ông phản đối: "Oh, I don't see it that way at all... that isn't the same thing as understanding."

4. More women pursue politics. → Both: người đàn ông nêu "how many more women are standing for office these days", người phụ nữ đồng ý: "Yes, I agree with you on that one."

👉 Mẹo: Bẫy ở ý 2 — người phụ nữ nói "the campaigning has moved online, fine, I'll give you that much" (nhượng bộ một phần) rồi phủ nhận kết luận, nên vẫn là Man chứ không phải Both.

questions.prompt: Social media changes politics.
People are now better informed about politics.
More women pursue politics.
What does the writer believe helps her the most in her writing process?
options: Finding a quiet space to work
questions.explanation:
Hi everyone. People often ask me how I finished my new book, so today I want to share what I learned about the writing process — and about writer's block. When you read advice for writers, two suggestions come up again and again. The first is to write every single day, even if only for fifteen or twenty minutes. The second is to find a completely quiet space where nobody can disturb you. I tried both, honestly, and neither worked well for me. Writing for twenty minutes a day left me stopping just when the ideas started to flow, and the silent room made me sleepy rather than creative. What truly helps me the most is creating dedicated periods for writing — long, planned blocks of time that fit my own rhythm. I write best in the late morning, so I protect those three hours and let nothing interrupt them. Once I organised my week this way, my writing moved forward steadily.
But I also want to be honest about my biggest mistake. In the middle of the book, I got completely stuck for almost two months. I had a clear plan for the story, and I never ignored the feedback my editor sent me — those were not the problem. The problem was pride. I refused to ask other people for advice. I thought a real writer should solve everything alone, and that is the thing I regret most. When I finally called two writer friends, their questions unlocked the story in a single afternoon. So please, if you get stuck, do not wait as long as I did.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
1. Đáp án: Create dedicated periods for writing. Bẫy: "viết 15-20 phút mỗi ngày" và "tìm chỗ yên tĩnh" đều được nhắc rồi bị loại ("neither worked well for me").
2. Đáp án: Refuse to seek advice of others — điều cô ấy hối tiếc. Bẫy: "ignoring feedback from editors" bị phủ định ("never ignored"), "writing without a plan" bị phủ định ("had a clear plan").

questions.prompt: What does the writer regret doing during her experience with writer's block?
options: Refuse to seek advice of others

questions.prompt: What does she say about working at home?
options: Video calls are superior to face-to-face conversation
questions.explanation:
Working from home — everyone seems to have an opinion about it, and after a full year of doing it, I have mixed feelings too. Let me start with the good side. There are no colleagues chatting next to my desk, so on paper it sounds like a world without distractions. The truth is different: the office noise simply gets replaced by the dirty laundry, the unwashed dishes and the doorbell. I can set my own hours and take a break when I need one, which I do enjoy. And video calls are useful — but anyone who tells you they are better than sitting across a table from a real person has never tried to solve a difficult problem through a screen. Some days I feel quite lonely, and that surprised me. So if you ask me for an honest summary, I would say working from home is not as good as I expected. It has real advantages, but the picture people paint of it is too rosy.
Let me finish with some practical points. You do not need a big home office — a small corner of a room works perfectly fine. What you do need is self-motivation, because nobody is watching you, and the sofa is always calling. And the most important lesson of all: there is no single answer that fits everybody. How well working from home goes really depends on your situation and your personality. Some people do their best work this way; others need the energy of an office. Know which type you are before you decide.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
1. Đáp án: Not good as expected. Bẫy: "no distractions" bị phủ định (việc nhà thay tiếng ồn văn phòng), "video calls are superior" bị phủ định trực tiếp.
2. Đáp án: It depends on your situation and personality. Bẫy: "needs a big home office" bị phủ định ("small corner works fine"), "do not require self-motivation" bị phủ định ("what you do need is self-motivation").

questions.prompt: According to the author, working from home:
options: It depends on your situation and personality

questions.prompt: A woman is talking about her school days. What was the woman good at?
questions.explanation:
People always assume I was the sporty type at school, and they are half right. Swimming lessons were my weekly nightmare — I sank like a stone and the teacher gave up on me. Running was worse; I was always last in every race, red-faced and furious. But put a ball at my feet and everything changed. I played football for the school team five years straight, captain for the last two. The boys stopped laughing very quickly.

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án B – Plays football.
• Vì sao đúng: "I played football for the school team five years straight, captain for the last two" — thành tích cụ thể, rõ ràng.
• Swimming sai: cô bơi rất tệ, giáo viên bỏ cuộc ("Swimming lessons were my weekly nightmare — I sank like a stone and the teacher gave up on me").
• Running sai: còn tệ hơn, cô luôn về chót ("Running was worse; I was always last in every race").
👉 Mẹo: câu hỏi "good at" — bắt các từ đánh giá: nightmare, worse, always last = kém; team, captain, top scorer = giỏi. Không cần hiểu hết câu vẫn chọn đúng.

questions.prompt: A saleswoman is describing a house to a customer. What is not original?
questions.explanation:
Let me walk you through this beautiful property. The architecture, as you can see, is completely untouched — every arch and beam exactly as the builder left it in 1910. The wooden floor under your feet is original too; we only polished it. The furniture, however, I must be honest about: the previous owners replaced every piece in the nineteen-eighties, so nothing you can sit on today belongs to the house's first era. Shall we see the garden?

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án B – Furniture.
• Vì sao đúng: câu hỏi hỏi thứ KHÔNG nguyên bản — "The furniture, however, I must be honest about: the previous owners replaced every piece in the nineteen-eighties".
• Floor sai: sàn gỗ là nguyên bản, chỉ được đánh bóng lại ("The wooden floor under your feet is original too; we only polished it").
• Architecture sai: kiến trúc còn nguyên vẹn từ 1910 ("completely untouched — every arch and beam exactly as the builder left it in 1910").
👉 Mẹo: câu hỏi phủ định ("What is NOT original?") đảo ngược logic thường gặp. Gạch mọi thứ đi kèm original/untouched, chọn thứ đi kèm replaced/new/modern.

questions.prompt: Listen to an announcement. Which platform to wait for the train?
questions.explanation:
Attention please, this is a platform announcement. The twelve fifteen service to Manchester will depart from platform two. Please note this is a change from the printed timetable. Passengers for Manchester, make your way to platform two, where the train is now boarding. First class is at the front of the train. Once again: the twelve fifteen to Manchester, now boarding at platform two. Thank you.

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án A – Platform 2.
• Vì sao đúng: "The twelve fifteen service to Manchester will depart from platform two", nhắc lại ở cuối "the twelve fifteen to Manchester, now boarding at platform two".
• Platform 5 sai: không được nhắc tới trong bài, chỉ là phương án gây nhiễu.
• Platform 8 sai: cũng không được nhắc tới trong bài.
👉 Mẹo: thông báo nhà ga luôn lặp lại thông tin quan trọng ở câu cuối ("Once again..."). Lỡ câu đầu thì đừng hoảng, chờ câu nhắc lại là đủ.

questions.prompt: An artist is talking about her job. What is the difference in her job?
questions.explanation:
People imagine an artist's life is all freedom, but let me tell you what my schedule really looks like. My office friends work nine to five and switch off; I have never once had a day shaped like that. And weekends off? When an exhibition is coming, Saturday and Sunday disappear completely. Some weeks I paint through the night and sleep till noon; other weeks I barely touch a brush. My hours follow the work, not the clock — that is the real difference in this job.

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án C – She works irregular hours.
• Vì sao đúng: "My hours follow the work, not the clock — that is the real difference in this job".
• She works from 9 to 5 sai: đó là giờ giấc của bạn bè làm văn phòng, cô chưa từng như vậy ("My office friends work nine to five and switch off; I have never once had a day shaped like that").
• She doesn't work on weekends sai: ngược lại, khi sắp có triển lãm cô làm cả cuối tuần ("When an exhibition is coming, Saturday and Sunday disappear completely").
👉 Mẹo: câu hỏi "what is the difference" — đáp án thường là câu tổng kết ở CUỐI bài, mở đầu bằng "that is the real difference / that's what makes it different".

questions.prompt: Anne is calling her daughter Sally. What does Anne need?
questions.explanation:
Sally, love, it's mum. Are you still at the supermarket? Perfect timing. I'm in the middle of baking and I've just realised I'm completely out of eggs — the recipe needs four and the box in the fridge is empty. Don't worry about bread, your father bought two loaves this morning, and we still have plenty of milk. Just the eggs, a dozen if they have the free-range ones. You're a lifesaver, darling. See you soon!

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án A – Eggs.
• Vì sao đúng: "I'm completely out of eggs — the recipe needs four and the box in the fridge is empty... Just the eggs, a dozen".
• Bread sai: bố đã mua sáng nay ("your father bought two loaves this morning").
• Milk sai: trong nhà vẫn còn nhiều ("we still have plenty of milk").
👉 Mẹo: dạng nhờ mua đồ, hai món nhiễu luôn đi kèm cụm "đã có": already bought, we still have, plenty of. Món cần mua đi kèm "out of / we need / just the...".

questions.prompt: A mom is talking to her son. What does he like to study?
questions.explanation:
Sweetheart, your report card came today and I want to talk about it, calmly, I promise. Your marks are fine, but your teacher wrote something interesting: she says the only lessons where you truly come alive are the art classes. The drawing, the painting, the projects — apparently you stay after class to finish them. Is that true? Because if art is what you love studying, then art is what we will support. Maybe those Saturday classes at the gallery?

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án A – Art.
• Vì sao đúng: "the only lessons where you truly come alive are the art classes. The drawing, the painting, the projects — apparently you stay after class to finish them".
• Science sai: không được nhắc tới trong bài, chỉ là phương án gây nhiễu.
• History sai: cũng không được nhắc tới trong bài.
👉 Mẹo: khi chỉ một môn học được nêu tên, câu hỏi thực chất kiểm tra bạn có bắt được từ đó không. Chú ý các từ mở rộng cùng chủ đề (drawing, painting, gallery = art) để chắc chắn.

questions.prompt: A tour guide is making an announcement. Why was the tour canceled
questions.explanation:
Good morning, everyone, and I'm afraid I have disappointing news about today's castle tour. I know you're all ready to go — the sun is finally out after yesterday's rain, and our bus is parked outside with a full tank. Unfortunately, the tour requires a minimum of twelve participants, and this morning only five of you signed up. With so few people, the company cannot run the trip. Everyone will receive a full refund at reception, and I'm truly sorry.

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án A – Not enough people.
• Vì sao đúng: "the tour requires a minimum of twelve participants, and this morning only five of you signed up. With so few people, the company cannot run the trip".
• Bad weather sai: hôm nay trời đẹp, mưa là chuyện hôm qua ("the sun is finally out after yesterday's rain").
• Transportation problems sai: xe buýt vẫn sẵn sàng và đầy xăng ("our bus is parked outside with a full tank").
👉 Mẹo: câu hỏi "why cancelled" luôn nêu trước những thứ KHÔNG phải nguyên nhân để loại trừ. Đáp án đứng ngay sau "Unfortunately..." hoặc "The problem is...".

questions.prompt: A man is talking about his job. What does the man want to do next?
questions.explanation:
My working life has been a strange journey. I trained as a chef and spent ten years in restaurant kitchens — good years, but my back finally said no. Then I retrained and taught history at the secondary school, which I enjoyed until the marking buried me. People keep asking which one I'll go back to. Neither, actually. All those kitchens and classrooms gave me stories, and I want to write them down properly — my next chapter is a book.

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án A – Become a writer.
• Vì sao đúng: "Neither, actually. All those kitchens and classrooms gave me stories, and I want to write them down properly — my next chapter is a book".
• Become a chef again sai: nghề cũ, đã bỏ vì lưng không chịu nổi ("I trained as a chef and spent ten years in restaurant kitchens... but my back finally said no").
• Start teaching history again sai: cũng là quá khứ, bỏ vì chấm bài quá nhiều ("I enjoyed until the marking buried me").
👉 Mẹo: câu hỏi "what next" — bắt thì tương lai (I want to / my next...). Mọi động từ chia quá khứ (trained, taught, spent ten years) đều là bẫy nghề cũ.

questions.prompt: A finance expert is giving advice to young people. What shouldn't they do?
questions.explanation:
A word to the young people in the room about money. Buying nice clothes now and then is perfectly fine — enjoy your salary, you earned it. And saving for emergencies is not just allowed, it is essential: three months of expenses in a separate account, always. But here is the habit that ruins independence: whenever the month runs long, calling home and asking for more money. Don't. Learn to live inside what you earn, and your confidence will grow with your savings.

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án B – Ask for more money.
• Vì sao đúng: câu hỏi hỏi điều KHÔNG nên làm — "here is the habit that ruins independence: whenever the month runs long, calling home and asking for more money. Don't".
• Spend too much on clothes sai: mua quần áo đẹp thỉnh thoảng được chuyên gia cho phép ("Buying nice clothes now and then is perfectly fine — enjoy your salary").
• Save for emergencies sai: đây là việc BẮT BUỘC phải làm ("saving for emergencies is not just allowed, it is essential").
👉 Mẹo: câu hỏi phủ định ("What shouldn't they do?") — tìm mệnh lệnh cấm "Don't", "never", "the habit that ruins...". Những gì đi kèm "fine", "essential" là điều NÊN làm.

questions.prompt: Pierre and Emma are talking together about the picnic on the weekend. What will they bring to the picnic?
questions.explanation:
Woman: Pierre! Are you coming to the picnic on Saturday?
Man: Of course, Emma. I'm trying to work out what we should bring. Marie already claimed the drinks — she's bringing lemonade and juice for everyone.
Woman: And I heard Tom's girlfriend is making her big salads, the ones with the walnuts.
Man: Right, so drinks and salads are taken. That leaves us the main food — sandwiches, the chicken, maybe those little pies from the bakery you like.
Woman: Perfect, we'll handle the food then. I'll cook the chicken Friday night, you get the bread and pies Saturday morning.
Man: Done. Food from us, and we take your car. Nine o'clock?
Woman: Nine o'clock. Don't oversleep, Pierre!

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án C – Food.
• Vì sao đúng: "That leaves us the main food — sandwiches, the chicken, maybe those little pies" và cô chốt "Perfect, we'll handle the food then".
• Drinks sai: Marie đã nhận phần này ("Marie already claimed the drinks — she's bringing lemonade and juice for everyone").
• Salads sai: bạn gái của Tom lo ("Tom's girlfriend is making her big salads, the ones with the walnuts").
👉 Mẹo: dạng phân công đồ mang đi — nghe cụm "already claimed / is making" gắn với TÊN NGƯỜI KHÁC để loại. Phần của người nói đứng sau "That leaves us...".

questions.prompt: A teacher and a student are talking about transportation. How does the teacher go to school?
questions.explanation:
Man: You look surprised to see me on foot, Minh!
Woman: Sorry, teacher! I always imagined you driving to school. Most teachers park in the yard.
Man: I used to drive, actually, years ago. Then the parking became impossible and petrol got so expensive.
Woman: So you take the bus now, like us students?
Man: I tried the bus for one term — twenty minutes of squeezing and pushing every morning. No, thank you. These days I simply walk. It's forty minutes each way, my doctor is delighted, and I arrive with a clear head.
Woman: Forty minutes! Every day?
Man: Every day, rain or shine. Best decision I've made. You should try it — you live closer than I do!

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án C – He walks.
• Vì sao đúng: "These days I simply walk. It's forty minutes each way, my doctor is delighted" — và ông xác nhận "Every day, rain or shine".
• He drives sai: đó là chuyện quá khứ, đã bỏ vì khó đỗ xe và xăng đắt ("I used to drive, actually, years ago").
• He takes the bus sai: chỉ thử một học kỳ rồi bỏ ("I tried the bus for one term — twenty minutes of squeezing and pushing every morning. No, thank you").
👉 Mẹo: câu hỏi phương tiện đi lại hiện tại — bám cụm chỉ thời gian "these days / now", loại mọi thứ đi kèm "used to / I tried... for one term".

questions.prompt: Tom is calling his friend. What time will they meet?
questions.explanation:
Man: Hey, it's Tom! Are we still on for tonight?
Woman: Definitely. What time were you thinking?
Man: Well, I finish work at five, so five o'clock is impossible for me — I'd still be at my desk.
Woman: And I have my yoga class until six, so six doesn't work for me either.
Man: Right. Then let's say seven? That gives you time to shower and me time to cross town.
Woman: Seven is perfect. The new noodle place on Green Street?
Man: Exactly the one. I'll book a table for seven o'clock. See you there!

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án C – 7 PM.
• Vì sao đúng: "Then let's say seven?" – "Seven is perfect" – "I'll book a table for seven o'clock".
• 5 PM sai: giờ đó anh vẫn còn ở bàn làm việc ("I finish work at five, so five o'clock is impossible for me").
• 6 PM sai: cô có lớp yoga đến 6h ("I have my yoga class until six, so six doesn't work for me either").
👉 Mẹo: trong hội thoại hẹn giờ, mỗi mốc bị loại đều kèm lý do cá nhân ("impossible for me", "doesn't work for me either"). Giờ đúng là giờ được cả hai đồng ý và có hành động đặt bàn kèm theo.

questions.prompt: A woman is talking to a police officer. What did she lose?
questions.explanation:
Man: Good afternoon, madam. You said you've lost something?
Woman: Yes, officer, somewhere on the high street this morning. I was terrified it was my wallet at first, but no — the wallet is right here, thank goodness, cards and all.
Man: That's a relief. So what exactly is missing?
Woman: My phone. The new one, barely a month old. I had it at the bakery — I paid with it — and by the car park it was gone from my pocket.
Man: You didn't leave it in the car?
Woman: I checked the car twice, it's not there. It must have fallen out or... been taken.
Man: All right, let's file a report. Phone, black, one month old. We'll check the bakery's cameras first.

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án B – Phone.
• Vì sao đúng: "My phone. The new one, barely a month old" — và cảnh sát ghi biên bản "Phone, black, one month old".
• Wallet sai: ban đầu cô tưởng mất ví, nhưng ví vẫn còn nguyên ("I was terrified it was my wallet at first, but no — the wallet is right here, cards and all").
• Car sai: xe không mất; cô chỉ kiểm tra trong xe xem có bỏ quên điện thoại không ("I checked the car twice, it's not there").
👉 Mẹo: dạng khai báo mất đồ — món bị mất luôn được xác nhận lại ở cuối khi lập biên bản. Món xuất hiện kèm "but no / it's right here" là bẫy.

questions.prompt: Four people are talking about protecting the environment. Match each person to the correct information.
questions.explanation:
Speaker A: In our house the war is against the meter on the wall. Lights off the second a room empties, the washing machine only runs full, and we swapped every bulb for the efficient kind. My son even unplugs the chargers at night because, he says, they drink secretly in the dark. Our bills have almost halved, and I like to think the power station burns a little less because of our small savings.
Speaker B: I made one big decision last spring: the car stays in the garage on weekdays. I take the number forty-two to the office instead, rain or shine. It adds fifteen minutes each way, and I read on the top deck, so honestly I have gained time rather than lost it. One less engine crawling through the morning jam — that is my contribution, and my head arrives at work calmer too.
Speaker C: Mine will sound lazy, but hear me out: I do almost all my buying from the sofa. One delivery van serving my whole street replaces forty separate trips to the shopping centre — forty engines, forty parking circles. I group my orders so everything comes in one box, once a week. My neighbour teases me about it, but I think my armchair habit is greener than her Saturday drive to the mall.
Speaker D: My obsession is the tap. Short showers with a timer, a bowl in the sink for washing vegetables, and that bowl then feeds the garden. I fixed the dripping bathroom tap the day I read how many litres it wastes in a year — the number shocked me. My children think I am strict about it, and I am. Clean water is the thing we will miss first, so every drop I keep matters.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
A = using less electricity (PARAPHRASE: "war against the meter... lights off... bills halved"). B = not driving to work (PARAPHRASE: "the car stays in the garage on weekdays... number forty-two to the office"). C = shopping online (keyword "buying from the sofa... orders... one box"). D = using less water (keyword "tap... short showers... every drop"). Nhiễu: cycling, recycling bottles.

questions.prompt: The internet makes education more accessible
questions.explanation:
W: You went to that open day at the university last weekend, didn't you? What did you make of it?
M: Impressive, on the whole. Though the place has changed enormously since our day.
W: It has. The thing that strikes me most is that the web has thrown the doors wide open — somebody in a tiny village can now follow lectures from a world-class institution without moving an inch.
M: Exactly, I'm completely with you on that. My cousin is doing a degree from her kitchen table in the middle of nowhere, and paying a fraction of what we did.
W: Quite. It's the best thing that's happened to education in decades.
M: Mind you, there's something you simply can't get down a wire. Mixing with other people — the arguments in the corridor, the societies, the late nights — that's the very heart of university life, and it doesn't survive a screen.
W: Hmm, I'm not convinced by that, I must say. I'll accept that the friendships are pleasant enough, but essential? Plenty of people have got their degrees quietly on their own and done perfectly well out of it.
M: You'd have thought differently if you'd lived in halls.
W: Possibly. What does bother me, though, is the menu of subjects these days. Offering students four hundred different modules isn't the blessing everyone claims — a good many of them walk out with a scattered qualification that means very little to an employer.
M: I don't see it that way at all. Choice is precisely what lets somebody stumble on the thing they turn out to be good at. Narrow it down and you just churn out identical graduates.
W: We'll have to differ on that one, clearly.
M: Fair enough. But here's something I do feel strongly about — universities ought to be pushed to compete with one another. A bit of rivalry drives standards up.
W: I'm not so sure about that, to be honest. All it really does is send them chasing league tables instead of actually teaching anybody anything.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
Key: Internet giúp việc học dễ tiếp cận hơn = Both · Giao tiếp xã hội thiết yếu với đời sống đại học = Man · Chương trình quá đa dạng không hẳn là tốt = Woman · Nên khuyến khích cạnh tranh giữa các trường = Man

1. The internet makes education more accessible → Both: người phụ nữ nêu "the web has thrown the doors wide open", người đàn ông tán thành rõ ràng: "Exactly, I'm completely with you on that."

2. Social interactions are essential to university life → Man: người đàn ông nêu "that's the very heart of university life, and it doesn't survive a screen". Người phụ nữ phản đối: "Hmm, I'm not convinced by that, I must say."

3. A diverse curriculum is not always a good thing → Woman: người phụ nữ nêu "Offering students four hundred different modules isn't the blessing everyone claims". Người đàn ông phản đối: "I don't see it that way at all."

4. Competitions between universities should be encouraged → Man: người đàn ông nêu "universities ought to be pushed to compete with one another". Người phụ nữ phản đối: "I'm not so sure about that, to be honest."

👉 Mẹo: Bẫy nằm ở ý 2 — người phụ nữ nói "I'll accept that the friendships are pleasant enough" nghe như đồng ý, nhưng câu hỏi ngược "but essential?" mới là quan điểm thật của cô ấy, nên đáp án là Man chứ không phải Both.

questions.prompt: Social interactions are essential to university life
A diverse curriculum is not always a good thing
Competitions between universities should be encouraged
What is the most important thing to help you sleep well?
options: Blocking noise and light is the key
questions.explanation:
Good afternoon. Today I want to clear up some common ideas about sleep, because there is a lot of confusing advice out there. Ask ten people how to sleep better and you will get ten different answers. Some will tell you that the bed itself matters most — that if you buy the right mattress, good sleep will follow automatically. Others simply say that resting enough is necessary, which is true, but it does not tell you how to actually get that rest. And a few people even believe strange tricks, like sleeping fewer hours to make the deep sleep stronger. As a sleep researcher, I can tell you what the evidence really shows: the key to sleeping well is blocking out noise and light. A quiet, dark room sends a clear signal to the brain that it is time to switch off. Compared with that, the brand of your mattress makes only a small difference.
Now let me say something about insomnia, because it is widely misunderstood. Many people assume it is caused only by physical health problems, but that is not correct — stress, worry and daily habits play just as big a role. Others imagine that people with insomnia secretly sleep too much during the day. Also wrong. The really interesting finding is this: people cannot always recognise the symptoms of their own tiredness. They feel restless, so they keep working or scrolling on their phones late at night, without realising how exhausted they already are. Sadly, that reaction makes the problem worse, night after night.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
1. Đáp án: Blocking noise and light is the key. Bẫy: "beds are best for sleeping" bị hạ cấp ("makes only a small difference"), "resting sufficiently is necessary" được công nhận là đúng nhưng "does not tell you how" — không phải chìa khóa.
2. Đáp án: People can't always recognize the symptoms of tiredness. Bẫy: "caused only by physical health problems" bị phủ định, "sleep too much" bị phủ định ("Also wrong").

questions.prompt: What is the speaker's view on insomnia in general?
options: Insomnia is caused only by physical health problems
Most people with insomnia actually sleep too much
People can't always recognize the symptoms of tiredness

questions.prompt: What happened to the TV series?
options: It didn't receive enough investment in the early stage.
It caught the audience's attention from the start.
questions.explanation:
Have you been watching Mystery City? If not, you are one of the few. When the series began, some journalists claimed it had not received enough money in its early stage, and others expected the critics to overlook it completely. Both predictions turned out to be wrong. The network actually invested heavily from day one, and the reviews have been warm from the very first week. Most importantly, the show caught the audience's attention from the start. The opening episode was full of tension and surprises, and within days social media was full of theories about the characters. People connected with the story immediately, and that early excitement is exactly what every new series dreams of.
But I want to look at this as a business story, because that is where it gets really interesting. Fans are already asking for new seasons, though nothing has been confirmed yet. Some film teachers even say the series will inspire young filmmakers to copy its style. Maybe so — but in my opinion, the real potential lies somewhere else: this series can help the network reach new customers. Younger viewers who never watched traditional television have signed up just to follow this one show, and once they arrive, they discover everything else on the platform. A single strong series, supported by clever promotion, can grow a network's audience in a way that ordinary advertising never could. That is the lesson other companies will take from Mystery City, and I expect many will try to copy it next year.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
1. Đáp án: It caught the audience's attention from the start. Bẫy: "didn't receive enough investment" và "overlooked by critics" đều là dự đoán bị chứng minh SAI ("Both predictions turned out to be wrong").
2. Đáp án: It can help reach new customers. Bẫy: "new seasons" chỉ là mong muốn của fan ("nothing has been confirmed"), "inspires young filmmakers" là ý kiến của người khác — người nói chốt "the real potential lies somewhere else".

questions.prompt: According to the expert, what is the series' potential?
options: New seasons will be produced due to great demand.
It inspires young filmmakers to follow a new movie-making style.
It can help reach new customers.

questions.prompt: A student is talking about housing. Where does he live now?
questions.explanation:
People ask how I'm settling in since starting university, and my answer always gets a laugh. I grew up in a small village — two shops and a church — but that's long behind me now. When I arrived, I hunted for an apartment near campus, and the waiting lists were two years deep, completely hopeless. Then came the surprise: the council had converted the old town hall into student rooms! So now I live in a town hall — chandelier on the ceiling, balcony over the square. Best address I'll ever have!

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án C – In a town hall.
• Vì sao đúng: "the council had converted the old town hall into student rooms! So now I live in a town hall — chandelier on the ceiling, balcony over the square".
• In a small village sai: đó là nơi cậu LỚN LÊN, đã là quá khứ ("I grew up in a small village — two shops and a church — but that's long behind me now").
• In an apartment sai: cậu có tìm nhưng danh sách chờ dài hai năm, hoàn toàn vô vọng ("the waiting lists were two years deep, completely hopeless").
👉 Mẹo: câu hỏi "where does he live NOW" — loại nơi đi kèm "I grew up / that's behind me" và nơi chỉ là ý định thất bại ("I hunted for... hopeless").

questions.prompt: Listen to a student talking about his study. What course is the student going to take this year?
questions.explanation:
This year I had to choose just one extra course, and it wasn't easy. My father pushed for math — he says it opens every door — but honestly, numbers and I stopped being friends years ago. Science tempted me too, especially the laboratory work. In the end, though, I signed up for the computer course. Everything I want to do later needs programming, and the teacher is supposed to be brilliant. So three afternoons a week, it's me and the keyboard now.

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án B – Computer.
• Vì sao đúng: "In the end, though, I signed up for the computer course. Everything I want to do later needs programming".
• Math sai: đó là ý của BỐ, còn cậu thì không hợp với con số ("My father pushed for math... numbers and I stopped being friends years ago").
• Science sai: chỉ dừng ở mức hấp dẫn, cậu không đăng ký ("Science tempted me too, especially the laboratory work").
👉 Mẹo: động từ quyết định thật là "signed up for / I chose". Các động từ như "pushed for" (người khác muốn) hay "tempted me" (mới cân nhắc) đều là bẫy.

questions.prompt: A girl is talking about a show she will attend. What will end with?
questions.explanation:
I'm so excited about the show on Saturday! My cousin performed last year, so she told me how the evening runs. It opens with a dance performance by the youngest group — apparently adorable. Then there's a big celebration in the middle, with the awards and the singing and everyone on stage. But the part nobody talks about beforehand is the ending: the teachers prepare a surprise performance, different every year, kept completely secret until the final curtain. Last year they say people cried with laughter!

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án C – A surprise performance.
• Vì sao đúng: câu hỏi hỏi phần KẾT — "the part nobody talks about beforehand is the ending: the teachers prepare a surprise performance... kept completely secret until the final curtain".
• A dance performance sai: đó là tiết mục MỞ ĐẦU ("It opens with a dance performance by the youngest group").
• A big celebration sai: diễn ra ở GIỮA chương trình ("Then there's a big celebration in the middle, with the awards and the singing").
👉 Mẹo: câu hỏi về thứ tự chương trình — bám ba từ khóa vị trí: opens with (đầu), in the middle (giữa), the ending / final curtain (cuối). Câu hỏi hỏi phần nào thì lấy đúng từ khóa đó.

questions.prompt: Listen to an auction man talking about a cabinet. Which part of the cabinet is original?
questions.explanation:
Ladies and gentlemen, lot number twelve: this fine oak cabinet from around 1890. Now, let me be honest about its condition, as always. The doors were replaced in the nineteen-sixties — you can see the newer wood. The brass handles are also modern reproductions, fitted by the last owner. But the drawer — please, come closer — the drawer is completely original, dovetail joints and all, exactly as the craftsman made it. A beautiful piece of history. Shall we start at two hundred?

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án A – The drawer.
• Vì sao đúng: "the drawer is completely original, dovetail joints and all, exactly as the craftsman made it".
• The doors sai: đã bị thay trong thập niên 1960 ("The doors were replaced in the nineteen-sixties — you can see the newer wood").
• The handles sai: là đồ phục chế hiện đại do chủ trước lắp ("The brass handles are also modern reproductions, fitted by the last owner").
👉 Mẹo: bài đấu giá/nhà cổ luôn xoay quanh cặp từ original ↔ replaced/reproduction. Chỉ cần nghe được cặp này là khoanh đúng, không cần hiểu hết phần mô tả.

questions.prompt: Listen to a voice message. How does Even feel?
questions.explanation:
Hi, it's Even, leaving a message for the whole team. Sorry for the strange voice. I know everyone thinks I've been overworking and I'm just tired — honestly, I wish that were it. And no, despite the holiday photos I posted, this is not a happy call. The doctor confirmed it this morning: proper flu, high fever, the lot. I'm staying in bed the rest of the week, so please move my meetings. Don't visit — you don't want what I have!

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án A – Sick.
• Vì sao đúng: "The doctor confirmed it this morning: proper flu, high fever, the lot. I'm staying in bed the rest of the week".
• Happy sai: chính anh phủ nhận dù có đăng ảnh đi chơi ("despite the holiday photos I posted, this is not a happy call").
• Tired sai: đó là suy đoán của đồng nghiệp và anh bác bỏ ("everyone thinks I've been overworking and I'm just tired — honestly, I wish that were it").
👉 Mẹo: câu hỏi cảm xúc/tình trạng — người nói thường bác hai suy đoán bằng "I wish that were it", "this is not...". Đáp án là điều được nguồn xác thực (bác sĩ) khẳng định.

questions.prompt: Listen to a tour guide. Where is the office located?
questions.explanation:
Good morning, group! Before we set off, please memorise where our tour office is, in case anyone gets separated today. People often look for us next to the park — that's our old address, we moved last spring. And no, we're not above a restaurant anymore either, thank goodness; the kitchen smells were unbearable. The office now sits directly opposite the Grand Hotel — big blue sign, you cannot miss it. Opposite the hotel. If you get lost, go there and wait for us.

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án B – Opposite the hotel.
• Vì sao đúng: "The office now sits directly opposite the Grand Hotel — big blue sign, you cannot miss it. Opposite the hotel".
• Next to the park sai: đó là địa chỉ CŨ, đã chuyển từ mùa xuân ("that's our old address, we moved last spring").
• Above a restaurant sai: cũng là quá khứ, đã bỏ vì mùi bếp ("we're not above a restaurant anymore either; the kitchen smells were unbearable").
👉 Mẹo: câu hỏi địa điểm hiện tại — từ khóa vàng là "now". Mọi vị trí đi kèm "old address", "not... anymore" đều bị loại.

questions.prompt: Listen to the announcement. When does the train leave?
questions.explanation:
Good morning, passengers. This is an announcement regarding the express service to London. Due to engineering work completed earlier than planned, this train will now leave at nine fifteen, not nine thirty as printed in your timetable. I repeat: departure is at nine fifteen. Passengers should be on platform four at least five minutes early. The following service departs at nine forty-five for those who miss this one. Thank you.

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án A – At 9:15.
• Vì sao đúng: "this train will now leave at nine fifteen, not nine thirty as printed in your timetable. I repeat: departure is at nine fifteen".
• At 9.30 sai: là giờ in trên lịch trình cũ, đã được sửa ("not nine thirty as printed in your timetable").
• At 9.45 sai: là chuyến SAU, dành cho ai lỡ tàu này ("The following service departs at nine forty-five for those who miss this one").
