👉 Mẹo: dạng hẹn lịch, gạch ngay ngày đi kèm "I'm out", "all day", "whole day gone". Ngày còn lại được CẢ HAI xác nhận ("perfect", "done") mới là đáp án.

title: Đề 10 - Purposes of using the Internet

questions.prompt: Four people are talking about using the Internet. Match each person to the correct information.
questions.explanation:
Speaker A: My evenings have one ritual: lights off, snacks ready, and something good on the screen. The internet has turned my little bedroom into a cinema — old classics, new releases, series from Korea and Spain with subtitles. I have not bought a cinema ticket in two years, because why queue when the whole film library of the world sits behind my login? Saturday nights, my sister joins me and we argue for twenty minutes about what to watch.
Speaker B: Half the people I love live in other time zones now — university scattered us across three continents. So my internet hours are spent talking: video calls with my best friend in Toronto every Sunday, voice messages to the group that never sleeps, long chats with my old roommate about nothing. Without the connection, those friendships would have faded into birthday texts. With it, we still finish each other's sentences from opposite sides of the planet.
Speaker C: For me the internet is basically a homework machine. Every essay starts with the online library, every presentation leans on the journals my university subscribes to, and when the deadline panics arrive, the tutorial videos save my grade. Last term I wrote my entire dissertation without borrowing a single paper book. My classmates use it the same way — the night before submission, you can feel the whole class online, typing.
Speaker D: I check one thing before leaving the house, always: which bus is actually coming, and when. The app knows about the roadworks before the radio does, shows me where my bus is crawling on the map, and reroutes me when the trains misbehave. Since I started trusting it, I have stopped standing at stops in the rain guessing. My whole journey to work is planned by my phone before I finish my coffee.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
A = watch film (keyword "cinema... film library"). B = communicate with friends (PARAPHRASE: "spent talking... video calls... friendships"). C = complete school assignments (PARAPHRASE: "homework machine... essay... dissertation"). D = find transport information (keyword "which bus is coming... journey planned"). Nhiễu: online courses, games.

questions.prompt: Singers can be good role models for young people.
questions.explanation:
Woman: Did you watch the interview with that young singer last night? She spoke about finishing school, refusing certain advertisements, donating her first big pay cheque. My daughter watched it three times — though honestly, I have known too many idols with beautiful interviews and ugly private lives to hand them my children's compasses.
Man: I saw it, and I would be kinder than that. A performer like her can show teenagers a way to carry themselves better than any lecture from me. What fascinates me more is how differently we all hear things. You adore those quiet piano albums that send me straight to sleep, and my heavy guitar records give you a headache. Nobody is right; the ear wants what it wants.
Woman: True enough — my sister and I grew up in one bedroom and cannot agree on a single record. Each pair of ears is its own country. And yet — here is the strange part — when I travelled through countries whose languages I could not speak a word of, a melody in a market square could still make every stranger around me sway together. Words need translating; a tune walks straight in.
Man: Sometimes, perhaps. I have also sat politely through foreign songs that meant nothing to me, so I will not sign that declaration. But here is something we should both be uneasy about: the people who understand exactly how a rising chord squeezes the heart — advertisers, film studios, campaign managers — use it on us daily.
Woman: Constantly. Play the right strings and you can steer a crowd wherever you wish. That power deserves more suspicion than we give it.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
Key: M-B-W-B (nữ nói trước như đề thật). Paraphrase:
1. "Singers good role models" → M: "A performer like her can show teenagers a way to carry themselves" — W từ chối ("hand them my children's compasses").
2. "Taste highly personal" → B: M "the ear wants what it wants" + W "Each pair of ears is its own country".
3. "Music universal language" → W: "a tune walks straight in" — M "I will not sign that declaration".
4. "Music manipulates feelings" → B: M "use it on us daily" + W "steer a crowd wherever you wish".

questions.prompt: Taste in music is a highly personal thing.
Music is a universal language
Music can be used to manipulate people's feelings
Why does the brother find traveling meaningful?
options: Because it allows him to escape his professional responsibilities.
Because he wants to document his trips for social media influence.
Because it brings him joy and chances to learn about different cultures.
questions.explanation:
My brother has always loved travelling, though people often misunderstand why he does it. Some of his colleagues believe he is simply trying to escape the pressure of his job — running away from deadlines by booking another flight. Others are sure he travels to feed his social media accounts, collecting beautiful photos to make his followers jealous. I can tell you that both guesses are wrong. He posts almost nothing online, and he plans his trips during his calmest months at work, not his busiest. The truth is much simpler: travelling brings him real joy and endless chances to learn about different cultures. He comes home full of stories about a cooking lesson in a small village or a festival he happened to walk into. Those moments of connection with local people and their traditions are, for him, the whole point of going anywhere.
I often tell him that his travelling is remarkably similar to my reading. Now, I do not mean they are alike because both are mandatory for academic success — no school forces you to wander through Vietnam or to finish a novel by Friday. Nor do they match because both demand great physical endurance; my sofa asks very little of me. The real similarity is deeper: both help people discover new worlds and grow as a person. Every country he visits changes him a little, and every book I finish changes me. When we compare notes at family dinners, we are really describing the same journey — his through places, mine through pages.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
1. Đáp án: Because it brings him joy and chances to learn about different cultures. Bẫy: "escape responsibilities" và "social media" đều là suy đoán của người khác bị bác ("both guesses are wrong").
2. Đáp án: Both help people discover new worlds and grow as a person. Bẫy: "mandatory for academic success" và "physical endurance" đều bị phủ định hài hước.

questions.prompt: How is traveling similar to reading a book?
options: Both are considered mandatory activities for academic success.
Both help people discover new worlds and grow as a person.
Both require a high level of physical endurance and preparation.

questions.prompt: According to the speaker, how should we learn to work?
questions.explanation:
In today's fast-moving workplace, the old ways of training are no longer enough, so let me share two ideas that I believe matter most for your career. The first is about how we work. Some people think the goal is to work independently, without any guidance at all — to prove you never need help. Others go the opposite way and follow strictly fixed instructions for every task, never asking whether the instructions still make sense. Neither approach will carry you far. What we should really learn is how to work effectively. That means organising your day around the tasks that create the most value, instead of simply staying busy. An effective worker asks: which two hours of my day actually matter? Master that question and you will stand out in any company, because busy people are everywhere, but effective people are rare.
The second idea is about progress. Efficiency alone will keep you employed, but it will not move you forward. If you want real growth, you must be willing to experiment. Try a new method, test an unfamiliar tool, volunteer for the project nobody understands yet. I know many people prefer to maintain a predictable daily routine, because routines feel safe. And I know others believe the wise strategy is to avoid any risks in the workplace. But think honestly: have you ever met a successful person whose whole story was "I kept my routine and avoided every risk"? Progress belongs to the people who try things, fail politely, learn quickly, and try again.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
1. Đáp án: Effectively. Bẫy: "independently without any guidance" và "following strictly fixed instructions" đều được nhắc rồi bị loại ("Neither approach will carry you far").
2. Đáp án: Experiment. Bẫy: "maintain a predictable daily routine" và "avoid any risks" đều được nhắc rồi bị phản bác bằng câu hỏi tu từ.

questions.prompt: What should people be willing to do in order to make progress?
options: Avoid any risks in the workplace

questions.prompt: A receptionist is checking the client list of a clinic. How many American clients are there?
questions.explanation:
Let me run through Friday's bookings before I lock up. Morning block: Mr. Tanaka from Japan at nine, then Mrs. Almeida — she's Brazilian — at half past ten. After lunch we have the new patient, Mr. Harris from Chicago; he's our only American this week, I should flag his insurance forms. Then Miss Novak from Prague at three, and Doctor Rossi, Italian, closes the day at five. Five patients, one American. Forms printed tonight, coffee machine refilled — done!

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án B – One.
• Vì sao đúng: "the new patient, Mr. Harris from Chicago; he's our only American this week" — và câu tổng kết "Five patients, one American".
• Two sai: bốn bệnh nhân còn lại đều không phải người Mỹ — "Mr. Tanaka from Japan", "Mrs. Almeida — she's Brazilian", "Miss Novak from Prague", "Doctor Rossi, Italian".
• Three sai: tổng cộng chỉ có năm bệnh nhân và người Mỹ duy nhất là Mr. Harris — "Five patients, one American".
👉 Mẹo: dạng hỏi SỐ LƯỢNG theo tiêu chí (bao nhiêu người Mỹ), đừng chộp con số đầu tiên nghe được. Vừa nghe vừa đếm theo quốc tịch rồi đối chiếu câu tổng kết cuối bài.

questions.prompt: Listen to a girl calling the cafe. Where did she ask the coffee shop to look for her lost item?
questions.explanation:
Hello, Sunny Corner Café? Oh thank goodness. I was there this afternoon and my reading glasses are missing — blue frame, in a soft grey case. Could someone look for them? Not on the counter, please don't bother — I never went near it, my friend paid. And we came in through the garden, so nowhere near the door either. We sat in the corner, the snug little table by the fireplace — check down the side of that armchair! Yes, the corner. I'll wait on the line!

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án C – In the corner.
• Vì sao đúng: "We sat in the corner, the snug little table by the fireplace — check down the side of that armchair! Yes, the corner".
• On the counter sai: cô chủ động loại vì không hề lại gần quầy, bạn cô trả tiền — "Not on the counter, please don't bother — I never went near it, my friend paid".
• Near the door sai: họ đi vào bằng lối vườn — "we came in through the garden, so nowhere near the door either".
👉 Mẹo: dạng hỏi vị trí đồ thất lạc, bám câu nhờ tìm ("check...", "could someone look..."). Vị trí đi kèm "not", "don't bother", "nowhere near" là loại thẳng.

questions.prompt: The daughter is calling her father. What did she buy?
questions.explanation:
Dad! Dad, don't hang up, it's good news, mostly! I'm at the shopping centre with Linh, and you know that wedding next month? Well — I found it. Not the shoes, calm down, I'm borrowing Linh's silver ones, they fit perfectly. And I looked at blouses for work, but they were all overpriced polyester, honestly. What I bought — and dad, it was thirty percent off — is a dress. THE dress. Emerald green, knee-length, elegant like in the films. You'll approve, I promise! Tell mum!

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án A – A dress.
• Vì sao đúng: "What I bought — and dad, it was thirty percent off — is a dress. THE dress. Emerald green, knee-length".
• A pair of shoes sai: cô mượn giày của Linh chứ không mua — "Not the shoes, calm down, I'm borrowing Linh's silver ones, they fit perfectly".
• A blouse sai: chỉ ngắm rồi chê đắt — "I looked at blouses for work, but they were all overpriced polyester".
👉 Mẹo: dạng hỏi "mua gì", chỉ tính động từ "bought/I got". Món đi kèm "borrowing" hay "looked at... but" là món KHÔNG mua.

questions.prompt: What country will they study next semester?
questions.explanation:
Big news from the exchange office today, everyone! The placements for next semester are finally decided. I know half of you dreamed of Germany, but Munich took no one from our faculty this year — their quota filled instantly. And Spain, sadly, suspended the partnership until the paperwork clears. But the good news is golden: we're going to France! Lyon, to be exact — the full semester, language course included, September to January. Start practising your bonjour, people!

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án C – France.
• Vì sao đúng: "the good news is golden: we're going to France! Lyon, to be exact — the full semester, language course included, September to January".
• Germany sai: Munich không nhận ai từ khoa của họ vì chỉ tiêu đầy ngay — "Munich took no one from our faculty this year — their quota filled instantly".
• Spain sai: chương trình hợp tác bị tạm dừng chờ giấy tờ — "Spain, sadly, suspended the partnership until the paperwork clears".
👉 Mẹo: dạng thông báo địa điểm, nghe cụm đảo hướng "But the good news is". Nước nào đi kèm "took no one", "suspended", "filled" thì gạch.

questions.prompt: What does he advise young people to do to save money?
questions.explanation:
Young listeners keep writing in: how do I actually save money on a first salary? Honest answer time. Public transport passes help, but the savings are pocket change unless you're currently driving a limousine. Second-hand shopping? Fine for furniture, though the hunting eats your weekends. The advice that truly moves the needle is this: cook for yourself. Those daily lunches out and delivery dinners quietly eat a third of a young salary. Learn five simple recipes, pack your lunch — watch your account grow within one month.

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án C – Cook for yourself.
• Vì sao đúng: "The advice that truly moves the needle is this: cook for yourself... Learn five simple recipes, pack your lunch — watch your account grow within one month".
• Use public transportation sai: có tiết kiệm nhưng không đáng kể — "Public transport passes help, but the savings are pocket change".
• Buy second-hand items sai: chỉ hợp đồ nội thất và ngốn hết cuối tuần — "Fine for furniture, though the hunting eats your weekends".
👉 Mẹo: dạng hỏi lời khuyên, tìm cụm nâng mức độ: "the advice that truly...", "what really works". Ý đi kèm "help, but", "fine, though" chỉ là lời khuyên hạng hai.

questions.prompt: An expert is talking about lack of satisfaction at work. What should be the solution?
questions.explanation:
A listener asks: I'm deeply unhappy in my role — what now? Careful, friend. Everyone's first instinct is a vacation, but two weeks on a beach only postpones the Monday you dread; the problem waits at your desk, tanned and rested. Quitting entirely for a new job? Drastic, and risky before you've diagnosed the illness. My advice: request a transfer first. Same company, different team, new manager — often the role was wrong, not the workplace. A transfer costs nothing and answers everything. Try that door before the exit.

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án A – Request a transfer.
• Vì sao đúng: "My advice: request a transfer first. Same company, different team, new manager" — và "A transfer costs nothing and answers everything".
• Take a vacation sai: chỉ trì hoãn vấn đề chứ không giải quyết — "two weeks on a beach only postpones the Monday you dread; the problem waits at your desk".
• Find a new job sai: bị đánh giá quá vội và rủi ro — "Quitting entirely for a new job? Drastic, and risky before you've diagnosed the illness".
👉 Mẹo: dạng chuyên gia tư vấn, đáp án nằm ngay sau "My advice:". Phương án bị gắn nhãn tiêu cực ("only postpones", "drastic", "risky") là nhiễu.

questions.prompt: Listen to a woman explaining why she was late. What is the main reason she gets late?
questions.explanation:
I owe the whole team an explanation for this morning's chaos! No, the car didn't break down — she's running beautifully since the service, thank you. And the traffic was actually kind for a Monday, moving the whole way. My disaster happened at the station: I watched my train close its doors from the top of the escalator. Missed it by eight seconds! The next one came forty minutes later, packed with everyone else's bad morning. So: guilty, one missed train, endless apologies — cake for everyone at lunch!

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án C – Missed the train.
• Vì sao đúng: "My disaster happened at the station: I watched my train close its doors from the top of the escalator. Missed it by eight seconds!".
• Car broke down sai: xe vẫn chạy tốt sau khi bảo dưỡng — "No, the car didn't break down — she's running beautifully since the service".
• Heavy traffic sai: hôm đó đường lại thông thoáng — "the traffic was actually kind for a Monday, moving the whole way".
👉 Mẹo: dạng hỏi lý do đi trễ, người nói loại trừ trước rồi mới nêu lý do thật. Đáp án nằm sau "The real problem/My disaster was...".

questions.prompt: A girl is talking about a show she will attend. What will it end with?
questions.explanation:
Saturday's show is going to be special — my sister helped organise it, so I know the secrets! People assume it closes with the mayor's speech, but no, they moved all the talking to the very start, mercifully short. Others expect a firework display; the theatre's roof says absolutely not, fire regulations. What actually ends the night — and keep this between us — is a surprise performance. All the teachers, in costume, doing a full dance number they've rehearsed in secret for months. Last year's finale made the front page!

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án A – A surprise performance.
• Vì sao đúng: "What actually ends the night — and keep this between us — is a surprise performance. All the teachers, in costume, doing a full dance number".
• A speech sai: phần phát biểu đã được chuyển lên ĐẦU chương trình — "they moved all the talking to the very start, mercifully short".
• A firework display sai: bị cấm vì quy định phòng cháy của nhà hát — "the theatre's roof says absolutely not, fire regulations".
👉 Mẹo: câu hỏi "end with" là hỏi TRẬT TỰ thời gian, không chỉ nghe từ khóa. "Moved to the very start" nghĩa là mục đó không còn nằm ở cuối.

questions.prompt: A woman is chatting with a friend about her afternoon plans. What is she going to do this afternoon?
questions.explanation:
My afternoon plans? Finally, something to look forward to! My flatmate voted for the cinema, but the only decent film starts at nine tonight — too late for an afternoon. And sleeping at home, tempting after this week, felt like wasting the first sunny day in ages. So I've booked the two o'clock city tour instead! The old walls, the cathedral roof walk, the guide with all the scandalous historical gossip. Two hours of being a tourist in my own city — camera charged, comfortable shoes on!

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án C – Go on a city tour.
• Vì sao đúng: "So I've booked the two o'clock city tour instead! The old walls, the cathedral roof walk, the guide with all the scandalous historical gossip".
• Go to the cinema sai: là ý của bạn cùng phòng, bị loại vì phim 9h tối, quá muộn cho buổi chiều — "the only decent film starts at nine tonight — too late for an afternoon".
• Sleep at home sai: có hấp dẫn nhưng cô thấy phí ngày nắng đầu tiên — "sleeping at home, tempting after this week, felt like wasting the first sunny day in ages".
👉 Mẹo: dạng hỏi kế hoạch, bám động từ đã chốt: "I've booked", "I've decided". Ý gắn với "my flatmate voted for" là ý người khác.

questions.prompt: How many weeks have they been in India?
questions.explanation:
Woman: You're back from India! You look transformed! How long were you actually there?
Man: The eternal question! Everyone assumes a month.
Woman: Well, your photos felt like four weeks of adventures, honestly.
Man: Four weeks was the original fantasy — the boss laughed at that leave request. Then we trimmed it to three.
Woman: And three didn't survive either?
Man: The project deadline moved, so three collapsed too. Final answer: two weeks, exactly fourteen days. Delhi, Agra, and five days in the south.
Woman: Two weeks that look like a lifetime! The photos fooled us all.
Man: Good packing and no sleep, my friend. Worth every second!

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án A – 2 weeks.
• Vì sao đúng: "Final answer: two weeks, exactly fourteen days. Delhi, Agra, and five days in the south".
• 4 weeks sai: chỉ là dự tính ban đầu, bị sếp bác — "Four weeks was the original fantasy — the boss laughed at that leave request".
• 3 weeks sai: rút xuống ba tuần rồi cũng đổ vì hạn dự án dời — "The project deadline moved, so three collapsed too".
👉 Mẹo: dạng hỏi độ dài chuyến đi, các con số thường giảm dần theo trình tự kể. Chỉ lấy số sau "Final answer", "in the end"; bỏ số gắn với "original", "we trimmed it to".

questions.prompt: Where do they go when they travel to India?
questions.explanation:
M: The India tickets are booked! Now the big question — what do we actually do there?
W: My vote was always the mountains. Cool air, tea gardens...
M: I checked — the mountain trains are sold out for the whole month. Completely full.
W: No! Okay... the beach then? Everyone posts those beach photos.
M: In monsoon season? The waves are dangerous and half the beach cafés close. My colleague was there last July — rain every day.
W: So mountains impossible, beach miserable... what does that leave?
M: The park! The enormous royal gardens in the city — fountains, ruins, those green parrots everywhere. Locals say sunrise there is magic.
W: Sunrise walks in a royal garden... fine, you win. The park it is!
M: Every morning, before the heat. It'll be the best part of the trip, promise.

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án B – Go to the park.
• Vì sao đúng: "The park! The enormous royal gardens in the city — fountains, ruins, those green parrots everywhere" — cô đồng ý "fine, you win. The park it is!".
• Go to the mountains sai: tàu lên núi hết vé cả tháng — "the mountain trains are sold out for the whole month. Completely full".
• Go to the beach sai: đang mùa mưa, sóng nguy hiểm, quán đóng cửa — "In monsoon season? The waves are dangerous and half the beach cafés close".
👉 Mẹo: dạng hai người bàn kế hoạch, đáp án là nơi được nêu SAU CÙNG và có câu đồng thuận ("you win", "it is"). Nơi đi kèm "sold out", "dangerous", "close" thì loại.

questions.prompt: Where did they meet?
questions.explanation:
Woman: There you are! I nearly froze waiting — where were you hiding?
Man: Me? I was exactly where we agreed... I thought. The back entrance, by the car park.
Woman: The back?! That's for deliveries! I said the doors with the flags!
Man: Well, first I actually tried the side entrance, the little one — locked, with a grumpy notice.
Woman: Of course it was locked, it's winter! So how did we find each other?
Man: I finally walked around and there you were, arms crossed, at the front entrance, exactly like a statue of disappointment.
Woman: The front entrance — where every normal person meets! Next time I'm drawing you a map.
Man: Next time, pin the map to my coat!

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án B – The front entrance.
• Vì sao đúng: "I finally walked around and there you were, arms crossed, at the front entrance" — cô xác nhận "The front entrance — where every normal person meets!".
• The back entrance sai: đó là chỗ anh ta chờ nhầm, vốn chỉ dành cho giao hàng — "The back?! That's for deliveries!".
• The side entrance sai: anh có thử nhưng cửa khóa — "first I actually tried the side entrance, the little one — locked, with a grumpy notice".
👉 Mẹo: "Where did they meet?" hỏi nơi họ THỰC SỰ gặp nhau, không phải nơi từng đứng chờ. Bám câu có "there you were", "I found you".

questions.prompt: Aman is ordering a drink. What does he want?
questions.explanation:
Woman: Evening! What are we drinking tonight?
Man: Something cold, I beg you. What's popular?
Woman: The beer garden selection just arrived — six new kinds, very proud of them.
Man: On any other night, yes! But I'm on antibiotics this week, so beer and I are on a break.
Woman: Sensible! Sparkling water then? Doctor-approved, with lime?
Man: Water while everyone celebrates feels like punishment... What's in that tall frosty glass over there?
Woman: Our fresh iced tea — peach, mint, mountains of ice. House recipe.
Man: That's the one. Iced tea, the biggest glass the law allows!
Woman: One legal maximum iced tea, coming up!

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án C – Iced tea.
• Vì sao đúng: sau khi nghe "Our fresh iced tea — peach, mint, mountains of ice", anh chốt "That's the one. Iced tea, the biggest glass the law allows!".
• Beer sai: anh phải kiêng vì đang uống kháng sinh — "I'm on antibiotics this week, so beer and I are on a break".
• Water sai: anh chê là như bị phạt giữa lúc mọi người ăn mừng — "Water while everyone celebrates feels like punishment".
👉 Mẹo: dạng gọi đồ uống, đáp án nằm ở lượt nói CUỐI của khách kèm mô tả cụ thể (cỡ ly, topping). Món có "on a break", "feels like punishment" là món bị từ chối.

questions.prompt: Four people are talking about doing exercise. Match each person to the correct information.
questions.explanation:
Speaker A: My company pays for our gym cards, and at first I thought it was just a nice perk. Six months later I understand their plan perfectly. On the days I swim before the office, I get through my inbox by ten and my ideas actually arrive when I need them. My boss noticed before I did — she said my reports read sharper. Exercise, for me, has become a work tool, as important as my laptop.
Speaker B: Everyone describes this wonderful energy after sport. Where is mine? Forty minutes of anything and I am a wrung-out towel — stairs become mountains, and my bed starts calling my name at eight in the evening. I still show up twice a week because the doctor insists, but let nobody tell you it feels light. For some of us, every single session is heavy from the first stretch to the last.
Speaker C: Book me for any sport, as long as there is a crowd. Wednesday volleyball with the neighbours, weekend badminton with my sisters — the score matters less than the laughing between points. Last week we spent more time imitating each other's serves than actually playing. Exercise alone feels like punishment; exercise with my favourite people is just a party where everyone happens to be sweating.
Speaker D: I will be the honest one here: I detest the whole business. The lycra, the counting, the mirrors, the smell of the changing rooms — every bit of it. My brother signs me up for things and I invent illnesses to escape. People say I simply have not found my sport yet. I have looked for forty years; my sport is reading on the balcony, and I am its champion.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
A = Improve work performance (PARAPHRASE: "inbox by ten... reports read sharper... a work tool"). B = Find exercise tiring (PARAPHRASE: "a wrung-out towel... every session is heavy"). C = Have fun exercising with others (keyword "neighbours... sisters... laughing"). D = Hate exercising (keyword "I detest the whole business"). Nhiễu: alone, lose weight.

questions.prompt: Housing space is more important than farming space.
questions.explanation:
W: Did you see the council's plan to put vegetable beds on the rooftops in the town centre?
M: I did, yes. And honestly, my first reaction was that we haven't got the land to spare. Every spare metre in this city ought to be going up as flats, not lettuce. People need somewhere to live before they need somewhere to grow beans.
W: I don't see it that way at all. Rooftops aren't competing with housing. Nobody is ever going to build a two-bedroom flat on the roof of a supermarket.
M: Hmm. I'm still not convinced the two can sit side by side.
W: And anyway, I find the whole idea rather lovely. Walking down a street where herbs are growing outside the chemist's makes a place feel alive.
M: See, that's where you lose me. I'm not so sure it's charming at all. To me it looks messy. Netting, plastic tubs, half of it brown and dying by August. I'd far rather have a proper park.
W: Well, we shall have to disagree on that one.
M: We shall.
W: There's a practical side too, though. This city genuinely hasn't got enough food coming into it. Supply is far tighter than people realise. One bad winter on the motorways and the shelves are empty.
M: I'll accept the figures you're quoting, but I don't read them that way. We aren't short of food. We're short of cheap food. Plenty is arriving; it's simply expensive. That's a completely different problem.
W: Hmm. Perhaps.
M: What I do think, though, is that it would do something real for jobs round here. Growers, deliveries, small shops buying direct from the roof next door.
W: Oh, absolutely, I agree with you there. Money going round the neighbourhood instead of off to a warehouse two hundred miles away.
M: Exactly. That's the part of it I'd actually vote for.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
Key: Chỗ ở quan trọng hơn chỗ trồng trọt = Man · Nông nghiệp đô thị hấp dẫn = Woman · Thành phố cần thêm lương thực = Woman · Nông nghiệp đô thị có lợi cho kinh tế = Both
1. Housing space is more important than farming space. → Man: Nam nêu "Every spare metre in this city ought to be going up as flats, not lettuce." Nữ phản đối: "I don't see it that way at all. Rooftops aren't competing with housing."
2. Urban farming is appealing. → Woman: Nữ nêu "I find the whole idea rather lovely." Nam phản đối: "that's where you lose me. I'm not so sure it's charming at all."
3. Cities need more food. → Woman: Nữ nêu "This city genuinely hasn't got enough food coming into it." Nam phản đối: "I'll accept the figures you're quoting, but I don't read them that way. We aren't short of food."
4. Urban farming will benefit the urban economy. → Both: Nam nêu "it would do something real for jobs round here". Nữ tán thành: "Oh, absolutely, I agree with you there."
👉 Mẹo: Ý 3 là bẫy kinh điển — nam chấp nhận số liệu ("I'll accept the figures") nhưng bác bỏ kết luận, nên vẫn chỉ là Woman, không phải Both.

questions.prompt: Urban farming is appealing.
Cities need more food.
Urban farming will benefit the urban economy.
What was one major problem the railways faced?
options: The lack of qualified engineers and staff
questions.explanation:
Welcome to today's talk on the history of our railways, and let me take you back to the middle of the twentieth century, the hardest period the network ever faced. When people guess what went wrong in those years, they usually mention extreme weather damaging the tracks, or a shortage of qualified engineers and staff. In fact, the tracks survived the storms well enough, and the railway schools were still producing plenty of capable engineers. The real problem was money — the railways were simply not making enough of it. Cars and trucks had become cheap and popular, so ticket sales and freight income fell year after year, while the cost of maintaining old bridges, stations and engines kept climbing. By the end of the decade, several lines were losing money every single day they operated.
What did the leadership do about it? This is the part of the story that historians still argue about. Some board members wanted to sell major assets to international investors, and one report even suggested suspending all operations for a complete restructure. The leader in charge rejected both ideas. Instead, he decided to continue the policies that had already been implemented in previous years — the same timetables, the same prices, the same structure — believing the economy would eventually turn and passengers would return by themselves. They did not. Most historians now agree that this decision to simply wait made the crisis longer and deeper than it needed to be, and it remains a warning for managers today.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
1. Đáp án: Not making enough money. Bẫy: "extreme weather" và "lack of qualified engineers" đều bị phủ định ("survived the storms", "plenty of capable engineers").
2. Đáp án: Continuing policies that had already been implemented. Bẫy: "selling assets" và "suspending all operations" là đề xuất bị lãnh đạo TỪ CHỐI ("rejected both ideas").

questions.prompt: What did the leader in charge decide to do during this period?
options: Selling the assets to international investors
Continuing policies that had already been implemented
Suspending all operations for a total restructure

questions.prompt: What should people do to maintain a healthy environment?
options: Replace all personal vehicles with electric bicycles
Make a daily effort to recycle, reduce waste, and use energy carefully.
Limit industrial production to strictly rural areas
questions.explanation:
Protecting our planet has become more urgent than ever, so today I want to talk about what ordinary people can actually do. Whenever this topic comes up, someone always suggests something dramatic. Replace every car with an electric bicycle! Move all the factories out of the cities and limit industry to the countryside! Ideas like these sound impressive, but they are neither realistic nor, honestly, necessary. What experts actually recommend is much closer to home: make a daily effort to recycle your rubbish, reduce unnecessary waste, and use energy carefully around the house. Turn off the lights you are not using, repair things instead of replacing them, carry a reusable bag. One person doing this changes little — but millions of people doing it, day after day, change a great deal. The environment is not saved by grand gestures; it is saved by small habits repeated everywhere.
At the same time, we cannot ignore what large-scale human activities are doing. Take deforestation. A few business voices still claim that clearing forests primarily benefits the local economy, and I have even heard the strange argument that it somehow creates more resilient ecosystems for the future. The research says the opposite. Activities like deforestation harm nature directly and cause serious problems — climate change accelerates, floods become more common, and communities suffer long-term health issues from dirtier air and water. Forests are the planet's natural filters, and every hectare we lose makes the daily efforts of ordinary people harder. We need both: small habits at home, and real protection for what remains.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
1. Đáp án: Make a daily effort to recycle, reduce waste, and use energy carefully. Bẫy: "electric bicycles" và "limit industry to rural areas" được nhắc là ý tưởng "neither realistic nor necessary".
2. Đáp án: They harm nature and cause problems like climate change and health issues. Bẫy: "benefit the local economy" và "resilient ecosystems" là lập luận bị bác ("The research says the opposite").

questions.prompt: According to the text, how do human activities like deforestation affect us?
options: They create more resilient ecosystems for the future
They harm nature and cause problems like climate change and health issues.
They primarily benefit the local economy in the short term

questions.prompt: A woman is going home after shopping. What did she buy?
questions.explanation:
What an afternoon at the sales! My feet are finished but my bag is happy. Listen — I went in for a blouse for the office, tried on five, hated every single one, the mirrors in that shop are cruel. Then the hat section called me, and there was a gorgeous straw one... but eighteen pounds for a hat I'd wear twice? No. And then I saw it: the dress. Navy blue, little white dots, perfect for summer weddings and Sunday lunches. Bought it before my brain could argue!

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án A – A dress.
• Vì sao đúng: "And then I saw it: the dress. Navy blue, little white dots, perfect for summer weddings and Sunday lunches. Bought it before my brain could argue!".
• A blouse sai: thử năm cái đều không ưng, không mua — "I went in for a blouse for the office, tried on five, hated every single one".
• A hat sai: thích nhưng chê đắt so với số lần dùng — "eighteen pounds for a hat I'd wear twice? No".
👉 Mẹo: dạng hỏi mua gì, chỉ tính động từ "bought". "Went in for", "tried on", "saw" chưa phải là đã mua.

questions.prompt: A woman is talking about her babysitter. How old is the babysitter?
questions.explanation:
Our new babysitter is a treasure, let me tell you about her! When she first wrote to us, I misread her message and thought she was twenty — I worried that might be a little young. My husband, typically, insisted she must be at least twenty-two because she seems so responsible. We were both wrong! We checked her student card for the paperwork: she's twenty-one, in her third year of early childhood studies. Twenty-one, patient as a saint, and the kids already adore her!

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án B – 21.
• Vì sao đúng: "We checked her student card for the paperwork: she's twenty-one, in her third year of early childhood studies".
• 20 sai: do người mẹ đọc nhầm tin nhắn — "I misread her message and thought she was twenty".
• 22 sai: chỉ là phỏng đoán của người chồng — "My husband, typically, insisted she must be at least twenty-two because she seems so responsible".
👉 Mẹo: dạng hỏi tuổi, con số đúng luôn có NGUỒN GIẤY TỜ (student card, ID, passport). Số gắn với "thought", "insisted", "misread" là nhiễu.

questions.prompt: A man is talking about his job. Where is he working now?
questions.explanation:
My career took a turn nobody predicted, least of all me! After graduation I nearly stayed at the university — they offered me a teaching assistant role, flattering, but the pay was pocket money. Then came two years in a big trading company: great salary, endless hours, my weekends fed to spreadsheets. So last spring I jumped again, and now I work in a bank. The mortgage department, regular hours, proper holidays, and my own desk by the window. Third time lucky — this one I'm keeping!

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án C – In a bank.
• Vì sao đúng: "So last spring I jumped again, and now I work in a bank. The mortgage department, regular hours, proper holidays".
• At a university sai: chỉ là lời mời sau tốt nghiệp mà anh không nhận vì lương bèo — "they offered me a teaching assistant role, flattering, but the pay was pocket money".
• In a big company sai: là chỗ làm trước đó, đã nghỉ — "two years in a big trading company: great salary, endless hours, my weekends fed to spreadsheets".
👉 Mẹo: câu hỏi "Where is he working NOW?" phải bám thì hiện tại. Chỗ nào đi kèm "after graduation", "then came", "two years" đều thuộc quá khứ.

questions.prompt: The man is talking about his key. Where did he find the key?
questions.explanation:
The great key hunt of this morning — I have to tell someone! I was already late, tearing the flat apart. First the car, obviously: checked every seat, under the mats, the glove box — nothing. Then the bedroom, because keys love yesterday's trousers: emptied every pocket in the wardrobe — also nothing. Finally I gave up and went to leave... and froze. There it was — the key was in the front door. Outside! It had spent the whole night sitting in the lock. New rule in this house: pocket check before bed.

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án B – In the front door.
• Vì sao đúng: "There it was — the key was in the front door. Outside! It had spent the whole night sitting in the lock".
• In his car sai: đã lục kỹ mà không thấy — "First the car, obviously: checked every seat, under the mats, the glove box — nothing".
• In the bedroom sai: cũng lục hết túi quần trong tủ mà không có — "emptied every pocket in the wardrobe — also nothing".
👉 Mẹo: "Where did he FIND it?" khác "Where did he look?". Nơi đi kèm "nothing", "no luck" là chỗ tìm hụt; đáp án nằm sau "Finally", "There it was".

questions.prompt: Mary is talking to her friend about her new home. What does she ask her friend about?
options: Where to buy a new table
questions.explanation:
Hi! It's Mary, calling about my endless apartment project! The living room is nearly human now — the mirror question you can forget, my mother donated her big gold one, drama included, free of charge. And the furniture is all chosen, delivered, assembled; my thumbs survived the instruction manuals. But one mystery remains, and you're my expert: where does one buy a proper dining table these days? Solid wood, seats six, doesn't cost a kidney? You bought yours somewhere clever — call me back with the address!

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án A – Where to buy a new table.
• Vì sao đúng: "one mystery remains, and you're my expert: where does one buy a proper dining table these days?" — và cô nhờ "call me back with the address!".
• The furniture sai: đồ đạc đã mua, giao và lắp xong — "the furniture is all chosen, delivered, assembled".
• Mirror sai: mẹ cô đã cho một cái miễn phí nên khỏi bàn — "the mirror question you can forget, my mother donated her big gold one, drama included, free of charge".
👉 Mẹo: dạng hỏi "cô ấy hỏi bạn về việc gì", tìm CÂU HỎI thật sự trong bài. Món đi kèm "you can forget", "all done" là việc đã xong.

questions.prompt: The woman is discussing her new exercise routine. How much time does she spend cycling?
questions.explanation:
My new exercise routine is finally settled, and my body has opinions! Monday and Thursday I swim for forty-five minutes — that part everyone knows. The gym circuit takes a full hour on Saturdays, sixty sweaty minutes, don't remind me. But the cycling, my favourite part: every morning before work, thirty-five minutes along the river path. Thirty-five exactly, timed by my watch — enough to wake up, not enough to need a second shower. The routine of a genius, if I say so myself!

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án B – 35 minutes.
• Vì sao đúng: "the cycling, my favourite part: every morning before work, thirty-five minutes along the river path. Thirty-five exactly, timed by my watch".
• 45 minutes sai: đó là thời gian BƠI thứ Hai và thứ Năm — "Monday and Thursday I swim for forty-five minutes".
• 60 minutes sai: đó là buổi tập gym thứ Bảy — "The gym circuit takes a full hour on Saturdays, sixty sweaty minutes".
👉 Mẹo: dạng hỏi thời lượng của MỘT môn cụ thể, vừa nghe vừa ghép cặp môn–số phút. Chỉ lấy con số đứng cạnh đúng từ khóa trong câu hỏi (cycling).

questions.prompt: A woman is calling her son. What time will the mother meet the son?
questions.explanation:
Sweetheart, it's mum, listen carefully because plans moved again! Forget two o'clock — grandma's doctor visit ran over and we're still in the waiting room. I thought we'd manage six, but that's too late, the shops will be closing and we still need your suit fitted. So: three o'clock, at the fountain entrance of the shopping centre. Three, on the dot! I have your measurements, grandma has opinions, and we have one hour to make you elegant. Don't be late, my love!

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án C – Three o'clock.
• Vì sao đúng: "So: three o'clock, at the fountain entrance of the shopping centre. Three, on the dot!".
• Two o'clock sai: bị hủy vì buổi khám của bà kéo dài — "Forget two o'clock — grandma's doctor visit ran over and we're still in the waiting room".
• Six o'clock sai: quá muộn, cửa hàng sắp đóng mà còn phải đo vest — "I thought we'd manage six, but that's too late, the shops will be closing".
👉 Mẹo: dạng hỏi giờ hẹn, gạch mốc đi sau "Forget..." và mốc bị chê "too late". Giờ đúng thường kèm địa điểm cụ thể và cụm "on the dot".

questions.prompt: A man is talking about his daily routine. What does he do after work?
questions.explanation:
My daily routine has one golden hour, and it happens right after work. My colleagues always head to the coffee shop downstairs — I skip it; coffee after five keeps me staring at the ceiling till two in the morning. And going straight home? I did that for years: sofa, screen, sleep, repeat. Never again. Now, every evening at five thirty, I play football — five-a-side on the pitch behind the depot, ninety minutes of running and shouting with the lads. Cheapest therapy in town, and I sleep like a baby.

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án C – Play football.
• Vì sao đúng: "Now, every evening at five thirty, I play football — five-a-side on the pitch behind the depot, ninety minutes of running and shouting with the lads".
• Go to the coffee shop sai: đó là thói quen của đồng nghiệp, anh bỏ qua vì cà phê sau 5h làm mất ngủ — "My colleagues always head to the coffee shop downstairs — I skip it".
• Go home sai: là thói quen CŨ đã bỏ hẳn — "And going straight home? I did that for years: sofa, screen, sleep, repeat. Never again".
👉 Mẹo: dạng hỏi thói quen hiện tại, bám mốc "Now", "every evening". Ý gắn với "I did that for years", "never again" là quá khứ đã bỏ.

questions.prompt: Doctor’s office is calling about a change in the appointment. When is the new appointment?
questions.explanation:
Good afternoon, this is Doctor Mitchell's surgery calling about your appointment change. Your original slot on Friday the fourteenth has to move, as the doctor will be at a medical conference. We know Wednesday the twelfth was mentioned as a possibility earlier — please disregard that, the morning is fully booked. Your new confirmed appointment is Thursday the thirteenth at nine thirty. Thursday the thirteenth, half past nine. Please arrive ten minutes early with your insurance card. Thank you!

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án A – Thursday 13th.
• Vì sao đúng: "Your new confirmed appointment is Thursday the thirteenth at nine thirty. Thursday the thirteenth, half past nine".
• Friday 14th sai: là lịch CŨ, phải dời vì bác sĩ đi hội thảo — "Your original slot on Friday the fourteenth has to move, as the doctor will be at a medical conference".
• Wednesday 12th sai: từng được nhắc nhưng buổi sáng đã kín chỗ — "We know Wednesday the twelfth was mentioned as a possibility earlier — please disregard that, the morning is fully booked".
👉 Mẹo: tin nhắn đổi lịch luôn nêu đủ 3 ngày. Bám cụm "new confirmed appointment" và ngày được LẶP LẠI hai lần; bỏ ngày có "original", "disregard".

questions.prompt: A man is talking to a waiter. What drink does the man choose?
questions.explanation:
Woman: Good afternoon! Ready to order drinks?
Man: More than ready — what a heat wave! What do you recommend?
Woman: Our milk tea is famous — sweet, creamy, with the tapioca pearls.
Man: Tempting, but milk and this weather argue in my stomach, sadly.
Woman: Understood! Hot tea, then? We have a beautiful jasmine.
Man: Hot tea in thirty-five degrees? You're testing me!
Woman: Ha! Then the obvious hero: fresh iced tea, lemon and mint, crushed ice to the top.
Man: Now we're talking. Iced tea, large, extra mint — and mercy on the sugar.
Woman: One large iced tea, gentle sugar. Rescue is coming!

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án C – Iced tea.
• Vì sao đúng: sau gợi ý "fresh iced tea, lemon and mint, crushed ice to the top", anh chốt "Now we're talking. Iced tea, large, extra mint".
• Milk tea sai: anh từ chối vì sữa không hợp bụng khi trời nóng — "milk and this weather argue in my stomach, sadly".
• Hot tea sai: bị gạt vì trời 35 độ — "Hot tea in thirty-five degrees? You're testing me!".
👉 Mẹo: dạng gọi đồ uống, phục vụ gợi ý 3 món theo thứ tự; đáp án là món khách CHỐT kèm size/yêu cầu riêng ("large, extra mint").

questions.prompt: Louis is calling his friend Standar. Where will Luis meet Standar?
questions.explanation:
Man: Standar! It's Louis. Confirming tomorrow before I sleep — where do we meet?
Woman: I was about to text you! You said the café first, right?
Man: I did, but I checked — the café doesn't open till nine, and our train is at nine fifteen. Too tight.
Woman: True. Near the ticket counter then? Central, easy to find...
Man: Have you seen the counter queues on a Saturday? We'd lose each other in the crowd instantly.
Woman: Fair. So — outside the station? The main steps, by the flower stall?
Man: Outside the station, by the flowers, eight forty-five. Tickets already in my pocket!
Woman: Eight forty-five. Bring coffee, the café won't!

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án A – Outside the station.
• Vì sao đúng: "Outside the station, by the flowers, eight forty-five. Tickets already in my pocket!".
• At the cafe sai: quán 9h mới mở trong khi tàu chạy 9h15 — "the café doesn't open till nine, and our train is at nine fifteen. Too tight".
• Near the ticket counter sai: thứ Bảy quầy vé đông, dễ lạc nhau — "Have you seen the counter queues on a Saturday? We'd lose each other in the crowd instantly".
👉 Mẹo: dạng hẹn địa điểm, chốt nằm ở lượt nói cuối kèm mốc giờ cụ thể. Nơi đi kèm "doesn't open till", "too tight", "queues" là loại.

questions.prompt: Jane is calling her friend Martha. What time are they going to meet?
questions.explanation:
Woman: Martha! It's Jane. About tonight — what time works?
Woman2: I was thinking four? We'd catch the whole afternoon.
Woman: Four is impossible for me, I'm at the dentist until quarter to five, remember?
Woman2: Oh right, the tooth saga! Six, then? After all the traffic dies?
Woman: Six is too late — the restaurant stops serving the early menu at six, and I want that discount!
Woman2: Ha! The truth comes out. So we split it: five thirty?
Woman: Five thirty is perfect. Dentist done, discount alive, traffic bearable.
Woman2: Five thirty at the corner table. Bring your appetite and your new tooth!

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án B – 5.30.
• Vì sao đúng: "So we split it: five thirty?" — "Five thirty is perfect. Dentist done, discount alive, traffic bearable", chốt "Five thirty at the corner table".
• 4.00 sai: cô ở phòng nha đến gần 5h — "Four is impossible for me, I'm at the dentist until quarter to five".
• 6.00 sai: nhà hàng ngừng phục vụ thực đơn giá ưu đãi lúc 6h — "the restaurant stops serving the early menu at six, and I want that discount!".
👉 Mẹo: khi hai người đưa hai mốc trái ngược (quá sớm / quá muộn), đáp án thường nằm Ở GIỮA. Nghe cụm thỏa hiệp "So we split it".

questions.prompt: Jack is calling to invite a friend to his house. What color is Jack’s house??
questions.explanation:
Man: Hello! Jack here — you're coming Saturday, yes? Let me describe the house so you don't wander the whole street.
Woman: Please do! Your street has forty identical houses, I've seen it.
Man: Identical except mine! Now — my neighbour's house is black, very dramatic, don't knock there, the dog is loud.
Woman: Noted. Avoid the black one and its opera dog.
Man: And across the road there's a green one — also not me, that's the retired teacher.
Woman: Black no, green no... so yours is...?
Man: Red! Bright red with white windows — my wife's choice, visible from space. You can't miss it.
Woman: A red beacon among the grey. Saturday at six, I'll follow the colour!

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án B – Red.
• Vì sao đúng: "Red! Bright red with white windows — my wife's choice, visible from space. You can't miss it".
• Black sai: là nhà hàng xóm, có con chó sủa to — "my neighbour's house is black, very dramatic, don't knock there, the dog is loud".
• Green sai: là nhà thầy giáo về hưu bên kia đường — "across the road there's a green one — also not me, that's the retired teacher".
👉 Mẹo: dạng hỏi màu/đặc điểm, mỗi màu gắn với một CHỦ NHÀ. Bám sở hữu cách: "mine", "my house" mới là đáp án; "my neighbour's", "that's the..." là nhiễu.

title: Đề 12 - The purposes of using the internet

questions.prompt: Four people are talking about using the Internet. Match each person to the correct information.
questions.explanation:
Speaker A: After a long shift, my routine never changes: dinner, sofa, screen. The internet replaced my television years ago — I follow three series at once and pick films by mood, from black-and-white classics to last month's releases. My flatmate and I have a Friday tradition of choosing the worst-reviewed film we can find and enjoying every terrible minute. Without the streaming sites, my evenings would be a lot quieter and a lot duller.
Speaker B: University turned me into a night-time typist. Every project, every essay, every group presentation runs through the online portal — I download the readings, join the shared documents, and submit everything before the midnight deadline. When I got stuck on statistics last term, a tutorial video explained in nine minutes what the lecture had failed to explain in ninety. My grades genuinely live or die by my connection.
Speaker C: My parents are back in the countryside and my brother works abroad, so the internet is really our dinner table now. Sunday evening video calls with the whole family, my mother showing me her garden through the camera, my father asking if I am eating properly. In between there are voice messages and photos of everything from new haircuts to burnt pancakes. Distance used to mean silence; now it just means a screen between us.
Speaker D: Before I even brush my teeth, I check the transport app. It tells me whether my usual bus is on time, which platform the train leaves from, and how the traffic is moving on the ring road. Twice last month it warned me about strikes before my colleagues had heard a word. Planning my route used to be guesswork and luck. Now the whole journey is arranged while the kettle boils.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
A = Watch movies (keyword "films by mood... streaming"). B = Complete assignments (keyword "essay... submit"). C = Stay in touch with family (PARAPHRASE: "our dinner table now... Distance used to mean silence"). D = Find transport information (PARAPHRASE: "whether my usual bus is on time... journey arranged"). Nhiễu: news, games.

questions.prompt: People share similar ideas about beauty
questions.explanation:
M: You went to that photography exhibition at the weekend, didn't you? What was it actually like?
W: Fascinating, genuinely. Portraits from about twelve different countries. And what struck me was how much overlap there was. Deep down, I think we all recognise the same faces as attractive, wherever we happen to come from.
M: Hmm, I'm not so sure about that. I'd say what counts as attractive varies enormously from one place to another. It's almost entirely learned, in my view.
W: There's quite a lot of research suggesting otherwise, you know.
M: I'll accept the research exists, but I'm not convinced it proves very much. What I am certain of is that these things shift with the decades. Look at any family album and you'll see the standards moving.
W: Well, that rather depends what you're looking at. I'd argue the fashions change, the hair and the clothes, but the underlying face people admire stays remarkably steady.
M: We'll have to differ on that one, I think.
W: We will, clearly. Though there was one room I absolutely loved. Photographs of an old scrapyard, of all places, and they were genuinely lovely to look at.
M: Oh, I'm completely with you there. Some of the most striking things I've ever seen have been in spots you'd never think to look. Building sites, motorway bridges, that sort of thing.
W: Exactly my point. It turns up wherever it likes, and usually where nobody's expecting it.
M: It does. And that's partly why I think the old-fashioned standards are quietly on their way out. The next generation simply won't put up with them.
W: I don't see that happening, personally. People have been predicting exactly that for fifty years now, and the magazines still look much the same to me.
M: Give it another ten years and ask me again.
W: I'll believe it when I see it.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
Key: Mọi người có quan niệm giống nhau về cái đẹp = Woman · Quan niệm về cái đẹp thay đổi theo thời gian = Man · Cái đẹp có thể tìm thấy ở nơi bất ngờ = Both · Quan niệm truyền thống về cái đẹp sẽ thay đổi = Man

1. People share similar ideas about beauty → Woman: người phụ nữ nêu "Deep down, I think we all recognise the same faces as attractive, wherever we happen to come from." Người đàn ông phản đối: "Hmm, I'm not so sure about that. I'd say what counts as attractive varies enormously from one place to another."

2. Ideas about beauty change over time → Man: người đàn ông nêu "these things shift with the decades. Look at any family album and you'll see the standards moving." Người phụ nữ phản đối: "I'd argue the fashions change... but the underlying face people admire stays remarkably steady."

3. Beauty can be found in unlikely places → Both: người phụ nữ nêu "Photographs of an old scrapyard, of all places, and they were genuinely lovely to look at.", người đàn ông tán thành: "Oh, I'm completely with you there. Some of the most striking things I've ever seen have been in spots you'd never think to look."

4. Traditional ideas about beauty are going to change → Man: người đàn ông nêu "the old-fashioned standards are quietly on their way out. The next generation simply won't put up with them." Người phụ nữ phản đối: "I don't see that happening, personally... the magazines still look much the same to me."

👉 Mẹo: Bẫy ở ý 1 — "I'll accept the research exists" của người đàn ông chỉ là nhượng bộ một nửa, không phải đồng ý, nên ý 1 vẫn là Woman chứ không phải Both.

questions.prompt: Ideas about beauty change over time
Beauty can be found in unlikely places
Traditional ideas about beauty are going to change
What does the speaker say about short-term goals?
options: It helps people adjust their priorities when circumstances change.
It creates pressure and limits creativity
It only apply to specific situations or certain types of people
questions.explanation:
Today I want to talk about making plans, and especially about short-term goals, because they have an unfair reputation. Many people believe short-term goals only apply to specific situations or certain types of people — students before exams, perhaps, or athletes before a competition. Others complain that these goals create pressure and limit creativity, as if writing down a target somehow locks your imagination in a box. Both views miss what short-term goals actually do best. Their real strength is flexibility: they help people adjust their priorities when circumstances change. Say you plan to read three books this month, and then a busy project lands on your desk. A short-term goal bends easily — you read one book instead, and set a fresh target next month. Nothing is broken, nothing is lost, and you are still moving forward. Long plans crack when life changes; short goals simply bend.
Now let me widen the picture to goal setting in general, because here too the common opinions are wrong. You will hear that having goals leads to confusion and distraction, with too many targets pulling you in different directions. And optimistic people love to say that goals bring about wonderful opportunities. My view, after years of coaching, is more practical than either: goal setting can prevent you from making mistakes. When your goal is written clearly, you check every decision against it, and you notice bad choices before you make them. The person without goals says yes to everything and discovers the mistake afterwards. The person with goals sees it coming.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
1. Đáp án: It helps people adjust their priorities when circumstances change. Bẫy: "create pressure and limit creativity" và "only apply to specific situations" đều được nhắc là quan niệm sai ("Both views miss...").
2. Đáp án: It can prevent you from making mistakes. Bẫy: "confusion and distraction" là lời phàn nàn của người khác, "bring about opportunities" là lời của "optimistic people" — người nói chọn ý thực dụng hơn cả hai.

questions.prompt: What is the speaker's opinion about goal setting?
options: It can lead to confusion and distraction
It can prevent you from making mistakes
It can bring about opportunities for individuals

questions.prompt: Why do modern buildings stand out?
options: They prioritize traditional materials over steel
They are primarily built in rural environments
questions.explanation:
Let us talk about modern architecture, because our cities are changing in front of our eyes. Why do modern buildings stand out? Some people expect me to say it is because architects now prioritise traditional materials — wood, brick and stone — over steel. Others assume the most striking new buildings are primarily built in rural environments, away from the crowds. Neither is true. Walk through any city centre and you will see the real answer: modern buildings stand out because they associate so closely with modern cityscapes. Glass surfaces, straight lines, minimal decoration — each new tower is designed to match the clean, uniform look of the contemporary city around it. They are recognised not as individual masterpieces but as pieces of one large visual identity, the way letters belong to the same alphabet.
But being recognisable is not the same as being impressive, and here I must be honest. Architecture magazines love to claim that today's buildings represent the peak of architectural innovation, and city councils like to boast that every new project focuses on maximising public green spaces. Look closely and both claims fall apart. What many new buildings actually display is a clear lack of ambition. Developers choose efficiency, low cost and fast construction over creativity, so the same glass box appears in London, Dubai and Singapore with only the address changed. Our skylines are filling with buildings that are tall, clean, profitable — and instantly forgettable. Until developers reward imagination again, the cities of this century will all look like each other.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
1. Đáp án: They associate with modern cityscapes. Bẫy: "traditional materials" và "rural environments" đều bị phủ định ("Neither is true").
2. Đáp án: They often display a lack of ambition. Bẫy: "peak of architectural innovation" và "public green spaces" là tuyên bố của tạp chí/chính quyền bị bác ("both claims fall apart").

questions.prompt: What does the speaker say about many new buildings?
options: They often display a lack of ambition.
They represent the peak of architectural innovation
They focus on maximizing public green spaces

questions.prompt: A man is talking about his eating habit. What time does he usually eat?
questions.explanation:
My eating schedule confuses every dinner guest we've ever had! Most of my friends eat at eight, fashionably late, wine and candles. My brother's family sits down at five like clockwork, farmers' hours, he calls it. Me? Seven o'clock, every single evening, rain or shine. It started with my old night shifts and simply stayed. Seven — early enough to digest, late enough to cook properly. My stomach could replace the town clock, my wife says!

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án B – 7 o'clock.
• Vì sao đúng: "Me? Seven o'clock, every single evening, rain or shine" — và "Seven — early enough to digest, late enough to cook properly".
• 8 o'clock sai: đó là giờ ăn của bạn bè anh — "Most of my friends eat at eight, fashionably late, wine and candles".
• 5 o'clock sai: đó là giờ ăn của gia đình ông anh trai — "My brother's family sits down at five like clockwork, farmers' hours".
👉 Mẹo: dạng hỏi thói quen của NGƯỜI NÓI, bắt tín hiệu đổi chủ ngữ "Me?", "As for me". Giờ gắn với "my friends", "my brother" chỉ là nền so sánh.

questions.prompt: A professor is talking to his student. What does the professor ask his student to do?
questions.explanation:
Come in, come in — I'll be brief, I know you have lectures. About the research project: good progress, but one thing needs to change. The written essay you proposed? Not needed anymore — the committee dropped that requirement last month, mercifully. And don't worry about the end-of-term report either; I'll compile that myself from your notes. What I do need from you is bigger: I want you to speak at the spring conference. Twenty minutes, your findings, real audience. You're ready — I wouldn't ask otherwise.

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án B – Speak at the conference.
• Vì sao đúng: "What I do need from you is bigger: I want you to speak at the spring conference. Twenty minutes, your findings, real audience".
• Write an essay sai: yêu cầu này đã bị hội đồng bỏ — "The written essay you proposed? Not needed anymore — the committee dropped that requirement last month".
• Submit a report sai: giáo sư tự tổng hợp báo cáo cuối kỳ — "don't worry about the end-of-term report either; I'll compile that myself from your notes".
👉 Mẹo: dạng hỏi "yêu cầu làm gì", bám cụm "What I do need from you is". Việc đi kèm "not needed", "don't worry about", "I'll do it myself" đều bị loại.

questions.prompt: A man is talking about his old school days. What was the man's favorite thing about school?
questions.explanation:
School days, what a question! My wife loved the maths classes — equations were her music, strange woman. Me? Numbers were my weekly punishment, and sports even worse: always picked last, always in goal, always freezing. But the history classes — those were mine. Old maps, battles, kings poisoning each other! Mr. Elwood telling the French Revolution like a thriller, chalk flying. I chose my degree because of that classroom. History — the only lessons I ever ran to.

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án B – History classes.
• Vì sao đúng: "But the history classes — those were mine... I chose my degree because of that classroom. History — the only lessons I ever ran to".
• Math classes sai: là môn vợ anh mê, còn anh thì sợ — "My wife loved the maths classes"; "Numbers were my weekly punishment".
• Sports sai: bị chê thẳng là còn tệ hơn toán — "sports even worse: always picked last, always in goal, always freezing".
👉 Mẹo: dạng hỏi sở thích, tách rõ ai thích gì. Bám sở hữu "those were mine"; môn gán cho "my wife" là nhiễu.

questions.prompt: Listen to a radio man talking about a new popular song. Which is the most attractive part of the song?
questions.explanation:
The song of the summer, listeners — let's talk about why it owns every radio! Musicians praise the melody, sweet but honestly nothing revolutionary, you've heard that tune's cousins before. The rhythm gets the clubs moving, sure, a solid beat, nothing more. But the words — the words are why grandmothers and teenagers both cry to this song! Poetry about going home after years away, every line a little knife. People tattoo these lyrics, print them at weddings. The words, my friends. That's the magic.

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án C – The words.
• Vì sao đúng: "the words are why grandmothers and teenagers both cry to this song! Poetry about going home after years away... The words, my friends. That's the magic".
• The melody sai: bị chê là bình thường, không có gì mới — "the melody, sweet but honestly nothing revolutionary, you've heard that tune's cousins before".
• The rhythm sai: chỉ ở mức tạm ổn — "The rhythm gets the clubs moving, sure, a solid beat, nothing more".
👉 Mẹo: dạng hỏi "phần hay nhất", nghe cụm hạ giá trị "nothing revolutionary", "nothing more". Yếu tố được khen bằng từ mạnh ("that's the magic") mới là đáp án.

questions.prompt: A man is talking about the environment of the countryside. What is the main cause of poor air quality?
questions.explanation:
People romanticise our countryside air, but let me tell you the truth from my porch! Everyone blames the factories first — we have exactly one, the little dairy plant, cleaner than most kitchens. Then they point at cars; forty vehicles pass on a busy day, hardly a highway. No — the real trouble comes every autumn, from the fires. Farmers burning the fields after harvest, smoke rolling in for weeks, the whole valley coughing under a grey blanket. Those countryside fires — that's what steals our clean air.

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án C – Fires from the countryside.
• Vì sao đúng: "the real trouble comes every autumn, from the fires. Farmers burning the fields after harvest, smoke rolling in for weeks, the whole valley coughing".
• Factories sai: cả vùng chỉ có một nhà máy sữa nhỏ và rất sạch — "we have exactly one, the little dairy plant, cleaner than most kitchens".
• Cars sai: lượng xe quá ít để gây ô nhiễm — "forty vehicles pass on a busy day, hardly a highway".
👉 Mẹo: dạng hỏi nguyên nhân chính, đáp án nằm sau "No — the real trouble is". Thứ mà "everyone blames" hoặc "they point at" thường là nhiễu.

questions.prompt: Stephanie is looking for a job taking care of children. How old is she?
questions.explanation:
Hello! I'm Stephanie, answering your childcare advertisement — let me introduce myself properly! People often guess I'm twenty-five because I'm tall, and my mother jokes I have the patience of a thirty-year-old. But no — I'm twenty-one, in my third year of nursery education studies. Twenty-one, with four younger siblings, so children hold no mysteries for me! I'm free every weekend, I cook, I do first aid, and I know forty fairy tales by heart. References ready — call me anytime!

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án A – 21.
• Vì sao đúng: "But no — I'm twenty-one, in my third year of nursery education studies. Twenty-one, with four younger siblings".
• 25 sai: chỉ là phỏng đoán của người khác vì cô cao — "People often guess I'm twenty-five because I'm tall".
• 30 sai: là câu đùa của mẹ cô về tính điềm đạm — "my mother jokes I have the patience of a thirty-year-old".
👉 Mẹo: dạng hỏi tuổi, gạch ngay số đi kèm "guess", "jokes", "people think". Tuổi thật nằm sau "But no — I'm..." và thường được nhắc lại lần hai.

questions.prompt: An author is talking about her daily routine. When does she usually write?
questions.explanation:
Readers imagine my writing life as candlelit midnights — the truth is far less romantic! Mornings are hopeless: before eleven I'm a zombie with a teacup, answering emails and staring at the garden. And night writing, which sounds so poetic? I tried it for a whole winter and deleted every word the next day — tired sentences, all of them. My real work happens in the afternoons. One o'clock to six, phone in the drawer, same chair, same desk. Every book I've published was written after lunch.

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án A – In the afternoons.
• Vì sao đúng: "My real work happens in the afternoons. One o'clock to six, phone in the drawer, same chair, same desk. Every book I've published was written after lunch".
• In the mornings sai: cô thừa nhận buổi sáng vô dụng — "Mornings are hopeless: before eleven I'm a zombie with a teacup".
• At night sai: đã thử suốt một mùa đông rồi xóa sạch — "I tried it for a whole winter and deleted every word the next day — tired sentences, all of them".
👉 Mẹo: dạng hỏi thời điểm làm việc, bám cụm "My real work happens...". Khung giờ gắn với "hopeless", "I tried... and deleted" là mồi nhử.

questions.prompt: A woman is talking about her usual Saturday routine. What does she usually do on Saturdays?
questions.explanation:
My Saturdays follow a sacred pattern, ask anyone who knows me! People assume I spend them shopping — wrong, I do all that online on Wednesday nights, crowds terrify me. Birthday parties happen maybe monthly, hardly a routine. No, every Saturday, without fail, I see my family. Morning coffee at grandma's, lunch at my parents', afternoon chaos with my sister's twins. Three houses, one street, forty years of tradition. Saturday is family day — the world can wait until Monday!

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án B – Sees her family.
• Vì sao đúng: "every Saturday, without fail, I see my family. Morning coffee at grandma's, lunch at my parents', afternoon chaos with my sister's twins".
• Goes shopping sai: cô mua online vào tối thứ Tư vì sợ đám đông — "wrong, I do all that online on Wednesday nights, crowds terrify me".
• Goes to a birthday party sai: khoảng một lần mỗi tháng, không phải thói quen — "Birthday parties happen maybe monthly, hardly a routine".
👉 Mẹo: câu hỏi có "usually/routine" thì loại mọi việc đi kèm "maybe", "hardly a routine", hoặc gắn với ngày khác trong tuần.

questions.prompt: A man is talking about his family trip. What does the man’s wife enjoy?
questions.explanation:
Our family trips are a delicate diplomatic operation! My daughter lives for the shopping streets — every city, every market, her suitcase returns pregnant. I'm the hiking madman, dragging everyone up hills for views they claim not to need. And my wife? Her camera is her passport. Photography — that's her whole holiday! She rises before dawn for the light, photographs fishermen, doorways, strangers' laundry. Our house is a gallery of her trips. We walk; she captures. Everyone's happy!

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án A – Photography.
• Vì sao đúng: "And my wife? Her camera is her passport. Photography — that's her whole holiday! She rises before dawn for the light".
• Shopping sai: đó là sở thích của con gái — "My daughter lives for the shopping streets — every city, every market".
• Hiking sai: đó là sở thích của chính người kể — "I'm the hiking madman, dragging everyone up hills".
👉 Mẹo: câu hỏi chỉ đích danh một người (the man's WIFE). Đợi câu đổi chủ ngữ "And my wife?" rồi mới lấy đáp án — ba sở thích thuộc ba người khác nhau.

questions.prompt: A woman is talking about her job. What encouraged her to become a scientist?
questions.explanation:
Man: Doctor, our listeners love origin stories. What pushed you toward science? A brilliant teacher? Your mother?
Woman: Ha! My mother campaigned hard for law school, actually — science horrified her. Not her doing at all.
Man: The family computer, then? Every scientist my age says the computer.
Woman: I only touched a computer at university — far too late to light any fires.
Man: So what was it?
Woman: A large stone. I was seven, on holiday, and found this rock packed with spiral shells. Fossils! I demanded explanations from every adult on the beach.
Man: And nobody could answer?
Woman: Nobody. So I decided I would become the person who could. That stone still sits on my desk, forty years later.

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án C – A large stone.
• Vì sao đúng: "A large stone. I was seven, on holiday, and found this rock packed with spiral shells. Fossils!" — và "That stone still sits on my desk, forty years later".
• Her mother sai: mẹ cô còn hướng cô học luật và ghét khoa học — "My mother campaigned hard for law school, actually — science horrified her. Not her doing at all".
• Her computer sai: cô chỉ chạm vào máy tính khi đã vào đại học, quá muộn — "I only touched a computer at university — far too late to light any fires".
👉 Mẹo: dạng phỏng vấn hỏi "điều gì thúc đẩy", người dẫn thường đoán sai hai lần trước. Đáp án là câu trả lời cuối của khách mời kèm kỷ niệm cụ thể.

questions.prompt: Listen to the speaker talking about their weekly schedule. When is the meeting scheduled?
questions.explanation:
Woman: Before you run off — the project meeting this week. When is it again? My calendar shows three different colours.
Man: The app struck again! What does Monday morning say?
Woman: Nine o'clock, big room?
Man: That's the sales huddle, ten minutes of shouting numbers. Not ours.
Woman: Then someone told me Friday afternoon...
Man: Pure legend. Half the office vanishes after Friday lunch and management knows it.
Woman: So our meeting is...?
Man: Wednesday afternoon, two thirty, same as all quarter. Agenda by Tuesday, coffee provided.
Woman: Wednesday, two thirty. I'm writing it in pen this time — on paper!

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án C – Wednesday afternoon.
• Vì sao đúng: "Wednesday afternoon, two thirty, same as all quarter. Agenda by Tuesday, coffee provided".
• Monday morning sai: 9h thứ Hai là buổi họp nhanh của bộ phận sales — "That's the sales huddle, ten minutes of shouting numbers. Not ours".
• Friday afternoon sai: chỉ là tin đồn, chiều thứ Sáu nửa văn phòng đã về — "Pure legend. Half the office vanishes after Friday lunch".
👉 Mẹo: dạng hỏi lịch họp, đáp án là mốc kèm chi tiết cụ thể (giờ, agenda) và cụm "same as all quarter". Mốc bị gán "that's the...", "pure legend" là nhiễu.

questions.prompt: A man is reading the news about a housing development plan. How many new houses are going to be built?
questions.explanation:
Man: Have you seen today's paper? The housing plan is finally approved!
Woman: The famous plan! Remind me — they wanted two and a half thousand houses originally?
Man: They did, until the flood survey killed that dream. Too much wetland.
Woman: And the protest group swears only fifteen hundred will ever get built.
Man: That's their pessimism, not the document. It says here, black on white: two thousand new houses over six years.
Woman: Two thousand! With schools? A clinic?
Man: Both promised, page four. Whether promises survive construction — that's next decade's news.
Woman: Two thousand houses... our quiet street is about to get very interesting.

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án B – 2000.
• Vì sao đúng: văn bản chính thức ghi rõ — "It says here, black on white: two thousand new houses over six years".
• 2500 sai: là con số dự kiến ban đầu, bị bỏ sau khảo sát ngập lụt — "They did, until the flood survey killed that dream. Too much wetland".
• 1500 sai: là dự đoán bi quan của nhóm phản đối, không phải của văn bản — "That's their pessimism, not the document".
👉 Mẹo: dạng hỏi số liệu tin tức, tin nguồn CHÍNH THỨC ("it says here", "the document"). Số gắn với "originally", "they swear", nhóm phản đối đều bị loại.

questions.prompt: Jana is talking to her friend. What does Jana’s sister look like?
questions.explanation:
Woman: Jana! Your sister lands tomorrow, right? I'm collecting her from the airport — describe her so I don't hug a stranger!
Man: Ha! People always expect us to look alike. They think she's blonde like me — no, her hair is dark brown, almost black.
Woman: Dark hair, got it. And is she tall? You're practically a lighthouse.
Man: Everyone assumes that too! No — the height gene skipped her completely. She's short, barely reaches my shoulder, and furious about it since childhood.
Woman: Short with dark hair. Anything else?
Man: She'll be the one laughing loudest at the arrivals gate. You literally cannot miss her.
Woman: Short, dark, loud and wonderful. I'll bring the welcome sign!

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án C – Short.
• Vì sao đúng: "No — the height gene skipped her completely. She's short, barely reaches my shoulder, and furious about it since childhood".
• Blonde sai: bị bác ngay, tóc cô ấy nâu sẫm gần như đen — "They think she's blonde like me — no, her hair is dark brown, almost black".
• Tall sai: cũng bị bác, chỉ người kể mới cao — "Everyone assumes that too! No — the height gene skipped her".
👉 Mẹo: dạng tả ngoại hình, bám cấu trúc phủ định "People think... — no, actually...". Đặc điểm của NGƯỜI KỂ (blonde, tall) hay bị gán nhầm sang người được hỏi.

questions.prompt: Four people are talking about where they like to run. Match each person to the correct information.
questions.explanation:
Speaker A: Rain, snow, heatwave — none of it matters to me anymore, because my kilometres happen indoors at the sports club. The machines measure everything, the physio works two doors down, and after my knee operation last year that safety means a lot. I book the same treadmill by the window every morning at six. My running friends call indoor running fake running. I call it running that my surgeon approves of.
Speaker B: I moved to the coast three years ago, and now I cannot imagine training anywhere else. Low tide gives me two kilometres of firm, flat sand, the salt air fills my lungs, and the sound of the water sets my rhythm better than any playlist.
