Some mornings I share the beach with nobody but the gulls and one old fisherman. My city friends visit, run one sunrise with me, and start checking property prices by lunchtime.
Speaker C: Give me the pavements, the crossings, the crowds — my route cuts straight through the busiest part of town. I time my runs by the bakery smells and wave at the flower seller setting up her stall. Yes, I stop for traffic lights, and yes, the ground is hard. But a city waking up around you is the best film ever made, and I get a free showing every single morning.
Speaker D: I train with a club, and we are spoiled: our sessions happen at the athletics stadium, on the proper red surface, under the floodlights. Marked lanes, exact distances, a coach with a whistle and no mercy. Interval nights are brutal — sprint, recover, sprint again, all measured to the metre. But when race day comes, I know my pace to the second, and that certainty was built lap by counted lap.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
A = in the fitness centre (PARAPHRASE: "indoors at the sports club... treadmill"). B = at the seaside (PARAPHRASE: "the coast... firm flat sand... gulls"). C = in the street (keyword "pavements... through the busiest part of town"). D = on the running track (keyword "athletics stadium... red surface... lanes"). Nhiễu: park, forest.

questions.prompt: Art is only suitable for the privileged few
questions.explanation:
W: Did you hear? The city has allocated 150 million dollars to fund arts programmes over the next year. That brings a lot of controversy among the residents.
M: I get why it's controversial. People pay taxes expecting their quality of life to improve - better infrastructure, cheaper public transport. Tax money should go towards the public interest. Only a small handful of people can actually afford those stage productions, concerts and painting exhibitions.
W: I don't see it that way. Anyone can just buy a ticket.
M: Those venues should run like any other business - deliver good service so customers keep coming back. From what I've seen, tickets to the theater and to art exhibits are really expensive. And if they're already taking in ticket money, why does the government keep pouring more in?
W: Actually, places like museums would have to close down without funding. If anything, I'd say those figures should be higher. And with that money, kids get the chance to encounter music and art from a young age.
M: That part I agree with. I'd like my own children to come across the arts at their school. Back then, it was pretty hard for our generation to get to see a musical.
W: Future generations will definitely find it much easier to reach those things.
M: OK, let's see.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
LƯU Ý: Đây là bản MỚI theo đề thi thật 25/8 (bài quỹ 150 triệu đô cho nghệ thuật), thay bản cũ. Key chuẩn: M-W-B-W.

1. Chỉ người ĐÀN ÔNG cho rằng nghệ thuật chỉ dành cho số ít: "Only a small handful of people can actually afford those stage productions, concerts and painting exhibitions." Người phụ nữ phản đối: "I don't see it that way. Anyone can just buy a ticket."
2. Chỉ người PHỤ NỮ muốn chính phủ đầu tư thêm: "If anything, I'd say those figures should be higher." Người đàn ông ngược lại thắc mắc "why does the government keep pouring more in?"
3. CẢ HAI đồng ý trẻ em nên tiếp xúc nghệ thuật sớm. Người phụ nữ: "kids get the chance to encounter music and art from a young age." Người đàn ông: "That part I agree with. I'd like my own children to come across the arts at their school."
4. Chỉ người PHỤ NỮ tin tương lai nghệ thuật dễ tiếp cận hơn: "Future generations will definitely find it much easier to reach those things." Người đàn ông chỉ đáp "OK, let's see" — hoài nghi, không đồng tình.

questions.prompt: The government should invest more in arts
Children should be exposed to art early
In the future, art will become more accessible
What does the speaker say mostly affects concentration?
options: Concentration is primarily influenced by individual effort.
Concentration depends mainly on external distractions.
questions.explanation:
Good morning. Today's lecture is about concentration — what really controls it, and what we keep getting wrong about it. Most people believe staying focused is mainly a matter of individual effort: try harder, be more disciplined, and the focus will come. Others blame everything on external distractions — the phone, the noisy colleague, the notifications. Both ideas contain a grain of truth, but research in psychology points somewhere else. What mostly affects concentration is your environment. The lighting in your room, the level of background noise, even the way your desk is arranged — these quiet factors decide how long your attention lasts, far more than willpower does. A tired student in a calm, well-lit library will usually focus better than a determined one in a chaotic cafe. If you want to concentrate, do not fight with yourself; redesign the space around you first.
The second misunderstanding is about our limits. We live in a culture that celebrates working non-stop, and I sometimes meet people who genuinely believe they excel at managing their own attention, or who claim they always recognise when their focus is running out. The evidence says otherwise. People often fail to consider the limits of concentration at all. Attention is a finite resource, like the battery in your phone, and it drains whether you notice or not. We push through hour after hour, wondering why the work gets slower and the mistakes pile up, when the honest answer is simple: the battery is empty, and only a real break can recharge it.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
1. Đáp án: Concentration depends mostly on environment. Bẫy: "individual effort" và "external distractions" đều được nhắc rồi bị hạ ("a grain of truth, but...").
2. Đáp án: People often fail to consider the limits of concentration. Bẫy: "excel at managing" và "always recognise" là niềm tin bị bác ("The evidence says otherwise").

questions.prompt: What is it that people often don't realize about focus?
options: People frequently excel at managing the limits of concentration.
People often fail to consider the limits of concentration.
People often recognize the limits of concentration.

questions.prompt: Why is an 'important customer' valuable to a company?
options: Because they guarantee the company's stock prices will never fall.
Because they provide steady money, influence others, and help improve services.
Because they are responsible for hiring and training new employees.
questions.explanation:
In business school we talk a lot about "key accounts" — the important customers — so let me explain why they matter so much. First, let me clear away two wrong ideas. Some analysts talk as if these customers were part of the company itself, responsible for internal tasks like hiring and training new employees. They are not; they are outsiders. And no customer, however large, can guarantee that the company's stock prices will never fall — markets simply do not work that way. The real value of an important customer has three layers. They provide steady money, giving the business a reliable stream of income it can plan around. They influence others, recommending the brand to friends and partners more convincingly than any advertisement could. And through their honest feedback, they help improve services, pointing out problems before thousands of smaller customers ever meet them.
This leads to my second point: customer behaviour today is genuinely unpredictable. Tastes shift, apps change habits, and last year's bestseller gathers dust. Some managers respond by cutting the marketing budget to avoid financial risks, which only makes the company invisible. Others try to standardise every product and ignore individual preferences, hoping one size will fit everyone. It never does. The wise response is the simplest: businesses should monitor customer habits closely and update their services whenever the data shows a change. Watch what customers actually do, not what they said last year, and adjust quickly. In a market that never stands still, the companies that survive are the ones that keep moving with it.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
1. Đáp án: Because they provide steady money, influence others, and help improve services. Bẫy: "hiring and training" và "stock prices" đều bị phủ định ngay đầu.
2. Đáp án: Businesses should monitor customer habits and update their services when needed. Bẫy: "reduce the marketing budget" và "standardize all products" đều được nhắc rồi bị chê ("only makes the company invisible", "It never does").

questions.prompt: What should a business do because customer behavior is unpredictable?
options: Reduce the marketing budget to avoid financial risks.
Standardize all products to ignore individual customer preferences.
Businesses should monitor customer habits and update their services when needed.

questions.prompt: How much does a bus card cost?
questions.explanation:
Quick announcement for the new students about the bus cards, since half of you overpaid last year! The monthly student card costs twenty dollars — twenty, from the machines at the depot or the app. Not thirty, that's the adult card the driver will happily sell you if you don't show your student ID. And forget the ten-dollar rumour — that's just the weekly card, useless maths for a whole term. Twenty dollars, student card, ID in hand. Your wallets can thank me later!

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án B – $20.
• Vì sao đúng: "The monthly student card costs twenty dollars — twenty, from the machines at the depot or the app".
• $30 sai: đó là vé người lớn, tài xế sẽ bán nếu bạn không trình thẻ sinh viên — "Not thirty, that's the adult card the driver will happily sell you if you don't show your student ID".
• $10 sai: đó chỉ là vé tuần, vô dụng cho cả học kỳ — "forget the ten-dollar rumour — that's just the weekly card, useless maths for a whole term".
👉 Mẹo: dạng hỏi giá vé, mỗi con số gắn với một LOẠI vé (student / adult / weekly). Đọc kỹ câu hỏi hỏi loại nào rồi mới bắt số.

questions.prompt: How much money is left in the kitchen?
questions.explanation:
Sweetheart, mum here, listen before you raid the kitchen! About the money on the counter — your father left thirty pounds this morning, but don't get excited, that number is history. I took twenty for the pharmacy run, grandma's tablets couldn't wait. So count what remains: ten pounds, exactly ten, under the fruit bowl. That covers the bread and the milk on the list — and no, it does not cover pizza, I know how your maths works! Ten pounds, receipts please! Kisses!

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án B – 10 pounds.
• Vì sao đúng: "So count what remains: ten pounds, exactly ten, under the fruit bowl" — 30 bố để lại trừ đi 20 mẹ đã tiêu.
• 30 pounds sai: là số tiền bố để lúc sáng, nay không còn nguyên — "your father left thirty pounds this morning, but don't get excited, that number is history".
• 20 pounds sai: là phần mẹ đã lấy đi mua thuốc cho bà — "I took twenty for the pharmacy run, grandma's tablets couldn't wait".
👉 Mẹo: dạng hỏi tiền CÒN LẠI phải làm phép trừ, đừng chộp con số to nhất. Nghe cụm "what remains", "left" và câu tổng kết cuối bài.

questions.prompt: What bus number stops near the boy's home?
questions.explanation:
Your first solo trip to grandma's, big man, so let's rehearse the bus plan once more! Bus number ten stops by the school — that one goes to the stadium, wrong direction entirely, never board it. And the number nine... there IS no number nine anymore, they cancelled it last spring, ignore the old sign. Your bus is the number eight — the eight stops right near our home, by the bakery corner, every twenty minutes. Number eight, green stripe, driver called Sam. Repeat it back to me!

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án A – eight.
• Vì sao đúng: "Your bus is the number eight — the eight stops right near our home, by the bakery corner, every twenty minutes".
• ten sai: xe số 10 dừng ở trường và chạy về sân vận động, ngược hướng — "Bus number ten stops by the school — that one goes to the stadium, wrong direction entirely, never board it".
• nine sai: tuyến này đã bị hủy từ mùa xuân trước — "there IS no number nine anymore, they cancelled it last spring, ignore the old sign".
👉 Mẹo: dạng hỏi số xe buýt, bám cụm sở hữu "Your bus is". Số đi kèm "wrong direction", "cancelled", "ignore the old sign" là loại ngay.

questions.prompt: What time is dinner?
questions.explanation:
Family meeting via voicemail, everyone listen up! Tonight's dinner time has been a battlefield of opinions. Your brother wanted eight thirty after his gym — vetoed, the roast would be sad and dry by then. Grandpa lobbied for nine thirty, which is frankly a midnight snack, not dinner. The kitchen has ruled: dinner is at seven thirty! Seven thirty, table set, hands washed, phones in the basket. The roast waits for no one. Love you all, chef mum out!

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án B – 7:30 pm.
• Vì sao đúng: "The kitchen has ruled: dinner is at seven thirty! Seven thirty, table set, hands washed, phones in the basket".
• 8:30 pm sai: là đề xuất của cậu em sau buổi gym, bị bác vì món quay sẽ khô — "Your brother wanted eight thirty after his gym — vetoed, the roast would be sad and dry by then".
• 9:30 pm sai: là ý của ông, bị chê là ăn khuya chứ không phải bữa tối — "Grandpa lobbied for nine thirty, which is frankly a midnight snack, not dinner".
👉 Mẹo: dạng hỏi giờ ăn, mỗi mốc gắn với một người đề xuất. Chỉ lấy mốc do người quyết định chốt — nghe "the kitchen has ruled", "vetoed".

questions.prompt: A man has a new job. How many days does the man have to work?
questions.explanation:
Signed the contract this morning — the new job is official! And before the family panics about my health: the schedule is civilised. The old warehouse job ate five days a week plus overtime, never again. They first offered me a four-day arrangement, but that included Saturdays, so I pushed back. Final deal: three days — Monday, Wednesday, Friday, eight to four. Three days of work, four days of life! The garden, the grandkids and the fishing rod will finally see me. Retirement rehearsal, I call it!

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án A – 3 days.
• Vì sao đúng: "Final deal: three days — Monday, Wednesday, Friday, eight to four. Three days of work, four days of life!".
• 5 days sai: là lịch của công việc CŨ ở kho hàng — "The old warehouse job ate five days a week plus overtime, never again".
• 4 days sai: là đề nghị đầu tiên của công ty, anh từ chối vì có cả thứ Bảy — "They first offered me a four-day arrangement, but that included Saturdays, so I pushed back".
👉 Mẹo: dạng hỏi số ngày làm, bám cụm chốt "Final deal", "in the end". Số gắn với "the old job", "they first offered" là nhiễu.

questions.prompt: Why can't he do the job today?
questions.explanation:
Mr. Kowalski, it's Ben the handyman, about your fence today — I'm so sorry, I have to reschedule! No, I'm not sick, thank goodness, healthy as a horse, don't cancel me forever! And it's not about lunch either, I can hammer and chew at the same time, ask anyone. The real problem: the dentist finally called with a cancellation slot, and this tooth has bullied me for three weeks. My appointment is at two, right across town. Tomorrow morning, first thing, your fence gets my full attention — promise!

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án B – He has another appointment.
• Vì sao đúng: anh phải đi khám răng đúng giờ làm — "the dentist finally called with a cancellation slot, and this tooth has bullied me for three weeks. My appointment is at two, right across town".
• He sicks sai: anh khẳng định vẫn khỏe — "No, I'm not sick, thank goodness, healthy as a horse".
• He has to eat sai: bị gạt thẳng, anh vừa làm vừa ăn được — "it's not about lunch either, I can hammer and chew at the same time".
👉 Mẹo: dạng hỏi lý do hoãn/hủy, người nói loại 2 lý do trước rồi mới nói thật. Bám cụm "The real problem:" và danh từ chỉ lịch hẹn (appointment, slot).

questions.prompt: What is the man going to do?
questions.explanation:
What a marathon of a day — three meetings, zero breaks, and my stomach has filed a formal complaint! The sofa is calling for a nap, I know, but if I sleep now I'll be awake at three in the morning, no thank you. And I did think about just pouring a big cold drink first... but honestly, liquid won't silence this hunger. No — straight to the kitchen, I'm getting something to eat. There's leftover noodles with my name on them. Food first, world later!

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án A – Get something to eat.
• Vì sao đúng: "straight to the kitchen, I'm getting something to eat. There's leftover noodles with my name on them. Food first, world later!".
• Go to sleep sai: bị gạt vì ngủ giờ này sẽ tỉnh lúc 3h sáng — "if I sleep now I'll be awake at three in the morning, no thank you".
• Get something to drink sai: có nghĩ tới nhưng không giải quyết được cơn đói — "I did think about just pouring a big cold drink first... but honestly, liquid won't silence this hunger".
👉 Mẹo: dạng "What is he going to do?", bám thì hiện tại tiếp diễn chỉ tương lai gần ("I'm getting..."). Ý đi kèm "I did think about... but" là bị loại.

questions.prompt: What is the new health center next to?
questions.explanation:
Residents, quick update from the town council newsletter — the new health centre location is confirmed! I know the early plans put it beside the airport, but the noise studies buried that idea fast, imagine hearing jets during a check-up! Others swore it would rise next to the bus station downtown — wrong again, that plot stays a car park. The final decision: the health centre will stand right next to the train station. Perfect for commuters, five minutes from every platform. Construction starts in spring!

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án B – A train station.
• Vì sao đúng: "The final decision: the health centre will stand right next to the train station. Perfect for commuters, five minutes from every platform".
• A bus station sai: chỉ là tin đồn, khu đất đó vẫn để làm bãi đỗ xe — "Others swore it would rise next to the bus station downtown — wrong again, that plot stays a car park".
• An airport sai: là kế hoạch ban đầu, bị bỏ vì tiếng ồn máy bay — "the early plans put it beside the airport, but the noise studies buried that idea fast".
👉 Mẹo: dạng thông báo địa điểm, bám cụm "The final decision". Nơi đi kèm "the early plans", "others swore", "wrong again" đều bị loại.

questions.prompt: In which room will the director's presentation happen?
questions.explanation:
Team, logistics for the director's big presentation tomorrow, please read twice! The living room of the guest house — where we did last year's — is being repainted, fumes included, so that's out. And someone booked the small bedroom upstairs as an option; a presentation among pillows, imagine the photos! No. The director will present in the meeting room, main building, second door — projector installed, twenty chairs, coffee station ready. The meeting room at nine sharp. Dress accordingly!

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án B – The meeting room.
• Vì sao đúng: "The director will present in the meeting room, main building, second door — projector installed, twenty chairs, coffee station ready".
• The living room sai: đang sơn lại, còn nồng mùi sơn — "The living room of the guest house — where we did last year's — is being repainted, fumes included, so that's out".
• The bedroom sai: có người đặt nhưng bị bác thẳng — "someone booked the small bedroom upstairs as an option; a presentation among pillows, imagine the photos! No".
👉 Mẹo: dạng hỏi phòng, chọn nơi được tả kèm TRANG THIẾT BỊ phù hợp (projector, chairs). Nơi đi kèm "so that's out", "No" là loại.

questions.prompt: What time do they arrange the meeting?
questions.explanation:
Woman: About tomorrow's project review — I need to lock the time before I book the room.
Man: Right. My notes say three thirty?
Woman: That was the first suggestion, but the finance call runs till four, we'd be walking in mid-sentence.
Man: Then four thirty? Clean gap after the call...
Woman: Almost — but the director joins us, and his train only lands at five.
Man: So five thirty it is? Last slot before the building empties.
Woman: Five thirty, small conference room, one focused hour. I'll send the invite tonight.
Man: Five thirty confirmed. I'll bring the numbers and the biscuits!

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án C – 5:30 pm.
• Vì sao đúng: "Five thirty, small conference room, one focused hour. I'll send the invite tonight" — và "Five thirty confirmed".
• 3:30 pm sai: là đề xuất đầu tiên, vướng cuộc gọi tài chính kéo dài tới 4h — "That was the first suggestion, but the finance call runs till four".
• 4:30 pm sai: bị loại vì tàu của giám đốc 5h mới tới — "the director joins us, and his train only lands at five".
👉 Mẹo: dạng chốt giờ họp, các mốc tăng dần và mốc nào cũng vướng một trở ngại. Lấy mốc cuối đi kèm "confirmed", "I'll send the invite".

questions.prompt: What time does the party start?
questions.explanation:
Man: Little sister! Your graduation party Saturday — when do the doors actually open?
Woman: Finally someone asks! Mum keeps telling everyone four o'clock, which was the OLD plan.
Man: So not four. Auntie swears she heard five?
Woman: Auntie hears what suits her nap schedule! Five is when we cut the cake — arriving then means missing everything.
Man: So the real start is...?
Woman: Three o'clock! Three sharp — speeches at half past, cake at five, dancing till they throw us out.
Man: Three o'clock, got it. I'll come at two to help with chairs — and to guard the cake from Auntie.
Woman: My hero! Bring the good camera!

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án C – 3 o'clock.
• Vì sao đúng: "Three o'clock! Three sharp — speeches at half past, cake at five, dancing till they throw us out".
• 4 o'clock sai: là kế hoạch CŨ mà mẹ vẫn báo nhầm cho mọi người — "Mum keeps telling everyone four o'clock, which was the OLD plan".
• 5 o'clock sai: đó là giờ cắt bánh, đến lúc đó là lỡ gần hết — "Five is when we cut the cake — arriving then means missing everything".
👉 Mẹo: câu hỏi "What time does the party START?" — cẩn thận giờ của một MỤC trong chương trình (cắt bánh, phát biểu). Bám từ "sharp", "the real start".

questions.prompt: On which floor is the French class?
questions.explanation:
Man: Excuse me, I'm here for the French class — the evening course? This building is a maze!
Woman: You're not the first lost linguist tonight! Which floor did they tell you?
Man: The first floor, I thought — but that's clearly the gym, unless French involves treadmills now.
Woman: Ha! No, the first floor schedule changed last month. And don't try the third — that's Spanish tonight, you'd leave with the wrong language entirely!
Man: So French is...?
Woman: Second floor, room 204, the door with the little Eiffel Tower poster. Monsieur Girard, he starts precisely on time.
Man: Second floor, 204, running now — merci!
Woman: Bonne chance! The stairs are faster than the lift!

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án C – Second.
• Vì sao đúng: "Second floor, room 204, the door with the little Eiffel Tower poster. Monsieur Girard, he starts precisely on time".
• First sai: tầng một là phòng gym, lịch đã đổi từ tháng trước — "that's clearly the gym"; "the first floor schedule changed last month".
• Third sai: tối nay tầng ba là lớp tiếng Tây Ban Nha — "don't try the third — that's Spanish tonight, you'd leave with the wrong language entirely!".
👉 Mẹo: dạng hỏi tầng/phòng, đáp án luôn kèm dấu hiệu nhận diện cụ thể (room 204, poster). Tầng gắn với môn hay hoạt động khác là nhiễu.

questions.prompt: Where is she taking the staff to?
questions.explanation:
Man: I heard the boss is planning the annual staff trip! Any inside news?
Woman: Fresh from this morning's briefing! And it's bigger than the rumours.
Man: Bigger than the mountain village they mentioned in spring? The quiet cabins?
Woman: The village idea died — too small for forty people, only one restaurant.
Man: So the backup — that city break? Museums, hotels, the usual?
Woman: Also cancelled! Too similar to last year, people groaned. No — she's taking us to a different country! Portugal, four days, flights included!
Man: A different COUNTRY? Our boss has upgraded dramatically!
Woman: Passports ready by October. Start practising your obrigado!

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án A – To a different country.
• Vì sao đúng: "she's taking us to a different country! Portugal, four days, flights included!" — và "Passports ready by October".
• To a village sai: ý làng miền núi đã bị bỏ vì quá nhỏ cho 40 người — "The village idea died — too small for forty people, only one restaurant".
• To a different city sai: phương án dự phòng cũng bị hủy vì trùng kiểu năm ngoái — "Also cancelled! Too similar to last year, people groaned".
👉 Mẹo: dạng hỏi điểm đến, nghe cụm đảo hướng "No — she's taking us to...". Nơi đi kèm "died", "cancelled" thì gạch; tên riêng (Portugal) là bằng chứng chốt.

questions.prompt: Four people are talking about doing exercise. Match each person to the correct information.
questions.explanation:
Speaker A: Let me be the villain of this recording: sport and I are enemies, and we always have been. School athletics scarred me for life — the whistle, the shouting, the cold mud. As an adult I have politely tried yoga, tennis and one horrifying spinning class, and I walked out of each one certain of my truth. Some people were built to move; I was built to sit in a warm café watching them through the window.
Speaker B: I never cared about sport until my job nearly broke me. Endless reports, afternoon headaches, a brain like wet paper by Thursday. My doctor prescribed movement instead of pills, and the change shocked me: three morning swims a week, and suddenly my reports finish before lunch and my ideas queue up politely instead of hiding. My manager keeps asking what changed. The swimming pool changed, I tell her — everything else followed.
Speaker C: I admire people who bounce out of the gym glowing. My experience is the opposite: halfway through any session, my arms resign, my legs file complaints, and the last ten minutes happen in slow motion. Afterwards I do not glow — I collapse. Friends insist that one day the heaviness turns into energy. I have given it two years; the heaviness has only learned my name.
Speaker D: For me the magic ingredient is company. Saturday football with my old classmates, evening badminton with the people from my building — we play badly and laugh loudly, and that is exactly the point. Once, when everyone was away, I tried exercising by myself and quit in fifteen minutes from pure boredom. Put my friends on the court, though, and I will happily chase a ball until midnight.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
A = hate exercising (PARAPHRASE: "sport and I are enemies... walked out certain of my truth"). B = help improve work performance (PARAPHRASE: "reports finish before lunch... ideas queue up"). C = find exercise tiring (keyword-lite "heaviness... collapse... slow motion"). D = has fun when exercising with friends (keyword "with my old classmates... laugh loudly"). Nhiễu: lose weight, alone.

questions.prompt: Children are interested in tech-based learning
questions.explanation:
W: How are your two getting on with that new tablet scheme at the school?
M: Rather well, actually, which honestly surprised me.
W: Same here. Put a lesson on a screen and they're suddenly wide awake — anything with an app or a game inside it and they'll happily sit there for an hour.
M: Exactly, I agree completely. My son will do twenty minutes of maths on a tablet without a murmur, then sulk for an hour over a paper worksheet.
W: It's the same story in every house I know.
M: What does worry me, though, is what happens the moment you take the screen away. A lot of them genuinely struggle to hold an ordinary conversation face to face.
W: Oh, I'm entirely with you there. My niece will type all evening quite happily, but ask her to order her own lunch in a café and she goes to pieces.
M: It's a proper skill, and they're simply not practising it any more.
W: Which is precisely why I think households need proper support with all this. Parents are left to work out the rules on their own, and most of them haven't the faintest idea where to start.
M: Hmm, I don't see it that way, to be honest. I'll accept that some parents find it hard going, but it isn't complicated — you set a time limit and you stick to it. You hardly need somebody coming round to explain that.
W: That's easy to say when you've only got the one at home.
M: Possibly. What I would say, though, is that children can be taught to manage their own behaviour online — to work out for themselves what's sensible and step away from it.
W: I'm not so sure about that at all. They're not old enough to see the harm coming, and every app has been designed by grown-ups to keep them hooked. That's hardly a fair fight.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
Key: Trẻ hứng thú với học qua công nghệ = Both · Trẻ khó giao tiếp ngoài đời = Both · Gia đình cần hỗ trợ quản lý công nghệ = Woman · Trẻ có thể tự điều chỉnh tương tác trực tuyến = Man

1. Children are interested in tech-based learning → Both: người phụ nữ nêu "Put a lesson on a screen and they're suddenly wide awake", người đàn ông tán thành rõ ràng: "Exactly, I agree completely."

2. Children find it difficult to communicate offline → Both: người đàn ông nêu "A lot of them genuinely struggle to hold an ordinary conversation face to face", người phụ nữ đồng ý: "Oh, I'm entirely with you there."

3. Families require help with management of technology → Woman: người phụ nữ nêu "households need proper support with all this". Người đàn ông phản đối: "Hmm, I don't see it that way, to be honest."

4. Children can learn to regulate their online interactions → Man: người đàn ông nêu "children can be taught to manage their own behaviour online". Người phụ nữ phản đối: "I'm not so sure about that at all."

👉 Mẹo: Bẫy chính ở ý 3 — người đàn ông mở đầu bằng "I'll accept that some parents find it hard going" nghe rất giống đồng ý, nhưng phần sau ("it isn't complicated") phủ nhận đúng việc gia đình cần được hỗ trợ, nên đáp án là Woman.

questions.prompt: Children find it difficult to communicate offline
Families require help with management of technology
Children can learn to regulate their online interactions
What occurs when things don't go according to plan in a team?
options: The team members become more assured.
The team members start again from the beginning.
questions.explanation:
Before I became a business coach, I spent ten years leading software teams, and tonight I want to share the most important lesson from those years: what really happens when a project goes wrong. Picture the scene — the deadline arrives, the product is not ready, the client is unhappy. What do the team members do next? The comfortable answer is that they calmly return to the beginning and start the plan again, like scientists repeating an experiment. An even more comfortable answer is that failure makes a strong team more assured, more determined than before. I have watched this moment dozens of times, and I can tell you what actually happens: the team members lose confidence. Quietly, one by one, people start wondering whether they are good enough. Meetings become careful, ideas dry up, and the next piece of work takes twice as long — not because the task is harder, but because the belief is gone.
A leader's job in that moment is to rebuild belief, and there are two popular shortcuts that do not work. Pouring extra money in — increasing the project budget significantly — changes nothing about how people feel. And focusing on individual performance only, measuring each person against the others, just adds fear to the disappointment. What works is almost embarrassingly simple: set a realistic goal. Give the team a target they can genuinely reach this week, then another next week. Every small success returns a piece of the confidence that failure took away, and step by step, the team learns to trust itself again.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
(Bản variant của Đề 09 bài 2 — cùng câu hỏi và đáp án, lời khác để hai đề không trùng script.)
1. Đáp án: The team members lose confidence. Bẫy: "start again from the beginning" và "become more assured" đều là "câu trả lời dễ chịu" bị bác bằng trải nghiệm thực.
2. Đáp án: Set a realistic goal. Bẫy: "increase the project budget" và "focus on individual performance only" là hai lối tắt "do not work".

questions.prompt: In the speaker's view, what helps a leader maintain team motivation?
Why does the brother find traveling meaningful?
options: Because it allows him to escape his professional responsibilities.
Because he wants to document his trips for social media influence.
Because it brings him joy and chances to learn about different cultures.
questions.explanation:
People at work keep asking about my brother, the one who is always at an airport somewhere. And I have heard every theory about why he travels so much. His manager is convinced it is escape — that he books flights to run away from his professional responsibilities. My aunt is equally sure it is all for social media, that he wants dramatic photos to impress strangers online. I find both theories funny, because his accounts have been silent for two years, and he actually clears his work completely before every trip precisely so that nothing follows him. The real reason is the one nobody guesses because it is so ordinary: travelling makes him genuinely happy, and it gives him chances to learn about different cultures. He learns ten phrases of every language, eats where the locals eat, and comes home with stories instead of souvenirs.
Here is the funny thing — I never travel, yet I understand him perfectly, because what he does with a backpack, I do with books. People sometimes assume reading and travelling belong together because both are somehow mandatory for success at school. They are not; nobody grades you on either. And clearly neither depends on physical endurance — one of us climbs mountains while the other sits in an armchair. What truly makes them similar is this: both help a person discover new worlds and grow. His borders are on maps and mine are on pages, but we cross them for exactly the same reason.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
(Bản variant của Đề 10 bài 1 — cùng câu hỏi và đáp án, lời khác để hai đề không trùng script.)
1. Đáp án: Because it brings him joy and chances to learn about different cultures. Bẫy: "escape responsibilities" (thuyết của manager) và "social media" (thuyết của bà cô) đều bị bác.
2. Đáp án: Both help people discover new worlds and grow as a person. Bẫy: "mandatory for academic success" và "physical endurance" đều bị phủ định.

questions.prompt: How is traveling similar to reading a book?
options: Both are considered mandatory activities for academic success.
Both help people discover new worlds and grow as a person.
Both require a high level of physical endurance and preparation.

questions.prompt: What is she going to take with her?
questions.explanation:
Hi Laura, it's me! I'm almost finished packing for the weekend at the lake house. I thought about bringing some books, but honestly, the bag is heavy enough already and I never open them anyway. And don't worry about food — Auntie says the kitchen there is full, so we don't need to carry anything to eat. What I AM going to take is the games — the cards and the big box of board games. Rainy evenings at the lake need games! See you at seven!

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án A – games.
• Vì sao đúng: "What I AM going to take is the games — the cards and the big box of board games. Rainy evenings at the lake need games!".
• books sai: cô nghĩ tới rồi bỏ vì túi đã quá nặng — "I thought about bringing some books, but honestly, the bag is heavy enough already and I never open them anyway".
• food sai: không cần mang vì bếp ở nhà hồ đã đầy đồ — "Auntie says the kitchen there is full, so we don't need to carry anything to eat".
👉 Mẹo: dạng hỏi "mang theo gì", bám câu nhấn mạnh "What I AM going to take is...". Món đi kèm "I thought about... but" hay "we don't need to" là loại.

questions.prompt: What will the student write about?
questions.explanation:
Good afternoon, Mrs. Reed, this is Daniel from your Tuesday class. You asked me to tell you my topic for the project before Friday, so here it is. I've decided to write about the land — how the fields and farmland around our town have changed over the last fifty years. My grandfather still has old photos of the area, so I have plenty of material to work with. I hope that's suitable. I'll bring my plan to the next lesson. Thank you very much!

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án A – land.
• Vì sao đúng: "I've decided to write about the land — how the fields and farmland around our town have changed over the last fifty years".
• bikes sai: không được nhắc tới trong bài, chỉ là phương án gây nhiễu.
• animals sai: không được nhắc tới trong bài, chỉ là phương án gây nhiễu.
👉 Mẹo: bài không cài bẫy thì chỉ cần bắt đúng cụm "I've decided to write about..." — danh từ ngay sau "about" chính là đáp án.

questions.prompt: What does the teacher want the student to do?
questions.explanation:
Hello Tom, this is Mr. Harris calling about your schoolwork this term. Your marks in the tests are actually fine, so this is not about studying harder. The problem is different: three of your assignments arrived late, and one is still missing. From now on, I want you to complete every assignment on time — that is the one thing I'm asking. Hand them in on the day they are due, and everything else will take care of itself. See you on Monday.

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án A – Complete the assignments on time.
• Vì sao đúng: "From now on, I want you to complete every assignment on time — that is the one thing I'm asking. Hand them in on the day they are due".
• Study harder sai: bị loại thẳng vì điểm kiểm tra đã ổn — "Your marks in the tests are actually fine, so this is not about studying harder".
• Rest sai: không được nhắc tới trong bài, chỉ là phương án gây nhiễu.
👉 Mẹo: dạng "thầy muốn học sinh làm gì", bám cụm "I want you to..." và "the one thing I'm asking". Ý đi sau "this is not about..." thì gạch.

questions.prompt: What do the students need to do every Tuesday?
questions.explanation:
Good morning, everyone, before you open your textbooks — one new rule for this term. Every Tuesday, each of you will write a report about the experiment we did that week. One page is enough: what you did, what you observed, and what you learned. You will hand it to me at the start of Wednesday's lesson. This is every single Tuesday, so put it in your diaries now. The reports will count towards your final mark, so please take them seriously.

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án B – write a report.
• Vì sao đúng: "Every Tuesday, each of you will write a report about the experiment we did that week. One page is enough".
• write a note sai: bài chỉ nói "report", hoàn toàn không nhắc tới việc viết note — đây là nhiễu bằng từ gần nghĩa.
• go camping sai: không được nhắc tới trong bài, chỉ là phương án gây nhiễu.
👉 Mẹo: dạng thông báo nhiệm vụ định kỳ, khoanh cụm "Every + thứ trong tuần" rồi bắt đúng ĐỘNG TỪ + DANH TỪ ngay sau đó (write a report), đừng đoán theo từ na ná.

questions.prompt: Listen to the radio program about a new restaurant. What does the man complain about?
questions.explanation:
And now our weekly restaurant review! Our reporter visited the new grill house on Station Road last night. The food? Excellent — he says the steak was the best he's had all year, and the prices were fair too. But there was one serious problem: the temperature. The heating was broken, the big windows let in every draught, and he sat through dinner in his coat and scarf. The place was freezing cold from starter to dessert. Fix the heating, he says — and he'll happily come back!

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án A – the place was cold.
• Vì sao đúng: "The heating was broken, the big windows let in every draught, and he sat through dinner in his coat and scarf. The place was freezing cold from starter to dessert".
• the place was hot sai: ngược hẳn với bài — hệ thống sưởi hỏng nên quán lạnh cóng, khách phải mặc áo khoác quàng khăn ăn tối.
• the place was ugly sai: không được nhắc tới trong bài, chỉ là phương án gây nhiễu; bài chỉ khen đồ ăn và giá — "the steak was the best he's had all year, and the prices were fair too".
👉 Mẹo: dạng hỏi "phàn nàn điều gì", bỏ qua mọi thứ được KHEN ở đầu bài và bám cụm đảo hướng "But there was one serious problem".

questions.prompt: Listen to a writer talking about her job. What is her first job?
questions.explanation:
People often think I've been writing all my life, but my road here was longer than that. After university, my first job was actually as a teacher — I taught English to teenagers for six years, and I loved reading stories aloud to my classes. Later I worked in the town library for a while, surrounded by other people's books, and that's when I started writing my own. My first novel came out ten years ago, and I've been a full-time writer ever since.

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án C – Teacher.
• Vì sao đúng: "After university, my first job was actually as a teacher — I taught English to teenagers for six years".
• Librarian sai: đó là công việc SAU đó — "Later I worked in the town library for a while, surrounded by other people's books".
• Writer sai: là nghề hiện tại, đến sau cùng — "My first novel came out ten years ago, and I've been a full-time writer ever since".
👉 Mẹo: câu hỏi "her FIRST job" là hỏi trình tự thời gian. Vẽ nhanh trục khi nghe: "After university / my first job" → "Later" → "ever since".

questions.prompt: Vincent is calling James. Why does Vincent call James?
questions.explanation:
James, it's Vincent! Don't panic, I'm not calling to ask for help with moving the furniture again — that's all done, my back survived. And before you ask, no, this is not about Sarah's party either, I know you already said you can't come to that. This is much simpler: it's been months since we properly talked, so how about a drink on Thursday evening? The little place near the bridge, seven o'clock, first round on me. Call me back!

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án B – Suggest a drink.
• Vì sao đúng: "This is much simpler: it's been months since we properly talked, so how about a drink on Thursday evening? The little place near the bridge, seven o'clock".
• Ask for help sai: bị phủ định ngay đầu, việc chuyển đồ đã xong — "I'm not calling to ask for help with moving the furniture again — that's all done".
• Invite him to a party sai: cũng bị loại vì James đã từ chối tiệc của Sarah — "this is not about Sarah's party either, I know you already said you can't come to that".
👉 Mẹo: dạng hỏi mục đích cuộc gọi, người gọi hay loại trừ 2 khả năng trước. Đáp án nằm ngay sau "This is much simpler:" hoặc "The real reason I'm calling".

questions.prompt: Anna is calling her brother Max. What does Anna do later in the afternoon?
questions.explanation:
Max, it's Anna. Small change of plan for today, so listen carefully. The big project is due tomorrow morning, and my part isn't finished, so this afternoon I'll be staying late at the office — probably until eight or nine. That means I can't do the school run, so could you collect the kids at four? Their bags are already packed, and dinner is in the fridge. I'll make it up to you at the weekend, I promise. You're the best, thank you!

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án B – Stay late at the office.
• Vì sao đúng: "The big project is due tomorrow morning, and my part isn't finished, so this afternoon I'll be staying late at the office — probably until eight or nine".
• Pick up the kids sai: đó là việc cô NHỜ Max làm, không phải việc của Anna — "I can't do the school run, so could you collect the kids at four?".
• Hang out with friends sai: không được nhắc tới trong bài, chỉ là phương án gây nhiễu.
👉 Mẹo: dạng hỏi "AI làm gì", tách rõ chủ ngữ. Việc đi sau "could you...?" là việc của người NGHE, không phải người nói.

questions.prompt: A woman is talking about her favorite film on the radio. What film did she recommend?
questions.explanation:
Welcome back to Film Corner! A listener asked me what to watch this weekend, and here is my honest answer. Everyone keeps talking about that new romantic film by the sea — I found it slow, and I nearly fell asleep. The comedy that opened last week? A few good jokes, but you'll forget it by Monday. No — the one I really recommend is the action film about the mountain rescue team. Two hours, my heart never stopped racing. Don't miss it!

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án A – Action film.
• Vì sao đúng: "the one I really recommend is the action film about the mountain rescue team. Two hours, my heart never stopped racing. Don't miss it!".
• Romantic film sai: bị chê chậm, xem suýt ngủ gật — "I found it slow, and I nearly fell asleep".
• Comedy film sai: chỉ được vài câu đùa rồi quên ngay — "A few good jokes, but you'll forget it by Monday".
👉 Mẹo: dạng hỏi "giới thiệu phim nào", bám đúng động từ "recommend". Phim gắn với "slow", "you'll forget it" là nhiễu dù được nhắc trước.

questions.prompt: What do they decide to write about?
questions.explanation:
M: So, the history essay — we still haven't picked a person to write about. Any ideas?
W: I was thinking about a politician at first. There's plenty of material about their speeches and elections.
M: Mmm, honestly, politics bores me. And half the class will choose a politician anyway.
W: True. What about someone from economics, then? A famous banker, maybe?
M: That sounds even drier, all those numbers... Wait — what about a historian? Someone who wrote about the past themselves?
W: Oh, that's clever! We'd be writing history about a historian. The professor will love that.
M: Exactly. Let's decide on the historian, then. I'll find the books tonight.
W: Deal. I'll start on the introduction tomorrow.

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án B – historian.
• Vì sao đúng: "Wait — what about a historian? Someone who wrote about the past themselves?" và chốt "Let's decide on the historian, then" — cô đồng ý "Deal".
• politic sai: bị loại vì chán và cả nửa lớp cũng chọn — "politics bores me. And half the class will choose a politician anyway".
• economy sai: bị chê còn khô khan hơn — "That sounds even drier, all those numbers...".
👉 Mẹo: dạng hai người chọn đề tài, đáp án là ý nêu SAU CÙNG kèm câu đồng thuận ("Let's decide on...", "Deal").

questions.prompt: Listen to Marry talking to Jane while waiting for James. What did they decide to do?
questions.explanation:
W1: Jane, it's already twenty past. Any message from James?
W2: Nothing, Marry. His phone just rings and rings. Should we cancel the whole meeting?
W1: Cancelling seems a waste — everyone else is here, and the room is only ours until twelve.
W2: We could wait another ten minutes, I suppose. He might just be stuck in traffic.
W1: We've waited long enough, honestly. And the first two points on the agenda don't even involve him.
W2: That's true. He can read the notes afterwards for the parts he missed.
W1: Right, decision made — we'll have the meeting without him. Can you close the door?
W2: Done. Okay, everyone, let's begin with point one.

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án B – Having the meeting without him.
• Vì sao đúng: "Right, decision made — we'll have the meeting without him. Can you close the door?".
• Cancel the meeting sai: bị gạt vì mọi người đã có mặt và phòng chỉ đặt tới 12h — "Cancelling seems a waste — everyone else is here, and the room is only ours until twelve".
• Wait for him longer sai: có đề xuất chờ thêm mười phút nhưng bị bác — "We've waited long enough, honestly".
👉 Mẹo: dạng "họ quyết định làm gì", bám cụm "decision made". Ý đi kèm "seems a waste", "we've waited long enough" là ý bị loại.

questions.prompt: A woman is talking to her coworker. When does the meeting start?
questions.explanation:
W: Morning, Paul! Quick question — the team meeting today, is it still at half past ten?
M: Ah, you haven't seen the email? It changed this morning.
W: Again? Last month they even tried to put it at quarter to ten, which was impossible with the school run.
M: I remember. No, this time it moved the other way — the boss has a call at ten thirty now.
W: So when do we actually start?
M: Quarter past ten. Ten fifteen sharp, same room as always.
W: Ten fifteen... that's fine, I can make that easily.
M: Bring your report — you're second on the agenda!

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án A – 10.15.
• Vì sao đúng: "Quarter past ten. Ten fifteen sharp, same room as always".
• 10.30 sai: là giờ CŨ, đã đổi vì sếp có cuộc gọi đúng lúc đó — "the boss has a call at ten thirty now".
• 9.45 sai: là lần đổi giờ của tháng trước, bất khả thi vì còn phải đưa con đi học — "Last month they even tried to put it at quarter to ten, which was impossible with the school run".
👉 Mẹo: dạng hỏi giờ họp, phải quy đổi cách nói giờ: "quarter past ten" = 10.15, còn "quarter to ten" = 9.45. Nghe nhầm past/to là mất điểm ngay.

questions.prompt: Samia is going to meet her friend. What time are they going to meet?
questions.explanation:
M: Samia! Are we still on for coffee tomorrow?
W: Of course! I was going to suggest half past nine, right when the café opens.
M: Ooh, that's early for a Saturday... I only get back from the gym around then.
W: Fair enough. Then how about eleven? The morning rush is over by then.
M: Eleven is a bit late, though — I promised Mum I'd drive her to the market at midday.
W: Okay, let's meet in the middle. Ten o'clock?
M: Ten is perfect. That gives us a whole two hours.
W: Ten it is, then. The usual table by the window!

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án C – 10:00.
• Vì sao đúng: "Okay, let's meet in the middle. Ten o'clock?" — "Ten is perfect. That gives us a whole two hours" và chốt "Ten it is, then".
• 9:30 sai: quá sớm cho thứ Bảy, lúc đó anh mới từ phòng gym về — "that's early for a Saturday... I only get back from the gym around then".
• 11:00 sai: hơi muộn vì trưa anh phải chở mẹ đi chợ — "Eleven is a bit late, though — I promised Mum I'd drive her to the market at midday".
👉 Mẹo: một người đưa giờ sớm, người kia chê muộn thì đáp án gần như luôn là mốc GIỮA. Bắt cụm "let's meet in the middle".

questions.prompt: Four people are talking about their studying habits. Match each person to the correct information.
questions.explanation:
Speaker A: The house is chaos until about ten — children, dishes, doorbells. So my textbooks wait, and they know they will get me when everyone else has surrendered to sleep. Between eleven and two, the flat is mine: no interruptions, no noise, just the desk lamp and my notes. My friends call those hours unnatural. I call them the only hours the world agrees to leave me alone, and my best marks were all born in them.
Speaker B: Ask my friends where I revise and they will laugh: everywhere. The train into college, the bench outside the sports hall, my aunt's kitchen, the launderette while my clothes spin. I have finished essays in waiting rooms and memorised vocabulary in a queue. One fixed desk makes my mind stiff; carrying my notes through the day keeps them alive. My record is studying in six locations before dinner — and remembering every page of it.
Speaker C: My secret weapon has wires: nothing enters my head without a soundtrack. Gentle jazz for heavy reading, film scores for essays, and one particular symphony that has carried me through every exam since I was sixteen. The melodies build a wall between me and the world, and inside that wall everything sticks. Silence, strangely, is what distracts me — my thoughts scatter without a rhythm to hold them in line.
Speaker D: I have one requirement, and it is absolute: no sound. I revise in the reading room where even a cough draws stares, or at home with everyone out and the windows shut. One barking dog can cost me a whole paragraph. My sister studies happily in noisy cafés and I genuinely do not understand how. For my brain, stillness is not a preference — it is the on switch.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
A = study late at night (PARAPHRASE: "between eleven and two... hours the world leaves me alone"). B = at various places (PARAPHRASE: "everywhere... six locations before dinner"). C = with music (keyword "soundtrack... melodies"). D = in a quiet place (keyword-lite "no sound... stillness"). Nhiễu: in a group, early morning.

questions.prompt: Media exaggerates the benefits of the programme
questions.explanation:
M: There have been so many volunteer events recently that it's almost impossible not to talk about them on my podcast.
W: Fair enough.
M: First of all, these volunteer groups have become incredibly popular — the media everywhere is covering them. But honestly, I think what these events actually achieve is being blown out of proportion.
W: I agree with you there. The press keeps saying these groups are going to change the whole world and fix the environment, when in fact they only deal with a tiny part of the problem. There are plenty of other issues going on.
M: Like littering — for me that's one of the biggest problems in society today. People assume dropping one wrapper has a tiny effect, but it all adds up until it becomes a huge issue.
W: Hmm, I'm not sure it's as serious as you make out — there are far bigger things to worry about. But let's leave that to one side. What I want to say is that these volunteers are getting a lot of publicity — interviews, posts, articles — and I think that's a good thing. Whether they do it for fame, for personal reasons or for the community, it makes no difference to the result: it still draws more people into volunteering.
M: I don't see it that way. If people who volunteer for their own benefit get all that publicity, it doesn't just attract more volunteers — it can backfire. You end up with people volunteering to boost their ego rather than to help the community, and that does change what the programme achieves.
W: OK, let's go back to the litter problem, since you feel so strongly about it. What do you think should be done?
M: The best approach is to introduce penalties. Other countries have very tough punishments — heavy fines, even prison — and the figures show those countries have far lower rates of littering.
W: I'll accept the figures, but I don't think punishment is the most appropriate answer here. A fine changes behaviour for a week and then people forget. What actually works is education and making it easy to do the right thing — more bins, clearer signs, campaigns in schools. Change the habit, not just the price of breaking it.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
Key theo đề thật 16/9: Media exaggerates = Both · Littering main problem = Man · Volunteers' motivations don't affect the outcome = Woman · Punishment most effective = Man.
1. Media exaggerates the benefits → Both: anh nói "blown out of proportion", cô "I agree with you there".
2. Littering is a major problem → The man: "one of the biggest problems in society today". Cô không đồng ý: "I'm not sure it's as serious as you make out".
3. Motivations do not affect the outcome → The woman: "Whether they do it for fame, for personal reasons or for the community, it makes no difference to the result". Anh phản bác: "it can backfire... that does change what the programme achieves".
4. Punishment is the most effective way → The man: "The best approach is to introduce penalties". Cô: "I don't think punishment is the most appropriate answer".
👉 Mẹo: câu 2 và 3 là bẫy — người nói đồng ý với SỐ LIỆU nhưng không đồng ý với KẾT LUẬN thì vẫn không phải Both.

questions.prompt: Littering will always be a problem
Punishment is the most effective way to prevent littering
The volunteers' motivations do not affect the programme outcome
When did she become a Nutritionist?
options: When she did a biology degree.
When she worked at a healthcare center.
questions.explanation:
People often ask how I became a nutritionist, and my path was a little unusual. Most of my colleagues found this profession later in life — some decided to specialise after working in a hospital, where they saw every day how much food affects recovery, and others made the choice while employed at a local healthcare centre. My story is different. I qualified as a nutritionist while I was still completing my biology degree at university. During my second year, a professor invited me to join a research project on diet and energy, and I knew immediately that this was my field. So by the time I graduated, I already held my professional qualification — the degree and the career began together.
How I became well known is another story people usually get wrong. Some assume I appeared on a famous TV talk show, and others have heard a rumour that I invented some revolutionary new health food. Neither happened — I have never been on television, and I have never invented anything. The truth is quieter. For six years I answered calls on a national nutrition helpline, three evenings a week. I helped thousands of ordinary people solve their problems: a mother whose son refused vegetables, an athlete who kept feeling weak, an older man confused about his diabetes diet. Those callers told their friends, the friends told their doctors, and slowly my name spread. I became known not through cameras or products, but through years of solving one small problem at a time.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
1. Đáp án: When she did a biology degree. Bẫy: "hospital" và "healthcare center" là con đường của ĐỒNG NGHIỆP ("Most of my colleagues...").
2. Đáp án: After solving people's problems in a helpline. Bẫy: "TV show" và "inventing a new food" đều bị phủ định ("Neither happened").

questions.prompt: When did she become famous?
options: After solving people's problems in a helpline.
After appearing on a famous TV show.
After inventing a new type of food.

questions.prompt: What makes the video stand out from others?
questions.explanation:
The sudden success of this short video has puzzled a lot of marketing experts, so let me break it down. When something gets thirty million views, people jump to the usual explanations. Some assume famous celebrities must have taken part — but watch it yourself: every face in the video is an unknown amateur. Others guess the creators spent a huge marketing budget pushing it across social media. In fact, the team has confirmed they spent almost nothing on promotion. What really makes this video stand out is its production techniques. The camera work is inventive, the editing is smooth in a way you rarely see outside professional studios, and the sound design pulls you in from the first second. Viewers may not know the technical terms, but they feel the quality instantly — and that feeling is what they share with their friends.
This leads to a bigger question: what makes videos succeed more generally? Some creators believe the secret is translating their work into multiple languages, and others chase whatever long-term trend the industry is predicting. Both strategies sound sensible, but the evidence points elsewhere: videos become more successful when they are released at the right time. The same clip that disappears on a quiet Tuesday can explode on a holiday weekend when millions are scrolling. Timing decides whether the spark meets dry wood or wet ground. So my advice to creators is simple: polish your craft, certainly — but study your audience's calendar just as carefully as your camera settings.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
1. Đáp án: Its production techniques. Bẫy: "celebrities" bị phủ định ("every face is an unknown amateur"), "marketing budget" bị phủ định ("spent almost nothing").
2. Đáp án: They should be released at the right time. Bẫy: "translated into multiple languages" và "follow long-term trends" được nhắc là chiến lược của người khác ("Both strategies sound sensible, but...").

questions.prompt: According to the reviewer, when can videos become more successful?
options: If they are translated into multiple languages.
They should be released at the right time.
When they strictly follow long-term trends.

questions.prompt: How many pages of the assignment?
questions.explanation:
Before you all rush out — one last thing about the history assignment! I've had three emails asking about the length, so let's settle it now. The instructions sheet from last year said six pages, but that was for the old course — ignore it. Somebody also heard five pages from the other class; that's their topic, not ours. For this assignment, I want exactly four pages — no more, no less. Four pages, typed, on my desk by Friday morning. Have a good weekend!

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án C – 4.
• Vì sao đúng: "For this assignment, I want exactly four pages — no more, no less. Four pages, typed, on my desk by Friday morning".
• 6 sai: là số trang trong tờ hướng dẫn của khóa CŨ — "The instructions sheet from last year said six pages, but that was for the old course — ignore it".
• 5 sai: là yêu cầu của lớp khác với đề tài khác — "Somebody also heard five pages from the other class; that's their topic, not ours".
👉 Mẹo: dạng hỏi số trang/số lượng, bám cụm "For THIS assignment, I want...". Số gắn với "last year", "the other class" đều bị loại.

questions.prompt: What is Mary's number?
questions.explanation:
Oh hi, Susan, glad I caught your voicemail at least! You asked for Mary's new number — she changed it last month, that's why you couldn't reach her. Have a pen ready? Here it is: five five five... three nine two zero. Let me repeat that slowly: five, five, five — three, nine, two, zero. She usually answers in the evening after seven. Tell her the book club moved to Thursday when you speak to her. Bye for now!

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án B – 555 3920.
• Vì sao đúng: người nói đọc rồi nhắc lại chậm — "five five five... three nine two zero. Let me repeat that slowly: five, five, five — three, nine, two, zero".
• 335 3902 sai: cụm đầu là 335 chứ không phải 555, và hai chữ số cuối bị đảo (3902 thay vì 3920).
• 333 3029 sai: cả cụm đầu lẫn cụm sau đều không khớp dãy số đọc trong bài.
👉 Mẹo: dạng chép số điện thoại, đừng chốt ở lần đọc đầu — bài luôn có câu "Let me repeat". Chép ở lần hai và soi kỹ THỨ TỰ hai chữ số cuối, vì nhiễu thường chỉ đảo chỗ.

questions.prompt: What type of location does the speaker enjoy living in most?
questions.explanation:
People are always surprised when I tell them where I feel most at home. I grew up in the countryside, and yes, the fields are pretty, but there was nothing to do after six o'clock. Then we tried the suburbs for a few years — quiet streets, nice gardens, and to be honest, I was bored there too. It was only when I moved into the city that everything clicked: the noise, the lights, a café on every corner. The city is where I truly enjoy living.

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án C – The city.
• Vì sao đúng: "It was only when I moved into the city that everything clicked: the noise, the lights, a café on every corner. The city is where I truly enjoy living".
• The countryside sai: nơi anh lớn lên nhưng buồn chán — "the fields are pretty, but there was nothing to do after six o'clock".
• The suburbs sai: đã thử vài năm và cũng thấy chán — "we tried the suburbs for a few years... and to be honest, I was bored there too".
👉 Mẹo: dạng hỏi nơi thích nhất, bài kể theo trình tự từng nơi đã sống. Đáp án là nơi CUỐI kèm từ cảm xúc mạnh ("everything clicked", "truly enjoy").

questions.prompt: Listen to a man calling his friend. Why does he make the call?
options: To tell her he will be late
questions.explanation:
Hey Claire, it's Rob! No, don't worry, I'm not lost this time — I actually know the way to the restaurant, no directions needed, miracle of miracles. And I'm not calling to invite you anywhere new either, we're already meeting tonight, aren't we? The thing is... I'm still stuck at the office. The report went back for changes at the last minute, so I'll be about forty minutes late. Order the starters without me — I'll run all the way. Sorry, sorry, sorry!

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án C – To tell her he will be late.
• Vì sao đúng: "The thing is... I'm still stuck at the office. The report went back for changes at the last minute, so I'll be about forty minutes late".
• To ask for directions sai: anh khẳng định biết đường — "I'm not lost this time — I actually know the way to the restaurant, no directions needed".
• To invite her out sai: hai người vốn đã hẹn gặp tối nay — "I'm not calling to invite you anywhere new either, we're already meeting tonight, aren't we?".
👉 Mẹo: dạng hỏi mục đích cuộc gọi, người gọi loại 2 khả năng bằng "I'm not calling to...". Lý do thật nằm ngay sau "The thing is...".

questions.prompt: Why did she return to the shop?
questions.explanation:
You won't believe my afternoon. Remember the blue shirt I bought for Dad's birthday on Saturday? When he opened the box, it turned out to be a medium, and Dad has worn a large for thirty years. So today I went back to the shop to exchange the shirt for the right size. The assistant was lovely about it — found the large straight away and even wrapped it again for free. Second try at the birthday present tomorrow. Wish me luck!

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án A – To exchange a shirt.
• Vì sao đúng: "today I went back to the shop to exchange the shirt for the right size" — vì áo mua là size medium trong khi bố mặc size large.
• To buy a skirt sai: bài không hề nhắc tới váy ngắn; "skirt" chỉ là nhiễu gần âm với "shirt", và cô đi ĐỔI chứ không mua mới.
• To exchange a dress sai: món đồ trong bài là chiếc áo sơ mi xanh — "the blue shirt I bought for Dad's birthday", không phải váy liền.
👉 Mẹo: bộ ba shirt / skirt / dress là bẫy nghe gần âm. Nghe kỹ phụ âm đầu, đồng thời bám manh mối bối cảnh (quà cho bố, size medium/large) để loại nhanh.

questions.prompt: Listen to a man talking about the game he is playing. What is the game stopping him from doing?
questions.explanation:
Okay, I need to talk about this game, because it's driving me crazy. Playing it is not the problem — I play every single evening, two hours minimum. And changing characters? Easy, I've tried all twelve of them, from the knight to the little wizard. But winning? That's another story. Whatever I do, that final level beats me every time. The game simply will not let me win. Forty-three attempts. Forty-three! One day, my friends. One day.

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án C – Win.
• Vì sao đúng: "Whatever I do, that final level beats me every time. The game simply will not let me win. Forty-three attempts".
• Play sai: việc chơi hoàn toàn không phải vấn đề — "Playing it is not the problem — I play every single evening, two hours minimum".
• Change characters sai: đổi nhân vật rất dễ, anh đã thử hết — "Easy, I've tried all twelve of them, from the knight to the little wizard".
👉 Mẹo: câu hỏi "stopping him from doing" là hỏi việc KHÔNG làm được. Gạch mọi việc đi kèm "not the problem", "easy"; đáp án nằm sau "But...".

questions.prompt: Listen to a student explaining the project. Why did the students do the experiment on the tree?
options: To study the effects of pollution
To measure the speed of the plant's growth
To observe how trees absorb water
questions.explanation:
For our science project this term, our group worked with the old oak tree behind the school. Let me explain what we were trying to find out. We put special filters on the leaves and collected samples every week, because we wanted to study the effects of pollution — our school is right next to the main road, and we wanted to see what the traffic is doing to the tree. The results surprised everyone, and our teacher has sent them to the town council.

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án A – To study the effects of pollution.
• Vì sao đúng: "we wanted to study the effects of pollution — our school is right next to the main road, and we wanted to see what the traffic is doing to the tree".
• To measure the speed of the plant's growth sai: không được nhắc tới trong bài, chỉ là phương án gây nhiễu.
• To observe how trees absorb water sai: cũng không được nhắc tới; bài chỉ nói đặt màng lọc lên lá và lấy mẫu hằng tuần — "We put special filters on the leaves and collected samples every week".
👉 Mẹo: dạng hỏi mục đích thí nghiệm, bám cụm "because we wanted to...". Đừng suy diễn từ chi tiết dụng cụ (lá, mẫu) sang một mục đích khác.

questions.prompt: What's the main change managers are going to do?
questions.explanation:
Team, quick summary of what the managers decided yesterday, so nobody is surprised on Monday. First — the budget stays exactly as it is; the rumours about cuts are wrong. Second — the meeting stays in our usual building; moving it across town was discussed and rejected. The real change is the schedule: the weekly meeting moves from Monday morning to Wednesday afternoon, and the deadlines shift with it. Check the new calendar tonight, and update your diaries. That's all — enjoy the weekend!

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án A – Adjust the schedule.
• Vì sao đúng: "The real change is the schedule: the weekly meeting moves from Monday morning to Wednesday afternoon, and the deadlines shift with it".
• Reduce the budget sai: ngân sách giữ nguyên, tin đồn cắt giảm là sai — "the budget stays exactly as it is; the rumours about cuts are wrong".
• Relocate the meeting sai: phương án chuyển địa điểm đã bị bác — "moving it across town was discussed and rejected".
👉 Mẹo: dạng thông báo "thay đổi chính là gì", nghe cụm "The real change is...". Ý đi kèm "stays exactly as it is", "was rejected" nghĩa là KHÔNG đổi.

questions.prompt: A man is talking about his day. What did he do in the morning?
options: Go for a walk in the park
questions.explanation:
What a perfect start to the day I had! I woke up before six, while the whole house was still asleep, and drove up the coast road to the top of the cliffs. I just stood there and looked at the view — the sea, the islands, the morning light on the water. I must have stayed an hour without checking my phone once. Only after that did I think about food and the rest of the day. Everyone should try a morning like that.

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án A – Look at a view.
• Vì sao đúng: "I just stood there and looked at the view — the sea, the islands, the morning light on the water. I must have stayed an hour without checking my phone once".
• Have breakfast at a cafe sai: anh chỉ nghĩ tới đồ ăn SAU đó — "Only after that did I think about food and the rest of the day".
• Go for a walk in the park sai: không được nhắc tới trong bài; anh lái xe lên vách đá rồi đứng yên ngắm cảnh — "drove up the coast road to the top of the cliffs".
👉 Mẹo: dạng hỏi "làm gì buổi sáng", chú ý trật tự thời gian. Việc nằm sau cụm "Only after that..." là việc làm SAU, không phải đáp án.

questions.prompt: What does her sister drink?
questions.explanation:
M: Right, drinks before the film — what shall I get everyone?
W: A glass of water for me, please, I'm still full from lunch.
M: Water, easy. And your sister? Coffee, I'm guessing? She looks like she needs one.
W: Oh no, definitely not coffee — she stopped drinking it last year, it kept her awake all night.
M: Really? So what does she have these days?
W: Tea. Always tea now — she's completely mad about it, green in the morning, black in the afternoon.
M: One water, one tea, and a coffee for me. Anything to eat?
W: Just the drinks — the film starts in ten minutes!

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án B – Tea.
• Vì sao đúng: "Tea. Always tea now — she's completely mad about it, green in the morning, black in the afternoon".
• Water sai: đó là đồ uống của chính người phụ nữ đang nói, không phải của em gái — "A glass of water for me, please, I'm still full from lunch".
• Coffee sai: em gái đã bỏ cà phê từ năm ngoái vì mất ngủ — "definitely not coffee — she stopped drinking it last year, it kept her awake all night".
👉 Mẹo: câu hỏi hỏi đồ uống của MỘT người cụ thể (her sister). Ghép nhanh cặp người–đồ uống khi nghe; món gắn với "for me" là của người khác.

questions.prompt: Which door do they need to take to get to Edinburgh?
questions.explanation:
W: Here we are — now, which door do we need for the Edinburgh coach?
M: The screen says... hmm, door four. No wait, that's the Glasgow service, look, it leaves ten minutes before ours.
W: Careful! And someone in the queue said door three earlier.
M: Door three is London — see the sign above it? Half the queue is going the wrong way.
W: So where is ours, then? We've got eight minutes!
M: There — door two, on the left, past the coffee stand. Edinburgh, ten fifteen, door two.
W: Door two it is. Come on, grab your bag!
M: Told you we should have arrived earlier!

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án A – Two.
• Vì sao đúng: "There — door two, on the left, past the coffee stand. Edinburgh, ten fifteen, door two".
• Four sai: cửa 4 là chuyến đi Glasgow, khởi hành sớm hơn 10 phút — "that's the Glasgow service, look, it leaves ten minutes before ours".
• Three sai: cửa 3 là chuyến đi London — "Door three is London — see the sign above it? Half the queue is going the wrong way".
👉 Mẹo: dạng hỏi cửa/bến, mỗi số gắn với một ĐIỂM ĐẾN. Chỉ chốt khi số đó đi kèm đúng tên thành phố trong câu hỏi (Edinburgh).

questions.prompt: When did they decide to meet?
questions.explanation:
M: So, the trip to the flower market — when are we actually going?
W: I first thought seven in the morning on Friday, before work. The flowers are freshest then.
M: Seven am on a work day? I'd fall asleep among the roses. What about the weekend?
W: Saturday at nine, then? That was my second idea.
M: Ah, Saturday I can't — I promised to help my brother move house, remember?
W: That's right, you told me. Okay — Sunday at nine? Nothing happens on Sunday.
M: Sunday at nine is perfect. Coffee first, flowers after.
W: Deal. Nine o'clock Sunday, at the main gate!

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án B – 9am on Sunday.
• Vì sao đúng: "Sunday at nine is perfect. Coffee first, flowers after" — chốt "Deal. Nine o'clock Sunday, at the main gate!".
• 7am on Friday sai: quá sớm vào ngày đi làm — "Seven am on a work day? I'd fall asleep among the roses".
• 9am on Saturday sai: anh bận giúp anh trai chuyển nhà — "Saturday I can't — I promised to help my brother move house".
👉 Mẹo: dạng hẹn giờ mà các phương án khác nhau cả GIỜ lẫn THỨ thì phải nghe đủ cặp, đừng bắt mỗi số 9. Chốt ở lượt có "perfect", "Deal".

questions.prompt: Listen to two friends talking about their plans for the holiday. What are they going to do on this holiday?
questions.explanation:
W: Only three weeks until the holiday! Have you decided what we're doing?
M: Well, my first idea was camping in the hills — tents, campfires, all of that.
W: In the rainy season? We'd float away in our sleeping bags!
M: True. Then I looked at flights — we could travel abroad, maybe Italy?
W: I'd love that, but honestly, after fixing the car, my savings are gone.
M: Which brings me to my last idea: the volunteer centre needs people to teach English at the summer camp. Free food, free rooms, and the kids are great.
W: Teaching at the camp... you know what, I really like that. Let's do it!
M: Excellent! I'll sign us both up tonight.

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án C – Teaching.
• Vì sao đúng: "the volunteer centre needs people to teach English at the summer camp. Free food, free rooms, and the kids are great" — cô đồng ý "I really like that. Let's do it!".
• Going camping sai: bị loại vì đang mùa mưa — "In the rainy season? We'd float away in our sleeping bags!".
• Traveling abroad sai: hết tiền tiết kiệm sau khi sửa xe — "after fixing the car, my savings are gone".
👉 Mẹo: dạng bàn kế hoạch, đáp án là ý CUỐI ("my last idea") kèm câu đồng thuận "Let's do it". Ý gắn với lý do cản trở (thời tiết, tiền bạc) là nhiễu.

questions.prompt: Four people are talking about listening to music. Match each person to the correct information.
questions.explanation:
Speaker A: My job empties me — eight hours of phone calls and complaints. So the first thing I do at home is drop onto the sofa, close my eyes, and let my favourite slow album wash the day away. Twenty minutes of those warm melodies and my shoulders finally come down from my ears. No wine, no television — just the speakers doing their quiet repair work. My wife says she can tell which song is playing by the look on my face.
Speaker B: My flatmates think I am strange, but my headphones go on the moment my books open. Instrumental only — words in songs fight with the words on the page. With the right quiet piano behind me, three hours of revision pass like one; without it, I check my phone every four minutes. I even match albums to subjects now: strings for history, soft electronic for maths. My exam playlist is basically a study partner.
Speaker C: In my family, music is not for listening — it is for joining in. The moment a song I know starts, my voice is already in it, harmonies and all. In the shower, over the cooking, in the car at full volume with the windows down. My neighbours have learned my entire repertoire through the walls, poor people. A song without my voice on top feels unfinished; that is simply how I enjoy music.
Speaker D: My alarm is set to silence — what actually starts my day is pressing play. Before my eyes fully open, the first song of my morning playlist is filling the bedroom, and by track three I am upright and human. Coffee, shower, dressing: all of it happens to music, every single morning. On the rare day the speaker battery dies, the whole house feels wrong until noon. Waking up without songs, to me, is only half waking up.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
A = To relax (PARAPHRASE: "wash the day away... shoulders come down... quiet repair work"). B = While studying (keyword "books open... revision"). C = While singing (PARAPHRASE: "my voice is already in it... my entire repertoire"). D = After waking up (keyword-lite "starts my day... morning playlist... waking up"). Nhiễu: while driving, before bed.

questions.prompt: There is too much information on the Internet
questions.explanation:
M: How did you get on with that evening course you signed up for — the online one?
W: I scraped through it, just about. Honestly, the worst part is that there's an endless mountain of stuff online — far more than any human being could ever wade through.
M: I'm not so sure that's the real trouble, though. I'll grant you it looks overwhelming at first glance, but a decent city bookshop holds more than you'd read in ten lifetimes and nobody ever moans about that.
W: Hang on, a bookshop has been filtered by somebody who knows what they're doing. Which brings me to my next point, actually — fishing out something you can actually trust online is a proper skill in its own right.
M: Oh, I agree with you there completely. Choosing the right search terms, spotting when a site is quietly selling you something — none of that comes naturally to anybody.
W: Exactly. My students click whatever sits at the top of the page and take it as gospel.
M: Mine do the same. And I'd go a step further, actually — I think all this scrolling is genuinely rewiring the way we reason things out.
W: Hmm, I don't see it that way, I'm afraid. I'll accept our habits have shifted — nobody reads a newspaper cover to cover any more. But our actual reasoning? No, that's much as it ever was.
M: You say that, but I can't hold an argument in my head the way I used to.
W: That's called being forty, I'd say.
M: Fair enough. One thing I am certain of, mind you — youngsters today simply won't wait for anything.
W: Now that I do agree with, one hundred per cent. If a video takes four seconds to load, they've swiped away and forgotten it ever existed.
M: My nephew watches entire films on double speed. I find it baffling.
W: I've caught myself doing exactly that, to be honest. Perhaps it isn't only the young after all.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
Key: Quá nhiều thông tin trên Internet = Woman · Tìm thông tin cần kỹ năng = Both · Internet ảnh hưởng cách ta tư duy = Man · Internet khiến giới trẻ thiếu kiên nhẫn = Both
