• Vì sao đúng: người chọn ngành y kể về vị bác sĩ trẻ ngồi giải thích cho cả nhà mỗi tối khi ông nội nằm viện, rồi chốt "I want to BE that for someone. I chose medicine to help people — full stop".
• To make his family proud sai: bố mẹ có mơ ước đó nhưng bị bác bỏ "living someone else's dream burns out fast. That's not it".
• To make a lot of money sai: cũng bị loại "After a decade of loans and night shifts? There are faster roads to money, believe me".
👉 Mẹo: dạng hỏi LÝ DO CHỌN NGHỀ, người bạn sẽ đoán 2 lý do phổ biến (gia đình, tiền) và đều bị phủ định. Đáp án thật đi kèm một câu chuyện cá nhân và cụm nhấn "full stop", "that's why".

questions.prompt: A woman is talking to the police. What did she lose?
questions.explanation:
M: Next, please! Yes, madam — you look like you've had a rough afternoon.
W: Terrible, officer. Something went missing at the shopping centre and I need to report it.
M: We'll take it down. First guess from experience: your wallet? The sales bring out the pickpockets.
W: The wallet is safe — zipped in my inside pocket, I've checked five times.
M: Good. A necklace, then? We've had two chains reported this week.
W: No jewellery today, officer. It's my bag — the small grey one with the long strap. I hung it on the fitting-room hook, tried on a coat, walked out... and only remembered at the escalator. When I ran back, the hook was empty.
M: A grey bag with a long strap, fitting rooms, roughly what time?
W: Around three. My keys and my daughter's birthday money are inside. Please hurry, officer.
M: I'll ring centre security right now — fitting-room finds usually reach lost property within the hour. Take a seat, madam.

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án B – A bag (chiếc túi xách).
• Vì sao đúng: bà nói "It's my bag — the small grey one with the long strap. I hung it on the fitting-room hook... When I ran back, the hook was empty".
• A wallet sai: ví vẫn còn "The wallet is safe — zipped in my inside pocket, I've checked five times".
• A necklace sai: hôm đó bà không đeo trang sức "No jewellery today, officer".
👉 Mẹo: dạng hỏi MẤT GÌ khi trình báo công an, viên cảnh sát sẽ đoán trước theo kinh nghiệm và bị bác bỏ. Đáp án đi kèm mô tả chi tiết (màu, kích cỡ, quai) và tình huống mất cụ thể.

questions.prompt: Tom is talking with his friend about his teachers. What is his favourite teacher?
questions.explanation:
W: Tom! How's the new term? Your mum says you actually LIKE school now — I demand an explanation.
M: Ha! It's true, and it's entirely one teacher's fault.
W: Let me guess — Miss Taylor? Everyone adores her music lessons.
M: Everyone except me — she made me sing a solo once and I still hear the laughter in my dreams.
W: Poor thing! Mr. Styles, then? You live in your football boots.
M: On the PITCH, yes — but his lessons are just running laps in the rain while he shouts encouragement from under an umbrella.
W: So who's the miracle worker?
M: Miss Brown, science! Last week we grew crystals, the week before we built a battery from lemons. She answers every question like it's the best question ever asked.
W: A lemon battery! Now I want to join her class.
M: Get in line — half the school suddenly loves science. Miss Brown is the reason I do my homework FIRST now.

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án C – Miss Brown (cô Brown dạy Khoa học).
• Vì sao đúng: Tom nói "Miss Brown, science! Last week we grew crystals, the week before we built a battery from lemons" và "Miss Brown is the reason I do my homework FIRST now".
• Miss Taylor sai: gắn với kỷ niệm xấu hổ "she made me sing a solo once and I still hear the laughter in my dreams".
• Mr. Styles sai: Tom mê bóng đá nhưng chê tiết học "his lessons are just running laps in the rain while he shouts encouragement from under an umbrella".
👉 Mẹo: dạng hỏi GIÁO VIÊN YÊU THÍCH, đừng chọn theo môn mà học sinh thích ngoài đời (bóng đá). Chọn giáo viên được kể kèm ví dụ tiết học cụ thể và câu khen trực tiếp.

questions.prompt: A woman is talking to a shop assistant. Why does the woman return the dress?
questions.explanation:
M: Welcome back to the boutique! Oh — you have one of our bags. A return?
W: I'm afraid so. This dress, from Tuesday. I'd like my money back, please.
M: Of course, let me just note the reason. Was it the colour after all? You did hesitate between the green and this one.
W: No, no — the colour is perfect, it's exactly the shade I wanted for the party.
M: Then perhaps the pattern? These leaves are quite... enthusiastic.
W: The pattern I love — it's why I chose it over the plain ones! The problem is the size. At home, in honest daylight, it simply doesn't fit — too tight across the shoulders, and the zip surrenders halfway. And your size chart says the next one up is out of stock everywhere.
M: I'm sorry — this cut does run small, we've had a few returns. A full refund, then?
W: Yes, please. And maybe a note to the factory: real shoulders exist!

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án A – Because of its size (vì kích cỡ không vừa).
• Vì sao đúng: cô nói "The problem is the size. At home, in honest daylight, it simply doesn't fit — too tight across the shoulders, and the zip surrenders halfway"; nhân viên cũng thừa nhận "this cut does run small".
• Because of its color sai: cô khen màu "the colour is perfect, it's exactly the shade I wanted for the party".
• Because of its pattern sai: cô còn thích họa tiết "The pattern I love — it's why I chose it over the plain ones!".
👉 Mẹo: dạng hỏi LÝ DO TRẢ HÀNG, nhân viên sẽ đoán sai vài lý do và khách bác bỏ bằng lời khen. Đáp án nằm sau "The problem is..." và có bằng chứng vật lý (chật vai, kéo khóa không lên).

questions.prompt: Louis is having dinner in a new restaurant. What does he complain about?
questions.explanation:
Reporting live from my table at the new bistro — this is Louis, your unofficial food critic! The verdict so far. The menu prices genuinely surprised me — main courses cheaper than the pizzeria across the road, no complaints there. And the food? My lamb was perfect, herbs, crispy edges, the works — the kitchen clearly knows its business. BUT. I ordered dessert twenty-five minutes ago. My water glass has been empty for half an hour. Three tables are waving at nobody. The service here is painfully slow — that's my one real complaint tonight!

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án C – The service is slow (phục vụ chậm).
• Vì sao đúng: cả bài khen rồi bẻ lái bằng chữ "BUT", và Louis chốt lại nhận xét trọng tâm "The service here is painfully slow — that's my one real complaint tonight", kèm bằng chứng: đợi tráng miệng 25 phút, cốc nước cạn nửa tiếng.
• The price is cheap sai: anh có khen giá "main courses cheaper than the pizzeria across the road", nhưng đó là chi tiết phụ, không phải nhận xét chính anh muốn nêu.
• The food is delicious sai: món ăn cũng được khen "My lamb was perfect, herbs, crispy edges", nhưng vẫn nằm ở phần trước chữ "BUT".
👉 Mẹo: dạng hỏi NHẬN XÉT/ĐÁNH GIÁ, nghe tới chữ "BUT" là biết trọng tâm nằm ở vế sau. Câu có "my one real complaint", "the only problem" chính là ý người nói muốn nhấn.

questions.prompt: A teacher is talking to her students. Where are the students now?
questions.explanation:
Eyes on me for a moment, class — and yes, you may take your coats off! I can see the confusion: this doesn't look like our classroom because it isn't one. Nor is it a museum, despite the old paintings — no glass cases, no tickets, look around. We are guests today in a genuine Georgian townhouse — a private home, three centuries old, lived in by the same family for five generations. The lady of the house will join us upstairs. Notebooks out: everything you see — the stairs, the fireplaces — is your worksheet today!

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án B – In a townhouse (trong một ngôi nhà phố cổ).
• Vì sao đúng: cô giáo nói "We are guests today in a genuine Georgian townhouse — a private home, three centuries old, lived in by the same family for five generations".
• At school sai: bị phủ định ngay "this doesn't look like our classroom because it isn't one".
• In a museum sai: cũng bị loại dù có tranh cổ "Nor is it a museum, despite the old paintings — no glass cases, no tickets".
👉 Mẹo: dạng hỏi ĐANG Ở ĐÂU, người nói thường loại trừ hai nơi dễ nhầm trước bằng "it isn't", "Nor is it". Đáp án đi kèm "We are... in" và mô tả đặc trưng (nhà riêng, ba thế kỷ, năm đời).

questions.prompt: A woman is calling her son. What time will the mother meet the son?
questions.explanation:
Danny, it's Mum — pick-up plan for today, memorise this! Your football practice was supposed to end at two, but Coach messaged all the parents: the other team needs the field early, so everything moved. And no, I can't do six either, love — Grandma's dinner starts at five, we'd be shamefully late. So: I will meet you at three o'clock. Three, at the school side gate, the usual spot by the bike racks. Three o'clock, Danny — showered and READY, not 'just five more minutes'. Love you!

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án C – Three o'clock (3 giờ).
• Vì sao đúng: mẹ chốt "So: I will meet you at three o'clock. Three, at the school side gate, the usual spot by the bike racks".
• Two o'clock sai: là giờ tan tập ban đầu nhưng đã đổi "Your football practice was supposed to end at two, but Coach messaged all the parents... so everything moved".
• Six o'clock sai: bị loại vì bữa tối nhà bà "I can't do six either, love — Grandma's dinner starts at five, we'd be shamefully late".
👉 Mẹo: dạng hỏi MẤY GIỜ ĐÓN, cẩn thận với "was supposed to" (dự kiến cũ). Đáp án đi sau "So:" và luôn kèm địa điểm đón cụ thể.

questions.prompt: Jack is calling to invite a friend to his house. What color is Jack’s house??
questions.explanation:
Hey Omar, it's Jack — you're really coming Saturday! Let me describe the house so you don't wander the whole street like Ben did. Number fourteen, Cherry Lane. Now, careful: my NEIGHBOUR's house is the black one with the iron gates — very dramatic, not mine, don't ring that bell, the dog is theatrical. Across the road there's a green one — also not me, that's the retired sea captain. Mine is the red house! Brick red, white windows, lemon tree by the door. The red one, number fourteen. Party starts at six!

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án B – Red (màu đỏ).
• Vì sao đúng: Jack nói "Mine is the red house! Brick red, white windows, lemon tree by the door. The red one, number fourteen".
• Black sai: đó là nhà hàng xóm "my NEIGHBOUR's house is the black one with the iron gates — very dramatic, not mine, don't ring that bell".
• Green sai: là nhà đối diện của ông thuyền trưởng về hưu "Across the road there's a green one — also not me".
👉 Mẹo: dạng hỏi MÀU NHÀ/ĐỒ VẬT, bài cố tình gán màu cho hàng xóm và nhà đối diện trước. Chỉ khoanh màu đi kèm đại từ sở hữu "Mine is...", "my house is...".

questions.prompt: A man is talking about his daily routine. What does he do after work?
questions.explanation:
My after-work routine — people assume it's boring, but it's the highlight of my day! Five o'clock hits, laptop closes. Now, my colleagues head straight to the coffee shop downstairs — I skip that, caffeine after five turns me into an owl. And going straight home? That's what I did for years: sofa, screen, sleep, repeat — never again. What I do now: I play football! Five-a-side, every single evening after work, the pitch behind the depot. Ninety minutes of running and shouting with the lads — best therapy money can't buy!

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án C – Play football (chơi bóng đá).
• Vì sao đúng: anh nói "What I do now: I play football! Five-a-side, every single evening after work, the pitch behind the depot".
• Go to the coffee shop sai: đó là việc đồng nghiệp làm, anh bỏ qua "my colleagues head straight to the coffee shop downstairs — I skip that, caffeine after five turns me into an owl".
• Go home sai: là thói quen cũ đã từ bỏ "That's what I did for years: sofa, screen, sleep, repeat — never again".
👉 Mẹo: dạng hỏi SAU GIỜ LÀM LÀM GÌ, phân biệt ba mốc: việc của đồng nghiệp, việc mình từng làm ("for years", "never again"), và việc hiện tại ("What I do now"). Chỉ lấy vế thứ ba.

questions.prompt: Doctor’s office is calling about a change in the appointment. When is the new appointment?
questions.explanation:
Good afternoon, this is Riverside Medical Centre with an important change to your appointment, please listen fully. Doctor Novak has been called to a training day, so your original booking — Friday the fourteenth — cannot go ahead. We know Wednesday the twelfth was mentioned as a possibility last week; that slot has unfortunately been taken. Your confirmed new appointment is Thursday the thirteenth, at the usual time, nine fifteen. Thursday the thirteenth, nine fifteen, same building, second floor. Press one to confirm, or call us back. Thank you!

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án A – Thursday 13th (thứ Năm ngày 13).
• Vì sao đúng: phòng khám thông báo "Your confirmed new appointment is Thursday the thirteenth, at the usual time, nine fifteen... same building, second floor".
• Friday 14th sai: là lịch cũ không thể diễn ra "your original booking — Friday the fourteenth — cannot go ahead" vì bác sĩ đi tập huấn.
• Wednesday 12th sai: từng được nhắc nhưng đã có người khác lấy "that slot has unfortunately been taken".
👉 Mẹo: dạng ĐỔI LỊCH KHÁM, ba mốc nằm liền kề nhau (12–13–14) nên phải nghe cả thứ lẫn ngày. Chỉ khoanh mốc đi kèm "confirmed", "your new appointment is".

questions.prompt: An author is talking about her daily routine. When does she usually write?
questions.explanation:
Readers always ask about my writing day, imagining candlelight and midnight inspiration — the truth is less romantic! Mornings? Hopeless. Before eleven I am a coffee-drinking zombie; I answer emails and stare at birds. And night writing, which sounds so poetic — I tried it for a year and produced nonsense I deleted every next day. My real writing happens in the afternoons. From one until six, phone off, same desk, same chair — that's when the sentences finally behave. Every book I've published was written after lunch!

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án A – In the afternoons (vào buổi chiều).
• Vì sao đúng: nhà văn nói "My real writing happens in the afternoons. From one until six, phone off, same desk, same chair" và xác nhận "Every book I've published was written after lunch!".
• In the mornings sai: buổi sáng cô không viết nổi "Mornings? Hopeless. Before eleven I am a coffee-drinking zombie".
• At night sai: đã thử một năm và thất bại "I tried it for a year and produced nonsense I deleted every next day".
👉 Mẹo: dạng hỏi THỜI ĐIỂM TRONG NGÀY, người nói hay bác bỏ hình dung lãng mạn của độc giả trước. Đáp án đi kèm "My real... happens in" và khung giờ cụ thể (from one until six).

questions.prompt: A woman is talking about her usual Saturday routine. What does she usually do on Saturdays?
questions.explanation:
Saturdays in my world are sacred, and everyone knows not to book me! People assume I spend them shopping — wrong; I do the boring food run on Thursday evenings precisely to keep Saturday free. And this week is unusual because there IS a birthday party — my niece turns seven — but that's a one-off, not the routine. My real Saturday tradition: I see my family. Every week: lunch at Mum and Dad's, board games with my brother's kids, the walk with Grandpa at four. Same rhythm for six years — and I protect it like treasure!

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án B – Sees her family (gặp gia đình).
• Vì sao đúng: cô nói "My real Saturday tradition: I see my family. Every week: lunch at Mum and Dad's, board games with my brother's kids, the walk with Grandpa at four" — duy trì suốt sáu năm.
• Goes shopping sai: việc mua sắm được dời sang thứ Năm "I do the boring food run on Thursday evenings precisely to keep Saturday free".
• Goes to a birthday party sai: chỉ là ngoại lệ tuần này "this week is unusual because there IS a birthday party — my niece turns seven — but that's a one-off, not the routine".
👉 Mẹo: dạng hỏi THÓI QUEN THƯỜNG LÀM, câu hỏi có chữ "usually" nên phải loại mọi việc gắn với "this week", "a one-off". Đáp án đi kèm "every week", "tradition", "same rhythm".

questions.prompt: A man is talking about his family trip. What does the man’s wife enjoy?
questions.explanation:
Our family trip worked because everyone got their own happiness — let me explain the system! Me, I'm the shopper: give me a local market and two hours, I'm in heaven — everyone else groans. The kids demanded hiking, so we did two mountain days, boots, blisters and all — my knees are still filing complaints. But my wife — her joy is photography! She carried that camera everywhere: sunrise over the harbour, old doors, strangers' dogs, four hundred photos of the same lighthouse. The album she's making is genuinely gorgeous. Happy wife, happy trip!

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án A – Photography (chụp ảnh).
• Vì sao đúng: người chồng kể "But my wife — her joy is photography! She carried that camera everywhere: sunrise over the harbour, old doors... four hundred photos of the same lighthouse".
• Shopping sai: đó là sở thích của chính người kể "Me, I'm the shopper: give me a local market and two hours, I'm in heaven".
• Hiking sai: là đòi hỏi của lũ trẻ "The kids demanded hiking, so we did two mountain days".
👉 Mẹo: dạng hỏi AI THÍCH GÌ trong gia đình, bài gán mỗi sở thích cho một người. Ghi nhanh cặp "người – sở thích" ngay khi nghe (Me / the kids / my wife) rồi mới trả lời đúng người được hỏi.

questions.prompt: The woman is discussing her new exercise routine. How much time does she spend cycling?
questions.explanation:
M: You look glowing lately — this new exercise routine is working! What does it involve?
W: A bit of everything, carefully timed — I'm quite proud of the schedule.
M: Give me the breakdown. I've heard you're at the gym for an hour?
W: Sixty minutes is the TOTAL session, yes, but that includes changing and chatting, so it doesn't count as one exercise!
M: Fine — the details, then. How's it split?
W: Forty-five minutes was my cycling target when I started... but honestly, my knees negotiated it down.
M: So what did the knees agree to?
W: Thirty-five minutes of cycling — that's my real number now, every session, plus stretching after. Thirty-five on the bike, and I feel fantastic.
M: Thirty-five minutes, three times a week? I'm officially inspired.
W: Join me Monday! The bikes next to mine are always free at seven am — I wonder why!

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án B – 35 minutes.
• Vì sao đúng: cô nói "Thirty-five minutes of cycling — that's my real number now, every session, plus stretching after".
• 60 minutes sai: là tổng thời gian cả buổi tập, gồm cả thay đồ và tán gẫu "Sixty minutes is the TOTAL session, yes, but that includes changing and chatting, so it doesn't count as one exercise".
• 45 minutes sai: là mục tiêu ban đầu, đã giảm xuống "Forty-five minutes was my cycling target when I started... but honestly, my knees negotiated it down".
👉 Mẹo: dạng hỏi THỜI LƯỢNG cho MỘT hoạt động, cảnh giác con số chỉ TỔNG buổi ("total session") và con số chỉ mục tiêu ban đầu ("target when I started"). Chỉ lấy số đi kèm chính hoạt động được hỏi.

questions.prompt: A woman is talking about her job. What encouraged her to become a scientist?
questions.explanation:
M: Doctor Reyes, my daughter wants to know: what makes a person become a scientist? Was it a computer? She thinks it's always computers.
W: Ha! Tell her computers came much later for me — we didn't even own one until I was at university.
M: Then your mother, perhaps? You mention her in every interview.
W: Mum was wonderful, but honestly, she wanted me to study law — she fainted a little when I chose geology!
M: So what was it?
W: A large stone! I was eight, on a beach holiday, and I found this huge grey stone with a perfect spiral shell pressed inside it. A fossil, millions of years old, in my little hands.
M: And that was the moment?
W: That was everything. I asked a thousand questions nobody could answer — so I spent my life finding the answers myself. That stone still sits on my desk!
M: My daughter will love this story. Maybe I should take her to the beach!
W: Do — and let her pick up every stone she likes!

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án C – A large stone (một hòn đá lớn có hóa thạch).
• Vì sao đúng: nhà khoa học kể "A large stone! I was eight, on a beach holiday, and I found this huge grey stone with a perfect spiral shell pressed inside it" và khẳng định "That was everything".
• Her computer sai: máy tính đến rất muộn "computers came much later for me — we didn't even own one until I was at university".
• Her mother sai: mẹ còn muốn bà học luật "Mum was wonderful, but honestly, she wanted me to study law — she fainted a little when I chose geology!".
👉 Mẹo: dạng hỏi ĐIỀU GÌ TRUYỀN CẢM HỨNG, người phỏng vấn sẽ đoán hai nguyên nhân "hợp lý" và đều bị bác. Đáp án là một kỷ niệm cụ thể có tuổi tác, địa điểm, chi tiết cảm giác.

questions.prompt: Listen to the speaker talking about their weekly schedule. When is the meeting scheduled?
questions.explanation:
W: New quarter, new schedule! Have you seen the team calendar yet?
M: Just opened it. Please tell me they didn't keep the Monday morning meeting.
W: They did NOT — mercy exists! Monday mornings are now protected focus time, no meetings allowed.
M: Finally! So when did the big weekly land? Someone mentioned Friday afternoon...
W: Friday afternoon was proposed, and the whole office rebelled — nobody's brain works after Friday lunch, and management actually listened.
M: Miracles everywhere. So...?
W: Wednesday afternoon! The meeting is every Wednesday at two — middle of the week, everyone's alive, reports ready.
M: Wednesday at two... that's actually sensible. Who ARE these new managers?
W: Ones who drink enough coffee! Block your calendar — first one is this Wednesday.

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án C – Wednesday afternoon (chiều thứ Tư).
• Vì sao đúng: cô nói "Wednesday afternoon! The meeting is every Wednesday at two — middle of the week, everyone's alive, reports ready".
• Monday morning sai: đã bị bỏ hẳn "They did NOT — Monday mornings are now protected focus time, no meetings allowed".
• Friday afternoon sai: từng được đề xuất nhưng bị phản đối "Friday afternoon was proposed, and the whole office rebelled — nobody's brain works after Friday lunch".
👉 Mẹo: dạng hỏi LỊCH HỌP HÀNG TUẦN, phải nghe cả THỨ lẫn BUỔI. Loại mốc đi kèm "was proposed", "no meetings allowed"; đáp án có giờ cụ thể ("at two") và lý do hợp lý.

questions.prompt: A man is reading the news about a housing development plan. How many new houses are going to be built?
questions.explanation:
M: Have you read this? The big housing development plan for the north fields — it's finally approved!
W: I saw the headline! The numbers kept changing though — what did they settle on?
M: Well, the first proposal said fifteen hundred houses, remember? The council rejected that as too few — wouldn't solve the waiting lists.
W: And then the developers swung the other way — twenty-five hundred, wasn't it? The neighbours went to war over that.
M: Exactly, petitions and everything — too much traffic, not enough schools. So the final compromise, signed yesterday: two thousand new houses.
W: Two thousand... with the new school and the park included?
M: Both included — that was the deal. Two thousand homes, building starts in spring.
W: My sister's been on the housing list for three years. This might finally be her chance!
M: Tell her to apply early — half the town is thinking the same thing.

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án B – 2000 (hai nghìn căn).
• Vì sao đúng: người đàn ông nói "the final compromise, signed yesterday: two thousand new houses" và nhắc lại "Two thousand homes, building starts in spring".
• 1500 sai: là đề xuất đầu tiên bị hội đồng bác vì quá ít "the first proposal said fifteen hundred houses... The council rejected that as too few".
• 2500 sai: là con số chủ đầu tư đưa ra sau đó và bị dân phản đối "The neighbours went to war over that... too much traffic, not enough schools".
👉 Mẹo: dạng hỏi SỐ LƯỢNG trong tin tức, ba con số theo trình tự đề xuất – phản đề – thỏa hiệp. Chọn số đi kèm "final", "compromise", "signed/approved", thường nằm ở giữa hai số kia.

questions.prompt: Four people are talking about protecting the environment. Match each person to the correct information.
questions.explanation:
Speaker A: People are surprised when I call my armchair shopping an environmental habit, but do the sums with me. My orders arrive in one van that serves the whole neighbourhood — one engine replacing the thirty cars that would each have driven to the retail park and circled for parking. I batch everything into a single weekly delivery, so no extra trips, no impulse petrol. My sister burns a litre of fuel to buy a toothbrush; my toothbrush shares a van with her street's groceries.
Speaker B: My car has learned to live without me on weekdays. Since March I catch the six-fifty into the centre — no fuel burned in my name, no half hour hunting for parking, and the queue of single-driver cars I sail past confirms my choice every morning. My colleagues thought the novelty would wear off before summer. Instead my car now spends its weekdays under a cover, and the planet and my wallet both breathe easier.
Speaker C: My electricity meter used to spin like a fan; now it crawls, and that is my proudest achievement this year. Every lamp in the house went low-energy, the heating drops two degrees at night, and the television no longer sleeps with one glowing eye — everything goes off at the wall. My teenagers complained for a week, then turned it into a competition. Last month's usage was barely half of last year's.
Speaker D: In my bathroom hangs a four-minute hourglass, and the family showers race it. The washing-up happens in a basin, never under a running stream, and the rinsing water ends its life in my flowerpots. I fitted the little flow-savers on every tap the day the utility report showed what an average family pours away. My children think I am obsessed. I tell them: electricity can be made tomorrow, but the well does not refill on demand.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
A = Shopping online (PARAPHRASE: "armchair shopping... orders... single weekly delivery"). B = Not driving to work (PARAPHRASE: "car has learned to live without me... catch the six-fifty"). C = Using less electricity (keyword-lite "electricity meter... low-energy... usage half"). D = Using less water (keyword-lite "showers race it... running stream... well"). Nhiễu: planting trees, recycling bottles. (Variant khác lời Đề 03.)

questions.prompt: Four people are talking about online shopping. Match each person to the correct information.
questions.explanation:
Speaker A: I broke my ankle in January, and that is when internet shopping saved my winter. Everything I needed simply appeared: the courier brought my groceries to the third floor, the pharmacy package came the next morning, and even my new crutch pads arrived faster than my sister could visit. Two months without leaving the flat, and I never missed a meal or a birthday present. The doorbell became my favourite sound in the house.
Speaker B: My grandmother taught me never to pay the first price, and the internet is her lesson made easy. I watch items for weeks, wait for the seasonal sales, stack the discount codes, and strike when the price bottoms out. The winter coat I am wearing cost me less than half the shop price. My colleagues call me stingy, but my bank account calls me clever — same product, same label, very different receipt.
Speaker C: I run my own bakery, which means my day off is Tuesday and only Tuesday. Spending it in queues would be a small tragedy, so my entire household shops itself online in stolen minutes — flour suppliers compared while the ovens heat, birthday gifts chosen on the bus, groceries ordered during my lunch break. The hours other people spend pushing trolleys, I spend by the river with my dog. That trade is the best bargain the internet ever offered me.
Speaker D: My daughter has unusual feet — one size larger than the other, if you can believe it. Every shoe shop in our city offers the same fifteen models and shrugs. Online, I found a maker who sells single shoes in mixed sizes, three colours, her exact fit. The same story repeats with everything unusual we need: left-handed scissors, extra-long trousers, that discontinued ink my husband swears by. The high street stocks the middle of the road; the internet stocks everyone else.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
A = The products are delivered (PARAPHRASE: "simply appeared... courier... doorbell became my favourite sound"). B = It is cheaper (PARAPHRASE: "less than half the shop price... different receipt"). C = It saves time (PARAPHRASE: "stolen minutes... hours other people spend pushing trolleys"). D = There are more choices (PARAPHRASE: "single shoes in mixed sizes... stocks everyone else"). Nhiễu: easy to return, safe to pay. (Variant khác lời Đề 05/06.)

questions.prompt: Four people are talking about listening to music. Match each person to the correct information.
questions.explanation:
Speaker A: My nervous system has an off switch, and it is shaped like a record player. After the children are in bed, I pour a tea, lower the needle on something slow, and let the day's knots untie themselves one by one. No screens, no talking — just twenty quiet minutes while the melodies do their gentle housework inside my head. My husband says he can measure my week by which record I reach for on Friday night.
Speaker B: I wake up before my alarm just to beat it to the speaker. The first song goes on while my eyes are still half closed, and it walks me through the whole morning — louder for the shower, brighter for breakfast, something cheerful for finding my keys. By the time I close the front door, side one is finished and I am fully human. A morning that starts in silence feels broken to me all day.
Speaker C: My voice is not good, and I could not care less — every song I know is a duet the moment it starts. I harmonise with the kettle-side radio, perform full choruses into the hairbrush, and my car is a one-woman concert hall on the motorway. The neighbours applauded from their balcony once, only half joking. Listening quietly feels like watching a dance and refusing to move; joining in with my own voice is the entire pleasure.
Speaker D: Exam season turned me into a musical creature. My revision only works with a instrumental stream in my ears — the notes hold my attention on the page the way a fence holds sheep. Lyrics ruin it: the words on the page and the words in the song start fighting. Four hours of formulas pass gently when the piano is playing. In silence, I last twenty minutes before my phone wins.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
A = To relax (PARAPHRASE: "off switch... knots untie themselves... gentle housework"). B = After waking up (PARAPHRASE: "wake up before my alarm... walks me through the morning"). C = While singing (PARAPHRASE: "every song is a duet... my own voice is the pleasure"). D = While studying (keyword "revision... formulas"). Nhiễu: while exercising, before bed. (Variant khác lời 16/18.)

questions.prompt: Four people are talking about outdoor activities. Match each person to the correct information.
questions.explanation:
Speaker A: My Saturdays begin at the stables before the mist lifts. Brushing her down, checking her hooves, then two hours through the fields with only hoofbeats for conversation — my mare knows the route better than I do by now. People ask if it frightens me, trusting an animal that size. It is the opposite: those two hours of moving together are the calmest partnership in my week. The saddle is my favourite chair in the world.
Speaker B: Rain or shine, my trainers hit the path along the canal at seven. Nothing complicated — just me, my breathing, and five kilometres of towpath before the world wakes up properly. I started to lose my temper less, honestly, and kept going because the mornings felt unfinished without it. Last month I entered my first ten-kilometre race and finished grinning like a fool. Simple legs, simple happiness.
Speaker C: My weekends are vertical. My club drives out to the crags every Sunday, ropes and helmets rattling in the boot, and we spend the day solving the rock face metre by metre. Fingertips ache, forearms burn, and the moment you pull over the top edge repays every scrape. People call it dangerous; done properly, it is chess with your whole body. I have never trusted people more than the ones holding my rope.
Speaker D: Two wheels, fat tyres, forest trails — that is my religion. Saturday mornings I load the bike, drive to the hills, and spend four muddy hours flying down tracks and pushing back up them. The bruises are a fair tax on the joy. My wife inspects the scratches on my arms every weekend and sighs; I remind her the alternative was golf, and she agrees the mud is better.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
A = horse riding (PARAPHRASE: "stables... my mare... saddle"). B = going for a run (PARAPHRASE: "trainers hit the path... five kilometres... race"). C = climbing (PARAPHRASE: "vertical... crags... ropes and helmets... rock face"). D = mountain biking (keyword-lite "Two wheels... bike... forest trails"). Nhiễu: swimming, camping.

questions.prompt: Four people are talking about doing exercise. Match each person to the correct information.
questions.explanation:
Speaker A: I have made my peace with an unpopular truth: physical activity and I were never meant to be together. The bicycle my wife bought me rusts elegantly in the garage, the yoga mat became the cat's bed, and my single visit to her aerobics class is a story her friends still request at parties. I have stopped apologising. My heart belongs to slow breakfasts and crossword puzzles, and it is very happy there.
Speaker B: Sport entered my life through the office door, oddly enough. Our director introduced walking meetings and lunchtime badminton, and within a month I noticed the difference at my desk: the afternoon fog lifted, my proposals came out cleaner, and I stopped rereading the same paragraph four times. Now I guard my lunchtime game like an appointment with a client. Whatever it costs in sweat, it repays in finished work.
Speaker C: Every trainer I have ever had says the same thing: it gets easier. It does not. Twenty minutes into any class, my lungs demand negotiations, my legs vote to go home, and the mirror shows a tomato in sportswear. I complete every session — pride insists — but I complete it the way one completes a tax return: slowly, painfully, and with relief that it is over for another week.
Speaker D: The trick nobody told me for years: bring your people. My cousin and I turned our runs into gossip sessions, my old classmates and I have a Sunday football ritual that ends in a noisy café, and even the neighbours join our badminton evenings now. Surrounded by friendly faces, two hours of sport disappear like ten minutes. Alone, I would not last one lap of the park — together, we forget to stop.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
A = hate exercising (PARAPHRASE: "never meant to be together... stopped apologising"). B = help improve work performance (PARAPHRASE: "afternoon fog lifted... repays in finished work"). C = find exercise tiring (PARAPHRASE: "lungs demand negotiations... tomato in sportswear"). D = has fun when exercising with friends (keyword "with friendly faces... together"). Nhiễu: lose weight, alone. (Variant khác lời 02/11/14.)

questions.prompt: Four people are talking about using the Internet. Match each person to the correct information.
questions.explanation:
Speaker A: My travel budget is small, so the world comes to me through my screen instead. Friday nights are for cinema at home — I work through the classics one director at a time, and my watchlist currently holds two hundred titles. Last month it was old Japanese films; this month, French comedies with subtitles. My local cinema shows six films; my laptop shows sixty thousand. For the price of one ticket a month, I have the largest screen-room in history.
Speaker B: When my best friend moved to Australia, I thought our friendship would shrink to birthday messages. Instead, we talk more now than when she lived two streets away. Sunday morning calls over breakfast — her dinner time — the running joke chat that never sleeps, photos of everything from her new beach to my old dog. The distance is nine thousand kilometres; the conversation has never been closer. The connection is what keeps us next-door neighbours.
Speaker C: My degree happens as much online as in the lecture hall. The reading lists live on the portal, my group project shares one document across five laptops, and the deadline uploads happen at two minutes to midnight, always. When the statistics module nearly defeated me, a professor in another country rescued my grade through a free video series. Ask what the internet is to me and I will answer honestly: it is where my homework gets done.
Speaker D: I refuse to stand at a bus stop hoping anymore. Before my shoes are on, the app has told me which line is running late, where my bus is on the map, and whether the trains are behaving. When the bridge closed last month, my phone had redrawn my whole route before the radio mentioned it. My colleagues arrive complaining about their journeys. I arrive having read a book, exactly on time.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
A = watch films (PARAPHRASE: "cinema at home... watchlist... largest screen-room"). B = communicate with friends (PARAPHRASE: "we talk more now... conversation has never been closer"). C = complete assignments (keyword "homework gets done... deadline uploads"). D = find transport information (keyword-lite "which line is running late... redrawn my route"). Nhiễu: news, games. (Variant khác lời Đề 10/12.)

questions.prompt: Four people are talking about art. Match each person to the correct information.
questions.explanation:
Speaker A: I moved to this city knowing exactly one person, so I signed up for the Thursday sketching circle out of pure loneliness. Best decision of the year. Twelve strangers drawing the same bowl of fruit, laughing at the results, then staying for coffee long after the easels are packed. Two of them are now my closest friends here. I came for the pencils, honestly — I stayed for the people around the table.
Speaker B: Rainy Sundays in our house mean one thing: the paint boxes come out and my daughters take over the kitchen. We do handprint chickens, cardboard castles, glitter everywhere including the butter. The results are objectively terrible and we frame them anyway. My phone stays in another room for those two hours — just three of us, aprons on, making a happy mess. Their grandmother receives every masterpiece by post.
Speaker C: My sketchbook pays my bills — I design patterns for a textile company, so drawing is what I do from nine to six with a lunch break. Deadlines, client corrections, colour charts: the romance wears thin some weeks, and I understand now why my art teacher warned me. Still, when a stranger walks past wearing a scarf born in my sketchbook, the office desk feels worth it. Few people get paid for their doodles.
Speaker D: My easel faces the window in the spare room, and what happens there is strictly between me and the canvas. I paint when the flat is empty, show nobody, and stack the finished work behind the wardrobe. My husband stopped asking to see them years ago. It is not shyness exactly — it is that the hour is mine, the mistakes are mine, and an audience would change everything. Some pleasures work best unwitnessed.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
A = social activity (PARAPHRASE: "signed up out of loneliness... stayed for the people"). B = with children (PARAPHRASE: "my daughters take over the kitchen... three of us"). C = part of their job (PARAPHRASE: "sketchbook pays my bills... nine to six"). D = alone (PARAPHRASE: "strictly between me and the canvas... unwitnessed"). Nhiễu: competitions, online classes. (Variant khác lời Đề 04.)

questions.prompt: Four people are talking about travelling to work. Match each person to the correct information.
questions.explanation:
Speaker A: My mornings start at the stop outside the flower shop, seven-fifteen sharp. The number twelve carries me and my thoughts across town while somebody else handles the gears and the traffic lights. I have a regular seat, a regular crossword, and a nodding acquaintance with the whole upper deck. Driving would save me ten minutes, my brother insists. Those ten minutes would cost me my crossword and my calm, so the twelve keeps winning.
Speaker B: Our house runs on a military timetable — two school drop-offs, then my clinic across town by eight-thirty. Only the family car makes that mathematics work. The children argue over the radio in the back, I drink my coffee at red lights, and the parking bill at the end of each month makes my eyes water. Friends preach about buses and bicycles. With our mornings, I would need three of each.
Speaker C: Between my front door and the office lie two parks and one bridge, and I cross them all on foot, by myself, every day. Those forty minutes are the only true silence I get — no passengers, no colleagues, just my own footsteps sorting out my thoughts. Offers of lifts come daily and I decline them all politely. By the time I reach my desk, the day's problems have already been walked into order.
Speaker D: My commute doubles as my social hour. My colleague Anh lives three doors down, so we cover the thirty minutes to the office side by side, on foot, dissecting yesterday's meetings and planning our lunches. When she is away I genuinely feel the difference — the same streets, half the fun. Our boss says he can hear us laughing from his window before we reach the gate. Best part of the working day, both of us agree.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
A = travel by bus (PARAPHRASE: "the number twelve carries me... upper deck"). B = travel by car (PARAPHRASE: "family car... parking bill... red lights"). C = walk alone (PARAPHRASE: "on foot, by myself... own footsteps"). D = walk with a friend (PARAPHRASE: "cover the thirty minutes side by side, on foot"). Nhiễu: bicycle, motorbike. (Variant khác lời Đề 17.)

questions.prompt: Four people are talking about their studying habits. Match each person to the correct information.
questions.explanation:
Speaker A: My friends joke that my textbooks have frequent flyer miles. Monday finds me at the kitchen counter, Tuesday in the corner café, Wednesday on the top floor of the faculty building, and sunny days pull me onto the grass by the fountain. A single fixed desk makes my thoughts go stale within an hour; every change of scenery presses a refresh button in my head. During finals I once revised in five spots in one day — my best results ever followed.
Speaker B: One squeaking chair can end my whole session, so I have searched the city for perfect stillness and found it: the archive room on the fourth floor, past the old maps, where even footsteps apologise. Nobody speaks, phones die at the door, and the loudest event of the afternoon is a page turning. My friends revise in the noisy common room and call me a monk. Fine — this monk remembers what he reads.
Speaker C: My revision has a sound engineer: me. Soft strings under heavy reading, low steady beats when the essay needs momentum, and one particular film soundtrack reserved for the night before every exam — my little superstition. Inside the headphones, the world disappears and the words on the page stand still. Take the melodies away and my eyes slide off every paragraph. My library is wherever my playlist is.
Speaker D: The house only becomes mine after midnight, and that is when the books open. One lamp, cold tea, absolute quiet from eleven until two — my brain does its finest work while the whole street sleeps. Morning people preach their sunrise routines at me, and I have honestly tried. Before nine, I read the same sentence six times; after midnight, I read it once and own it forever.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
A = In various places (PARAPHRASE: "textbooks have frequent flyer miles... change of scenery"). B = In a quiet place (PARAPHRASE: "perfect stillness... even footsteps apologise"). C = With music (keyword-lite "headphones... melodies... playlist"). D = Late at night (keyword-lite "after midnight... eleven until two"). Nhiễu: with friends, classroom. (Variant khác lời 09/15.)

questions.prompt: Four people are talking about where they study. Match each person to the correct information.
questions.explanation:
Speaker A: I like studying somewhere with sunshine and fresh air. It doesn't have to be completely quiet — in fact, when it's too quiet I don't feel inspired at all, which is why I never study in the library or in a classroom. What I love is the park near my university. I take my books, sit on the grass, and read. Nice weather and a light breeze — what could be more perfect than that?
Speaker B: Every day I spend about an hour on the train, and that's when I do most of my homework. A lot of people ask me how anyone can concentrate on public transport, but honestly the background noise is exactly what helps me focus. Quite often I can finish an important assignment in that one hour, before I even get to campus.
Speaker C: I have a real problem with noise. I did think about the university library, but there's always something — cups clinking, people sipping coffee, and someone dragging a chair across the floor. I live with my parents, and they're usually out at work during the day, so the house is completely silent. That's when I sit on the sofa and get my assignments done.
Speaker D: I actually need background sound to concentrate. There's a coffee shop near my house that a lot of people go to, and I love the atmosphere there. I can sit in a corner with my laptop, enjoy a cup of coffee, and somehow the buzz of the place lets me focus completely on my work.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
A → In the park: "What I love is the park near my university... sit on the grass". Bẫy: A NHẮC library và classroom nhưng là để loại ("never study in the library or in a classroom").
B → On public transport: "about an hour on the train... background noise is exactly what helps me focus".
C → At home: "I live with my parents... the house is completely silent... sit on the sofa". Bẫy: C nhắc library nhưng để chê (cups clinking, chair dragging).
D → In the coffee shop: "There's a coffee shop near my house... enjoy a cup of coffee".
Nhiễu: In the library (A và C đều nhắc nhưng đều KHÔNG học ở đó), In the classroom (A loại).
👉 Mẹo: người nói nhắc một địa điểm để CHÊ rồi mới nói nơi mình học — chờ câu có "what I love / that's when I".

questions.prompt: Four people are talking about their favourite sports. Match each person to the correct information.
questions.explanation:
Speaker A: Eleven of us, one captain's armband, and a league table we take far too seriously — that is my Sunday. I have played with the same club since school, and the best part was never the goals; it is the changing-room jokes, the shared bus to away games, the feeling of covering for a teammate having a bad day. Individual training bores me stiff. Give me a squad, a formation and someone to celebrate with.
Speaker B: I grew up beside the sea, and my sport never left it. Four mornings a week I am in the pool before work, counting lengths, and summer weekends belong to the open bays — goggles, cap, and an hour of open blue. The weightlessness resets whatever the week has bent. Dry-land sports have never tempted me; if my sport does not involve getting wet, I fundamentally do not trust it.
Speaker C: Our neighbourhood has an unofficial stadium: the flat stretch of tarmac between the bakery and the parked cars. Every evening the kids and half the adults gather there — jumpers for goalposts, chalk lines redrawn weekly, matches interrupted respectfully for passing motorbikes. No membership, no schedule, no referee except the old man on the balcony. The fancy pitches charge by the hour; our tarmac has been free for thirty years.
Speaker D: My teammates have four legs. Saturday means the riding school: grooming my horse, checking tack, then jumping practice in the sand arena and long rides through the hills when weather allows. People assume the horse does all the work — let them try holding a canter for an hour. The partnership is the point: two heartbeats negotiating every fence together. No gym machine has ever nuzzled my pocket for apples afterwards.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
A = plays in a team sport (PARAPHRASE: "Eleven of us... squad, formation... teammate"). B = spends time in the water (PARAPHRASE: "in the pool... open bays... getting wet"). C = plays in the street (PARAPHRASE: "flat stretch of tarmac... jumpers for goalposts"). D = does sports with animals (PARAPHRASE: "teammates have four legs... riding school... horse"). Nhiễu: alone, running.

questions.prompt: What does the radio MC say about how the research on happiness has been covered by the media?
options: It has been accurately reported by the media
It has not been accurately reported by the media
It has been ignored completely by the media
questions.explanation:
Good morning, listeners, and welcome back to the show. Today we are talking about that big new research study on happiness — the one you have probably seen in every newspaper this week. Now, you might assume that with all this coverage, the study has been accurately reported by the media. Sadly, the opposite is true. And it certainly has not been ignored — you cannot open a website without seeing it. The problem is different: the media has not reported it accurately at all. The papers chose the most dramatic lines, cut away all the careful details, and turned a serious piece of science into shocking headlines. As a result, many of you now believe the study says money cannot buy happiness, or that married people are always happier — and it says neither of those things.
So what does the research actually tell us? Here I want to be honest about the limits of science. These studies can help people think about their personal happiness, and they certainly give the media something to discuss. But if you are hoping researchers will one day find a conclusive answer — a final formula for a happy life — that is the one thing that is unlikely ever to happen. Happiness is personal and complicated. What fills one person's life with joy leaves another person empty. The research can light the path a little, but each of us still has to walk it in our own way.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
1. Đáp án: It has not been accurately reported by the media. Bẫy: "accurately reported" bị phủ định trực tiếp, "ignored completely" bị phủ định ("you cannot open a website without seeing it").
2. Đáp án: To find a conclusive answer — điều KHÔNG THỂ xảy ra. Bẫy: "personal happiness" và "discuss in the media" đều được công nhận là khả thi; chỉ "conclusive answer" là "unlikely ever to happen".

questions.prompt: According to the radio MC, what is unlikely regarding the research on happiness??
options: To discuss happiness in the media

questions.prompt: Why hasn't he gone to college?
options: He wasn't ready to start higher education
He couldn't afford the tuition fees.
He didn't get good enough grades
questions.explanation:
People keep asking why I am not at university like the rest of my class, so let me explain properly. It is not about money — my parents had saved for years, and the tuition fees were never a problem. And it is not about my grades either; my results were actually good enough for every course I looked at. The honest reason is simpler: I just was not ready to start higher education. After thirteen years of school, my head was full and my motivation was empty. I knew that if I walked straight into a lecture hall that September, I would waste both the money and the opportunity. So I made a choice that surprised everyone: I stopped.
For the next two years I travelled through Asia and Europe, and I want to be clear about why. It was not simply for the travelling itself — the buses and the beaches were never the point. And I certainly was not trying to avoid studying; I actually read more books on the road than I ever did at school. I travelled because I wanted to become more independent. I wanted to cook my own food, fix my own problems, manage my own money in places where nobody knew me. Two years later, I can say it worked. I am starting university this autumn, and I am arriving as someone who can stand on his own feet — which, I think, is worth more than arriving two years earlier.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
1. Đáp án: He wasn't ready to start higher education. Bẫy: "tuition fees" bị phủ định ("never a problem"), "grades" bị phủ định ("good enough for every course").
2. Đáp án: To be more independent. Bẫy: "to travelling" bị gạt ("the buses and the beaches were never the point"), "to avoid studying" bị phủ định ("read more books on the road").

questions.prompt: Why did he decide to travel for 2 years?
What does this guidebook offer to its audience?
options: It focuses solely on historical landmarks.
questions.explanation:
Before my last big trip, I decided to write the travel guidebook I had always wished existed, and it has finally been published. Let me tell you what it offers. Readers expecting a book that focuses solely on historical landmarks will be surprised — the famous monuments are in there, but only as a starting point. And a few early reviewers worried it might be difficult to navigate, with all its side stories and detours. In practice, the opposite happens: those detours are the whole idea. The book offers its audience an adventure. It encourages you to leave the main square, follow a local story down a side street, try an activity no tour bus ever stops for, and come home with memories that belong only to you. Every chapter is built around one simple question: what would make this journey unforgettable?
Who is the book for? I will be honest about that too. Some booksellers assumed it caters only to seasoned travellers, the people with a hundred stamps in their passports. Others, seeing all the unusual suggestions, wondered whether the style was outdated compared with travel apps. Neither is quite right. What I have found is that the book is suitable for particular generations — it clicks most strongly with younger readers, people in their twenties and thirties who want experiences rather than checklists. Older readers often prefer a classical guide, and that is perfectly fine. A book, like a journey, does not have to be for everyone.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
1. Đáp án: It creates an adventure. Bẫy: "focuses solely on historical landmarks" bị phủ định ("only as a starting point"), "difficult to navigate" bị bác ("the opposite happens").
2. Đáp án: It is suitable for particular generations. Bẫy: "caters only to seasoned travelers" và "outdated" đều là giả định bị bác ("Neither is quite right").

questions.prompt: What is the speaker's opinion about this guidebook?
options: It caters only to seasoned travelers.
It is suitable for particular generations.

questions.prompt: What is the importance of advertising?
options: It can help reach new customers
questions.explanation:
In tonight's business class I want to talk honestly about advertising, because opinions are so divided. Small business owners always tell me the same two worries. First, that advertising will push up their product prices, since the marketing money has to come from somewhere. Second, that advertising is really just about building brand recognition — getting a logo remembered — which feels like a luxury when budgets are tight. I understand both concerns, but they miss the main point. The real importance of advertising is that it can help a business reach new customers. Your existing customers already know you; advertising is the bridge to the thousands of people who have never walked past your shop. A modest, well-aimed campaign brings in buyers you could never have met otherwise, and that — not fame, not recognition — is what pays the bills and grows the company.
Sponsorship of sports tournaments, however, deserves a separate warning. When companies hesitate, they usually give the wrong reasons. Some say sponsorship is simply too expensive, though packages now exist at every price level. Others fear it creates unfair competition, giving big brands an advantage smaller firms cannot match. Neither of those is the real danger. The true risk is that sponsorship can generate negative publicity for the sport itself. One doping scandal, one match-fixing story, one ugly incident in the stands — and the sponsor's name is printed right next to the bad news in every report. Before you put your logo on a tournament, ask yourself one question: whose mistakes am I prepared to share?

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
(Bản variant của Đề 04 bài 1 — cùng đáp án, nhiễu khác: expensive / unfair competition.)
1. Đáp án: It can help reach new customers. Bẫy: "increases the product price" và "build brand recognition" là hai lo ngại bị gạt ("they miss the main point").
2. Đáp án: They can generate negative publicity for the sport. Bẫy: "too expensive" và "unfair competition" đều bị bác ("Neither of those is the real danger").

questions.prompt: Why shouldn't we sponsor sports tournaments?
options: They can generate negative publicity for the sport

questions.prompt: What is the way to have a good sleep according to the speaker?
options: Sleeping fewer hours increases deep sleep quality
Blocking out noise and light is key
Drinking coffee before bed helps relax the mind
questions.explanation:
Welcome to our health programme. Tonight: sleep, and the strange advice people give about it. Over the years I have heard everything. One listener wrote in convinced that sleeping fewer hours actually improves the quality of deep sleep — the idea being that a tired brain sleeps harder. Another swears by a cup of coffee before bed, claiming it relaxes her mind. I have to be direct with you: neither idea survives contact with the research. Cutting your hours simply builds up exhaustion, and caffeine at night keeps the brain alert exactly when it should be winding down. What the sleep laboratories keep confirming, study after study, is far less exotic: blocking out noise and light is the key. Darkness tells the brain to produce the hormones of rest, and silence lets it stay there. Thick curtains and a closed door will do more for your sleep than any clever trick.
Now, a few words about insomnia, because the myths here are just as stubborn. It is often assumed that insomnia is caused only by physical health problems, but stress, habits and worry are equally powerful causes. And no — people with insomnia do not secretly sleep too much in the daytime; most barely rest at all. The finding that deserves your attention is this one: people cannot always recognise the symptoms of their own tiredness. They mistake exhaustion for restlessness, reach for the phone or the laptop, and push the body further from sleep — night after night, without ever understanding why.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
(Bản variant của Đề 03 bài 1 — cùng đáp án, lời khác.)
1. Đáp án: Blocking out noise and light is key. Bẫy: "sleeping fewer hours" và "coffee before bed" đều bị bác ("neither idea survives contact with the research").
2. Đáp án: People can't always recognize the symptoms of tiredness. Bẫy: "caused only by physical health problems" và "sleep too much" đều bị phủ định.

questions.prompt: What is the speaker's view on insomnia in general?
options: Insomnia is caused only by physical health problems
Most people with insomnia actually sleep too much
People can't always recognize the symptoms of tiredness

questions.prompt: What does the speaker say is a key benefit of making plans?
options: They reduce the need for communication.
questions.explanation:
People often misunderstand planning, so tonight let me clear a few things up. When I ask people what a plan gives you, I hear the same answers. Some say plans make life more predictable — you always know what happens next. Others joke that a good plan reduces the need for communication, because everyone can just read the document instead of talking. There is a small truth in both, but neither is the real prize. In my experience, the key benefit of making plans is that they help you make decisions. Planning forces you to think about your priorities in advance, so when two options appear on a busy Tuesday, you already know which one serves your goal. Instead of reacting at the last minute, you choose calmly — and you can explain to yourself exactly why. That clarity, not predictability, is what a plan is really for.
Of course, I will not pretend planning is all sunshine. Some critics claim it discourages people from taking risks, but I have found that a well-made plan actually gives you the safety to take bigger ones. Others insist planning only works in professional situations, which anyone who has planned a wedding or a family trip knows is untrue. The genuine difficulty is different: planning requires you to set yourself certain limits. A real plan means saying no — no to extra projects, no to attractive distractions, no to keeping every option open forever. Choosing your limits is uncomfortable. But without limits, what you have is not a plan; it is only a wish.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
1. Đáp án: They help you make decisions. Bẫy: "more predictable" và "reduce the need for communication" được nhắc rồi hạ cấp ("neither is the real prize").
2. Đáp án: It requires you to set yourself certain limits. Bẫy: "discourages taking risks" và "only works in professional situations" đều bị bác.

questions.prompt: What does the speaker mention as a difficulty when planning?
options: It discourages people from taking risks.
It requires you to set yourself certain limits.
It only works in professional situations.

questions.prompt: What should you do to better control your short-term spending?
options: Monitor your spending for a weekly plan
Rely on credit cards to control spending
Put aside a large sum every single day only
questions.explanation:
On today's money programme: how to actually control your spending, starting with the short term. Beginners usually try one of two things. Some rely on credit cards, believing the monthly statement will somehow keep their daily costs under control — until the statement arrives and the shock does the controlling instead. Others go to the opposite extreme and try to put aside a large sum every single day, which lasts about a week before life gets in the way. Neither works. What does work is boring and reliable: monitor your spending and build a weekly plan. Write down what you spend for seven days, look at where the money actually goes, and set a simple limit for each category the following week. Coffee, transport, evenings out — when you can see the numbers, you control them. When you cannot, they control you.
For the long term, the game changes, and so should your method. I meet people who proudly keep all their savings in one single account, where one emergency can empty everything. I meet others who refuse to make any long-term financial plans because the future feels too uncertain to think about. Both are mistakes, but the bigger mistake is trying to figure everything out alone. My strongest advice: seek guidance from someone with real experience. A relative who has paid off a house, a colleague who invested through a crisis, a qualified adviser — people like this have already paid for the lessons you are about to learn. Borrow their experience; it is the cheapest thing in finance.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
(Bản variant của Đề 08 bài 1 — nhiễu khác.)
1. Đáp án: Monitor your spending for a weekly plan. Bẫy: "credit cards" và "large sum every day" đều bị bác ("Neither works").
2. Đáp án: Seek advice from someone who have experience. Bẫy: "single account" và "avoid long-term plans" đều được nhắc là sai lầm.

questions.prompt: What should you do to better control your long-term spending?
options: Seek advice from someone who have experience
Keep all your savings in a single account
Avoid making any long-term financial plans

questions.prompt: What does the speaker say is one major strength of successful television series?
options: They focus mainly on famous actors.
They are usually shorter than films.
questions.explanation:
Television series have taken over our evenings, and as a media researcher I am often asked why some series succeed while hundreds disappear. People love simple answers. Many point to famous actors — put a film star on the poster and success follows. Others argue that series win because the episodes are shorter than films, easier to fit into a busy evening. Both factors help a launch, but they do not explain survival. Watch the series that run for five or ten years and you will find one shared strength: they maintain consistent quality throughout. The writing in season six is as sharp as in season one, the acting never relaxes, and the production standard holds from the first episode to the last. Audiences forgive a weak episode; they abandon a series that becomes reliably weaker. Consistency, not star power, is what keeps millions returning every week.
The way series are made is also changing, and it is worth understanding why. Some commentators claim streaming platforms have reduced production costs — in reality, budgets for major series have never been higher. Others complain television is becoming less creative, though this decade has produced some of the boldest storytelling ever filmed. The real change is quieter: viewer habits now influence the way series are made. Because platforms can see exactly when audiences pause, rewatch or give up, writers shape episode length, cliffhangers and season structure around real viewing data. For the first time in history, the audience is silently sitting in the writers' room.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
1. Đáp án: They maintain consistent quality throughout. Bẫy: "famous actors" và "shorter than films" được nhắc rồi hạ ("they do not explain survival").
2. Đáp án: Viewer habits influence the way that series are made. Bẫy: "reduced production costs" và "less creative" đều bị phủ định.

questions.prompt: What does the speaker suggest about changes in television production?
options: Streaming platforms have reduced production costs.
Television series are becoming less creative.
Viewer habits influence the way that series are made.

questions.prompt: What do these two famous writers have in common?
options: They both wrote in the same genre
They both were born in the same country
They both make references to each other in their work
questions.explanation:
In this week's literature lecture, we look at two writers who changed modern fiction — and at what actually connects them, because students always guess wrong. The first guess is that they wrote in the same genre. In fact, one spent his life on realistic novels while the other moved between fantasy, essays and poetry. The second guess is that they were born in the same country. Also wrong — an ocean separated their birthplaces, and they met in person only twice. What they truly share is more unusual: they make references to each other in their work. Open one writer's short stories and you will find the other's characters walking through them; read the second writer's essays and whole passages answer arguments the first had made years before. Across different languages and continents, their books carried on a lifelong conversation of mutual respect.
Now, what should you expect when you read them? Do not expect simple language and structure — anyone who tells you these are easy books has not read them. And do not assume their works are based on real events; both invented freely, even when history appears in the background. What is genuinely special is that the meaning of their work is not always easily identified. Both writers hid ideas beneath the surface — symbols, private jokes, arguments in disguise. You may finish a chapter unsure of what it truly said, return a year later, and find a different book waiting for you. That richness is exactly why we still study them.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
(Bản variant của Đề 05 bài 2 — nhiễu khác: same genre / same country.)
1. Đáp án: They both make references to each other in their work. Bẫy: "same genre" và "same country" đều bị phủ định ngay đầu.
2. Đáp án: The meaning of their work is not always easily identified. Bẫy: "simple language" và "based on real events" đều bị phủ định.

questions.prompt: What is special about their works?
options: They use simple language and structure
The meaning of their work is not always easily identified
Their works are all based on real events

questions.prompt: What should students do when choosing a career?
options: Choose the same career as their friends
Focus only on the salary offered
questions.explanation:
Welcome, final-year students. Today we talk honestly about life after graduation, starting with the biggest decision: choosing a career. Every year I watch the same two mistakes. A group of friends all apply to the same company, because choosing the same career as your friends feels safer than choosing alone. And other students scan job advertisements looking only at the salary, as if the number were the whole story. Please avoid both paths. Your friends' perfect job may be your nightmare, and a high salary in the wrong field buys you comfortable unhappiness. What you should be is flexible and open-minded. Explore industries you know nothing about, accept that your first job is a starting point rather than a destination, and let your career surprise you. The best professional lives I know were never planned in a straight line.
When you actually apply for jobs, let me correct two rumours going around. No, companies do not prefer handwritten applications — that advice died decades ago, and everything is digital now. And no, it is not true that most jobs no longer require qualifications; your degree still opens the door. But here is what you must truly pay attention to: the job market is becoming more competitive every year. For every position you want, dozens of graduates with similar degrees are applying. The degree gets you considered — it no longer gets you chosen. Skills, experience, a genuine attitude, and something that makes you memorable: build those now, before you need them.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
(Bản variant của Đề 07 bài 1 — nhiễu câu 2 khác: handwritten / no qualifications.)
1. Đáp án: Be flexible and open minded. Bẫy: "same career as friends" và "focus only on salary" là hai sai lầm bị cảnh báo.
2. Đáp án: They are becoming more competitive. Bẫy: "handwritten applications" và "no longer require qualifications" đều là tin đồn bị bác.

questions.prompt: What should students pay attention to when applying for jobs these days?
options: Most jobs no longer require any qualifications

questions.prompt: What is the speaker's opinion on this script?
options: The characters' background are not adequately explored
The dialogue is too complex for viewers
questions.explanation:
Thank you for inviting me to review this script, and I will be honest with the writing team, because that is the only useful kind of review. Let me start with what is not wrong. The setting is not the problem — the small coastal town feels completely believable, right down to the ferry timetable on the harbour wall. Nor is the dialogue too complex; the conversations are natural, and viewers will follow them without any effort. The real weakness lies with the characters: their backgrounds are not adequately explored. We watch the heroine make a life-changing decision in episode two, but we know almost nothing about her past, her family, or what shaped her fears. Without that foundation, her choices feel random rather than moving, and the audience stays at arm's length from people it should love.
Why does this keep happening to promising scripts? Because of the industry itself. Studios like to claim that today's fast production cycles increase audience engagement, and streaming platforms insist their model gives more creative freedom to writers. From where I sit, the truth is the opposite: the new industry demands have a negative influence on script production. Writers are pushed to follow whatever trend is popular this quarter, to deliver drafts on impossible deadlines, and to satisfy commercial checklists before creative ones. Under that pressure, the slow work — building a character's history layer by layer — is always the first thing cut. And it shows on the screen.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
1. Đáp án: The characters' backgrounds are not adequately explored. Bẫy: "setting unrealistic" và "dialogue too complex" đều bị phủ định ("not the problem").
2. Đáp án: The new industry demands have a negative influence. Bẫy: "increase audience engagement" và "more creative freedom" là tuyên bố của studio/platform bị bác ("the truth is the opposite").

questions.prompt: How do industries impact script production?
options: They provide more creative freedom to writers
The new industry demands have a negative influence.

questions.prompt: What does the reviewer say about the characters in the novel?

They feel realistic and emotionally engaging.

Good evening, book lovers — tonight, the novel everyone is talking about. Let me start with the characters, because opinions online are noisy. Some reviewers call them too difficult to understand; I disagree — spend ten pages with them and they open up. Others dismiss them as less important than the storyline. Wrong again, in my view. For me, the characters are the beating heart of this book: they feel realistic and emotionally engaging, people you recognise from your own kitchen table, with flaws that make you wince and hope.

And what about the novel's impact? Some academics predict it will mainly appeal to their own seminar rooms — too clever for the general public, they say. Others warn it may divide readers' opinions, with its unusual ending. I see something simpler and bigger: this book will establish the author's popularity. Mark my words — the bookshop queues, the reading clubs, the translations already being negotiated. Within a year, hers will be a household name, and this novel will be the reason.

title: Đề 26 - A Promotion Campaign for a Product

questions.prompt: What is the speaker's main criticism of the promotion campaign?
options: It makes exaggerated claims about the product.
It provides too little information about the product.
It focuses too much on the product's low price.
questions.explanation:
As a marketing consultant, I was asked to evaluate this promotion campaign, and I will share my conclusions openly. Some colleagues suggested the campaign provides too little information about the product — actually, the opposite is true; the advertisements are packed with details and specifications. Others thought it focuses too much on the low price, but price barely appears in any of the materials. My main criticism is more serious: the campaign makes exaggerated claims about the product. The advertisements promise results that are simply too good to be true — perfect skin in three days, twice the energy in a week. When promises reach that level, customers do not get excited; they get suspicious. Instead of building trust, the campaign plants doubt, and doubt is the most expensive thing a new product can create. Honest, realistic messages would convince far more people than these fireworks ever will.
There is also the question of money, and here my worry is different from what the company expects. They fear the campaign targets the wrong group of customers — it does not; the audience selection is actually quite clever. They also worry it has not attracted enough public attention, yet the view numbers are perfectly healthy. The real problem is the mathematics: the campaign costs too much compared with the return it can realistically bring. Celebrity fees, prime-time slots, three production studios — the spending is enormous, and even optimistic sales forecasts cannot cover it. A campaign can win every award in the industry and still sink the product it was meant to sell.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
1. Đáp án: It makes exaggerated claims about the product. Bẫy: "too little information" và "focuses on low price" đều bị phủ định.
2. Đáp án: It costs too much to make compared with the possible return. Bẫy: "wrong group of customers" và "not enough attention" đều bị bác ("it does not", "perfectly healthy").

questions.prompt: Why does the speaker think the campaign may not be profitable?
options: It targets the wrong group of customers.
It costs too much to make compared with the possible return.
It has not attracted enough public attention.

questions.prompt: Why is the book so popular?
options: It uses simple language to describe complex ideas
It was endorsed by a famous celebrity
questions.explanation:
Let me tell you about the book everyone in my reading club is talking about — a new biography of a famous physicist. Why has it become so popular? People guess the usual reasons. Some assume a famous celebrity endorsed it on television; nobody did. Others think it must be full of colourful illustrations; in fact it contains hardly any pictures at all. The real reason is the writing itself: the author uses simple language to describe complex ideas. Quantum physics, relativity, the strange behaviour of light — everything is explained through everyday comparisons that a reader with no scientific background can follow. My neighbour, who left school at sixteen, finished it in a weekend and then explained an experiment to me over the fence. That is what good science writing does, and the bestseller lists show how rare it is.
Of course, no successful book escapes criticism, and this one has its share. Interestingly, the critics do not complain that it focuses too much on entertainment instead of facts — the science has been checked and praised. Nor does anyone call it too short to be meaningful; at four hundred pages, it is substantial. What people actually criticize is that it is very similar to the author's previous book about the same scientist. The structure, the tone, even some of the stories repeat. Readers who loved the first book call this familiarity comfortable; reviewers call it lazy. Either way, if you have not read the earlier biography, this problem will not bother you at all.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
(Bản variant của Đề 09 bài 1, khác câu hỏi: câu 2 hỏi điểm bị CHÊ.)
1. Đáp án: It uses simple language to describe complex ideas. Bẫy: "celebrity" và "illustrations" đều bị phủ định.
2. Đáp án: It is similar to the previous book about the scientist. Bẫy: "entertainment rather than facts" và "too short" đều bị phủ định ("the critics do not complain...").
