questions.prompt: Adjusting the pace of lessons may help children learn more efficiently
questions.explanation:
W: My cousin has taken both her children out of school and is teaching them at home now.
M: Has she really? And what do you make of that?
W: Well, I've come round to it, actually. The big thing for me is speed. If a child races through maths and crawls through reading, you can simply adjust. Slow down here, speed up there. They cover far more ground that way.
M: I'm not so sure it works like that in practice. One parent, two children, no training. I think you end up moving at the pace of whoever complains loudest. It looks neat on paper and falls apart by Wednesday.
W: Hmm. Maybe with two.
M: What bothers me most, though, is the other children. They join a club on a Thursday and everyone decides that's enough. It isn't remotely the same as seeing the same faces every single morning.
W: No, I agree with you entirely there. A once-a-week meet-up doesn't replace a room full of people you can't escape from. That's where you learn to rub along with someone you don't much like.
M: Exactly. You can't timetable that.
W: You can't.
M: Mind you, for some families it genuinely is the better option. If a child is a competitive swimmer, or the family moves every eight months, or the child is simply miserable by nine in the morning, then a fixed timetable just doesn't fit their life.
W: I'd push back on that, actually. That's precisely when a child needs the routine most. Pulling them out only makes their world smaller.
M: Fair enough, though I'd still say it.
W: For me it comes down to one thing. Can the parents actually do the job? Have they got the subject knowledge, the patience, the hours? If they have, marvellous. If not, it's a slow disaster.
M: I'll accept that some parents manage it brilliantly, but I don't think that's the deciding factor at all.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
Key: Điều chỉnh tốc độ bài học giúp học hiệu quả hơn = Woman · Hoạt động nhóm thỉnh thoảng không thay thế được tiếp xúc thường xuyên với bạn học = Both · Học tại nhà có lợi cho trẻ khó theo thời khoá biểu cố định = Man · Thành công của homeschooling phụ thuộc vào khả năng dạy và hỗ trợ của gia đình = Woman
1. Adjusting the pace of lessons may help children learn more efficiently → Woman: Nữ nêu "If a child races through maths and crawls through reading, you can simply adjust." Nam phản đối: "I'm not so sure it works like that in practice."
2. Occasional group activities may not completely replace regular contact with classmates → Both: Nam nêu "They join a club on a Thursday and everyone decides that's enough. It isn't remotely the same as seeing the same faces every single morning." Nữ tán thành: "No, I agree with you entirely there."
3. Home education can benefit children whose circumstances make a fixed school timetable difficult → Man: Nam nêu "for some families it genuinely is the better option". Nữ phản đối: "I'd push back on that, actually. That's precisely when a child needs the routine most."
4. The success of homeschooling depends on whether a family can provide suitable teaching and support → Woman: Nữ nêu "Can the parents actually do the job? Have they got the subject knowledge, the patience, the hours?" Nam phản đối: "I'll accept that some parents manage it brilliantly, but I don't think that's the deciding factor at all."
👉 Mẹo: Câu cuối của nam bắt đầu bằng lời khen ("I'll accept that some parents manage it brilliantly") nhưng vế "but" mới là quan điểm thật — đáp án là Woman, không phải Both.

Why hasn't he gone to college?
options: He couldn't afford the tuition fees.
He wasn't ready to start higher education.
He didn't get good enough grades.
questions.explanation:
Today I want to tell you about one of my former students, because his story answers a question parents ask me constantly: is it a disaster if a young person delays university? Let me start with why he did not go straight to college. It was not money — his family had planned for the fees, and a scholarship covered part of them anyway. It was not his grades either; his results would have opened most doors he cared about. The honest reason is that he was not ready for higher education. Thirteen years of classrooms had drained him, and he knew that arriving at university exhausted would waste the whole opportunity. So, against plenty of advice, he stopped for a year — worked in a warehouse, travelled cheaply, lived away from home for the first time.
Now the interesting part: what did that break actually teach him? He worked part-time for months, but ask him and he will tell you the job itself taught him little beyond patience. He certainly came back appreciating education more — yet that gratitude was a side effect, not the lesson. What he really learned from the year, in his own words, was how to be more independent. He managed his own money, cooked his own disasters, fixed his own problems with nobody checking his work. When he finally entered university, professors kept mistaking him for an older student. Independence, it turns out, is not taught in any lecture hall — but it improves every lecture that follows.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
(Bản variant của gap year — góc người kể là giáo viên cũ.)
1. Đáp án: He wasn't ready to start higher education. Bẫy: "tuition fees" và "grades" đều bị phủ định.
2. Đáp án: How to be more independent. Bẫy: "working part-time" ("taught him little") và "importance of education" ("a side effect, not the lesson").

questions.prompt: What does he learn from his break from study?
Why didn't he go to college immediately after finishing school?
options: He was not ready to start higher education.
He could not afford the tuition fees.
His grades were not good enough.
questions.explanation:
People still ask why I did not go to college immediately after finishing school, so let me tell the story properly. My grades were perfectly fine — good enough for every course I applied to later. And although tuition worried my parents at first, money was never the deciding factor; we would have managed. The truth is simpler and harder to admit at eighteen: I was not ready for higher education. Years of examinations had emptied me. I could not name what I wanted to study, and starting a degree without knowing why felt like boarding a train without reading its destination. So I made the decision that shocked my teachers: I bought a backpack instead of textbooks.
For two years I travelled, and I want to be precise about my reasons, because people guess them wrong. I was not running away from studying — I read constantly on the road, more than I ever had at school. And it was never simply about seeing new places; the sightseeing grew ordinary within months. I travelled because I wanted to become more independent. I took temporary jobs in three countries, arranged my own rooms, stretched a thin budget through expensive cities, and solved every emergency with nobody to call. When I finally walked into university at twenty, I arrived knowing how to run a life — which made learning how to run a career remarkably easy.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
(Bản variant của Đề 20 bài 2 — ngôi thứ nhất, chi tiết khác.)
1. Đáp án: He was not ready to start higher education. Bẫy: "tuition fees" ("never the deciding factor") và "grades" ("perfectly fine").
2. Đáp án: To become more independent. Bẫy: "avoid studying" ("read constantly") và "simply to travel" ("grew ordinary within months").

questions.prompt: Four people are talking about their restaurant experiences. Match each person to the correct information.
questions.explanation:
Speaker A: I chose that restaurant because friends kept telling me how beautiful the decoration was, and honestly, they were right. The service was quick as well, so I have nothing bad to say about that. The problem was the food itself. The portion was so small that when I got home I had to make myself a sandwich. I walked out of there still hungry.

Speaker B: The atmosphere was lovely and the waiters brought our dishes out very quickly, so I really cannot complain about the service. What shocked me was the bill at the end of the evening. Every single dish cost far more than I had expected, and I ended up paying almost double what I had planned to spend on dinner.

Speaker C: I am allergic to peanuts, so eating out always makes me a little nervous. One of the waiters went through the entire menu with me, explained exactly how each dish was cooked, and then suggested something that was completely safe for me. He was so patient and never once made me feel like I was being difficult. That is what I remember most about the evening.

Speaker D: I did not go there for the food, to be honest, and the dishes were nothing special. I went because there was live music that night. The singer and the band were absolutely fantastic. I listened to every song carefully and I could not find a single mistake anywhere. It was, without doubt, the best evening of music I have had in years.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ---

A — was still hungry after dinner: A mở đầu bằng lời khen trang trí đẹp và phục vụ nhanh, rất dễ khiến người nghe chọn nhầm. Nhưng đó chỉ là phần dẫn; ý chính nằm ở cuối: "The portion was so small that when I got home I had to make myself a sandwich. I walked out of there still hungry."

B — paid a high price: B cũng khen phục vụ ("I really cannot complain about the service") để gài bẫy. Ý chính là hóa đơn: "Every single dish cost far more than I had expected, and I ended up paying almost double what I had planned."

C — met the helpful staff: C bị dị ứng đậu phộng, và một nhân viên đã giải thích cả thực đơn, nói rõ cách chế biến từng món rồi gợi ý món an toàn. C tự chốt: "That is what I remember most about the evening."

D — watched a perfect performance: D nói thẳng không đến vì đồ ăn ("the dishes were nothing special") mà vì nhạc sống. "I could not find a single mistake anywhere" — không một lỗi nào, tức màn trình diễn hoàn hảo.

Mẹo: cả A và B đều mở đầu bằng lời khen tích cực về trang trí và tốc độ phục vụ. Nghe câu đầu rồi chọn ngay là dính bẫy — luôn chờ tới câu chốt của mỗi người.

questions.prompt: Describe the picture.
questions.explanation: In this picture I can see a man and a woman decorating the living room of their house. The man is standing on the left, reaching up to hang a framed picture of a plant on the wall, while the woman is standing on the right and pointing at the wall, probably telling him where to put it. There are already several frames hanging above the sofa, so they seem to be creating a gallery wall. The room looks warm and comfortable, with a green sofa, cushions, a wooden coffee table and a large plant near the window. questions.prompt: Why do people like hanging pictures on their walls?
questions.explanation: I decorated my room at the beginning of this year, mainly because I wanted a fresh start. The room had looked the same for years and I was tired of it. The first thing I changed was the colour of the walls, from plain white to a soft grey, which made the room feel calmer. After that I bought a new bookshelf and arranged my books by size, and I put a few framed photographs of my family on the wall next to the door. I also replaced the old ceiling light with a warmer one. It took me a whole weekend, but the result was worth it.

questions.prompt: How often do you make changes to your room?
questions.explanation: I think there are two main reasons. Firstly, photographs and paintings carry memories and meaning. A photo of a holiday or of family members reminds people of happy moments every time they walk past it, so the house feels more personal and less like an empty space. Secondly, pictures are one of the cheapest and easiest ways to make a room look attractive. A large blank wall can look cold, but adding a few frames immediately gives the room colour and character. In addition, the pictures people choose often say something about their taste and interests, so visitors can learn about them just by looking around.

questions.prompt: Describe the picture.
questions.explanation: In the picture, I can see a young couple decorating a room in their home. The man is standing close to the wall and using a yellow hammer to knock a nail into it. Behind him, a woman is smiling and holding a large white frame, waiting to hang it once the nail is ready. They both look relaxed and happy, so I think they are enjoying the work together. Through the window on the left I can see green plants and a brick wall outside, which suggests the house has a garden. Overall it looks like an ordinary weekend at home when a couple is making their living space nicer.

questions.prompt: When was the last time you decorated your room? What did you change?
questions.explanation: The last time I decorated my room was about three months ago, just before the new school year started. I decided to change it because the room felt old and a bit boring. First, I moved my desk closer to the window so that I could get more natural light while studying. Then I bought a few small posters and hung them above my bed, and I also added a green plant on the shelf. The biggest change was the curtains, because I replaced the dark ones with light blue ones. After finishing, the room felt much brighter and more comfortable, and I found it easier to concentrate.

questions.prompt: Why do people like to change the look of their homes?
questions.explanation: I think people like to change the look of their homes for several reasons. The most common one is that living in the same space for a long time can feel boring, so even a small change such as new paint or new furniture makes the house feel fresh again. Another reason is that our needs change over time. For example, when someone starts working from home, they may need to turn a spare room into an office. Finally, a home shows who we are, so people decorate it to express their personality and to feel proud when friends or relatives come to visit.

questions.prompt: Art is only suitable for the privileged few
questions.explanation:
W: You came round that exhibition with me on Sunday and barely said a word. Go on, what did you really think of it?
M: Honestly? I felt out of place the whole time. That's the trouble with art — it's really a pastime for a small, comfortable set of people, and everyone else is expected to nod politely and move along.
W: I don't see it that way at all. The gallery was free, it was full of perfectly ordinary families, and half the room had wandered in straight from the market.
M: It still felt like a private club to me.
W: Well, that's precisely why I think the government ought to be putting a good deal more money into the arts. Funding is exactly what keeps those doors open to everybody.
M: I'm not convinced, I have to say. I'll accept that the arts do matter — I'm not a complete philistine. But public money, when hospitals are struggling? No. Let the people who enjoy it pay for it themselves.
W: And there you've just described how it ends up belonging to the wealthy.
M: Hmm. Point taken, but I'd still spend the money elsewhere. Where I do agree with you, mind you, is on the children. They ought to be meeting paintings and music when they're tiny, not at sixteen.
W: Absolutely, I couldn't agree more. My nephew was sitting drawing in a gallery at four, and it has never once occurred to him that it might not be for him.
M: That's the bit that sticks, isn't it. Start late and you feel like a visitor forever.
W: Which makes me rather hopeful, actually. I reckon in twenty years art will be far easier for ordinary people to get at than it is now — whole collections online, work turning up in shopping centres and stations.
M: I don't share your optimism there, I'm afraid. A photograph of a painting on a phone simply isn't the same thing, and the real galleries will still be sitting in the same handful of expensive cities.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
Key: Nghệ thuật chỉ hợp với số ít có đặc quyền = Man · Chính phủ nên đầu tư nhiều hơn cho nghệ thuật = Woman · Trẻ em nên tiếp xúc nghệ thuật sớm = Both · Tương lai nghệ thuật sẽ dễ tiếp cận hơn = Woman

1. Art is only suitable for the privileged few → Man: người đàn ông nêu "it's really a pastime for a small, comfortable set of people". Người phụ nữ phản đối: "I don't see it that way at all."

2. The government should invest more in arts → Woman: người phụ nữ nêu "the government ought to be putting a good deal more money into the arts". Người đàn ông phản đối: "I'm not convinced, I have to say."

3. Children should be exposed to art early → Both: người đàn ông nêu "They ought to be meeting paintings and music when they're tiny, not at sixteen.", người phụ nữ tán thành: "Absolutely, I couldn't agree more."

4. In the future, art will become more accessible → Woman: người phụ nữ nêu "in twenty years art will be far easier for ordinary people to get at than it is now". Người đàn ông phản đối: "I don't share your optimism there, I'm afraid."

👉 Mẹo: Ý 2 có bẫy "I'll accept that the arts do matter" — nghe như hai người cùng phe, nhưng người đàn ông bác bỏ đúng chuyện tiền ngân sách; ngược lại ở ý 3 anh ta chủ động đồng ý thật, đây mới là ý Both duy nhất.

questions.prompt: There is too much information on the Internet
questions.explanation:
M: Have you read that piece about how the Internet has changed us? It's been on my mind all week.
W: Go on then. Though my first thought is always the same: there's simply far too much material sitting out there. Nobody could ever get through a fraction of it.
M: I'm not so sure about that, to be honest. You can't really have too much of it. It's just there, quietly waiting. Nothing is forcing you to open all of it.
W: Fair enough, but it does leave me feeling swamped before I've even started.
M: Well, here's what I would say. Digging out something decent takes proper technique. You have to know how to word a search, where to look, when to give up on a page.
W: Exactly, I agree with you there completely. Half the people in my office type in a whole sentence and then wonder why they get rubbish back.
M: Right. It's a skill like any other, and almost nobody sits down and teaches it.
W: Nobody teaches it at school either, which is odd.
M: Here's my bigger worry, though. I reckon all this has genuinely reshaped the way our minds work. We skim, we jump about, we never follow an argument through to the end any more.
W: I don't see it that way, I'm afraid. I'll accept that our habits have shifted, but our actual thinking? That's a huge leap. People were easily distracted long before any of this existed.
M: Hmm. I still think something has changed in here.
W: What I will say is that youngsters now have almost no tolerance for waiting. My nephew sighs if a video takes three seconds to load.
M: Oh, I completely agree with you on that one. I see it constantly at work. If a page doesn't open instantly, they've already given up and wandered off.
W: It's the on-demand culture, isn't it. Everything now, or not at all.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
Key: Quá nhiều thông tin trên mạng = Woman · Tìm thông tin cần kỹ năng = Both · Internet ảnh hưởng cách ta suy nghĩ = Man · Internet khiến giới trẻ kém kiên nhẫn = Both
1. There is too much information on the Internet → Woman: Nữ nêu "there's simply far too much material sitting out there". Nam phản đối rõ: "I'm not so sure about that, to be honest. You can't really have too much of it."
2. Finding information on the Internet requires skills → Both: Nam nêu "Digging out something decent takes proper technique." Nữ tán thành: "Exactly, I agree with you there completely."
3. The use of the Internet affects the way we think. → Man: Nam nêu "I reckon all this has genuinely reshaped the way our minds work." Nữ phản đối: "I don't see it that way, I'm afraid. I'll accept that our habits have shifted, but our actual thinking? That's a huge leap."
4. The Internet makes young people less patient. → Both: Nữ nêu "youngsters now have almost no tolerance for waiting". Nam tán thành: "Oh, I completely agree with you on that one."
👉 Mẹo: Bẫy nằm ở ý 3 — nữ nói "I'll accept that our habits have shifted" nghe như đồng ý, nhưng ngay sau đó bác bỏ kết luận ("but our actual thinking? That's a huge leap"), nên đáp án là Man chứ không phải Both.

questions.prompt: The internet makes education more accessible
questions.explanation:
Woman: That looks interesting. What are you up to?
Man: Oh, I just came across this interesting report about universities and how they're evolving in the digital age. It talked about the impact of the internet, student experiences, and even competition between institutions. It got me thinking, there's so much to unpack when it comes to how education is changing, don't you think?
Woman: Yeah, I've been reading about similar things lately. It's amazing how different opinions can be on what makes a good university experience. I think we can both agree that the internet has made education more accessible. It's great how people from different backgrounds can now access high-quality education without being physically on campus.
Man: Absolutely, I agree with that. It's a game-changer for those who can't afford to relocate or attend in person. But I still believe that social interactions are a crucial part of university life. Online education can never truly replace the friendships, group work, and networking that happen in a physical setting.
Woman: Hmm, I'm not so sure. While social interactions can be important, I think online learning allows students to focus more on their studies without all the distractions of campus life. Not everyone benefits from that kind of environment.
Man: I see your point, but I think universities provide a unique space for students to develop their social skills alongside their academic ones. Another thing I'm really in favor of is encouraging competition between universities. When universities compete, it drives innovation and pushes them to offer better resources.
Woman: I disagree there. Competition can sometimes lead to universities focusing too much on rankings and flashy features instead of the quality of education. It can become more about marketing than genuine improvement.
Man: That's a fair concern. But competition also forces universities to constantly improve, which can benefit students in the long run. What about the diversity in curricula? I'm curious where you stand on that.
Woman: To be honest, I'm not a fan of having too many options in the curriculum. A diverse curriculum sounds good in theory, but it can overwhelm students and take away from the depth of learning in core subjects.
Man: I can see that perspective, but I think having variety gives students the flexibility to explore different fields. It can be especially beneficial for those who are unsure of their career paths.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
1. Người phụ nữ nói: "I think we can both agree that the internet has made education more accessible." Người nam trả lời: "Absolutely, I agree with that."
2. Người nam nhấn mạnh: "But I still believe that social interactions are a crucial part of university life." (Tương tác xã hội là thành phần quan trọng đối với đời sống đại học).
3. Người phụ nữ bày tỏ quan điểm: "To be honest, I'm not a fan of having too many options in the curriculum. A diverse curriculum sounds good in theory, but it can overwhelm students..."
4. Người nam ủng hộ ý tưởng này: "Another thing I'm really in favor of is encouraging competition between universities."

3. Chọn A vì A nói học sinh, sinh viên được nghỉ cuối tuần và nên tham gia; việc này rất bổ ích cho các em. => Tình nguyện quan trọng với học sinh, sinh viên.
4. Chọn D vì D nói con trai mơ thành nhà sinh vật học nên việc dọn công viên rất có ích cho cháu: "cleaning up this park will be very helpful for my son". => Có lợi cho công việc tương lai.
5. Chọn C vì C nói sẽ hỏi em trai và bạn của em trai xem có thể giúp không. => Sẽ nhờ người khác hỗ trợ.
6. Chọn B vì B nói hồ, rừng địa phương và hai bên đường cũng cần được dọn. => Các khu vực xung quanh cũng cần làm sạch.
7. Chọn C vì C nói công viên có cảnh quan tự nhiên, khác với thành phố bụi bặm. => Là nơi đẹp để thư giãn.

questions.prompt: Community design can influence people's behavior.
questions.explanation:
Woman: Hey, have you noticed how much effort cities are putting into improving neighborhood layouts these days?
Man: You mean things like parks, shared courtyards, bike lanes? Yeah, I've seen that. I suppose it does make people interact more.
Woman: Exactly. It's fascinating how the way a space is designed can actually change how people relate to each other. When a place feels open and welcoming, people naturally feel more inclined to talk, connect, even help one another.
Man: I never used to think much about it, but after I moved last year, I noticed how different things felt. The new place has a community garden, and I ended up chatting with neighbors I might never have met otherwise.
Woman: That's what I mean! I'm really hopeful that more cities will keep this trend going. Man: Yeah, I'm all for it. Still, I think there's more to forming bonds than just the environment. Even in the most community-friendly setting, you can't expect people to feel a strong sense of connection right away.
Woman: That's fair. Though I believe that it happens more quickly than we think. When someone joins a new team or starts volunteering, they often start to feel like part of the group sooner than expected. You know, like a "natural process".
Man: Maybe in some cases. But in my experience, when you move to a new town or start over in a completely different setting, it takes a while before you really feel integrated. It's a gradual growth, not something that just clicks.
Woman: Speaking of integration, I think community isn't limited to a specific context. Whether it's colleagues at work or friends outside, the essence is the same-feeling seen, supported, and involved, whichever the size or type of group doesn't matter as much as the emotional connection people have within it
Man: That's an interesting point. I'm not so sure I'm the best person to judge that. I've mostly kept my work life and personal life pretty separate. Though these days, a lot of those connections don't even happen face-to-face anymore.
Woman: Totally. Online platforms are redefining what community means. I've seen people build strong support networks without ever meeting in person.
Man: Same here. I joined a language exchange group online, and it's actually one of the most engaging communities I've been part of. Technology really has changed the game.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
1. Người phụ nữ nói: "...the way a space is designed can actually change how people relate to each other." Người nam cũng nhận thấy điều đó qua trải nghiệm của mình: "I noticed how different things felt... ended up chatting with neighbors..."
2. Người nam cho rằng kết nối cần thời gian: "it takes a while before you really feel integrated. It's a gradual growth, not something that just clicks."
3. Người phụ nữ nói: "Whether it's colleagues at work or friends outside, the essence is the same—feeling seen, supported, and involved..."
4. Người phụ nữ nhận xét: "Online platforms are redefining what community means." Người nam đồng ý hoàn toàn: "Same here. ... Technology really has changed the game."

Future generations may struggle with information overload caused by technology.
questions.explanation:
Man: I've been thinking about how future generations might really struggle with all the information technology throws at them. With the sheer volume of data available, it's easy to see how they could feel overwhelmed and unsure of what to trust.
Woman: I get that, but I actually think this technological revolution is beneficial for our economy. It's opened up new job opportunities and streamlined many industries, driving growth in ways we haven't seen before.
Man: I understand your point, but we also need to consider the potential downsides. As automation increases, many traditional jobs could disappear and not everyone will be able to transition to new roles. We have to ensure that the workforce is prepared for these changes. Woman: Still, we should recognize that no matter how advanced they get, computers can't replicate the complexity of the human brain. Our ability to think critically and empathize is irreplaceable, and we need to nurture those qualities even as we embrace new technologies. Man: I see. However, while we're advancing I believe we both see the need for stronger protections around individual privacy. As where more on the internet safeguarding personal information becomes increasingly important.
Woman: Exactly! Protecting privacy is essential in this digital age. We have to ensure that people maintain control over their data balancing innovation with the right to privacy.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
1. Người nam bày tỏ lo lắng việc trẻ em bị quá tải thông tin: "future generations might really struggle with all the information technology throws at them."
2. Người phụ nữ khẳng định sự chuyển tiếp công nghệ giúp tạo sự tăng trưởng kinh tế: "I actually think this technological revolution is beneficial for our economy."
3. Người phụ nữ so sánh công nghệ và con người: "we should recognize that no matter how advanced they get, computers can't replicate the complexity of the human brain."
4. Người nam nói: "I believe we both see the need for stronger protections around individual privacy." Người phụ nữ đáp trả đồng thuận: "Exactly! Protecting privacy is essential in this digital age."

questions.prompt: The technological revolution is good for the economy.
No computer is superior to the human brain.
More should be done to protect individual privacy.
Housing space is more important than farming space.
questions.explanation:
M: Have you seen they're turning that old car park on Bridge Street into allotments for the neighbourhood?
W: I have, and honestly I think it's completely the wrong call. In a city this crowded, putting up flats has to come before growing vegetables. Homes win every single time.
M: I don't see it that way, I'm afraid. We've got acres of derelict land sitting empty, and it doesn't all have to become housing.
W: Well, you try telling that to the people sitting on the council waiting list.
M: Fair point, I'll grant you. But I'll be honest with you, the whole idea of growing food in the middle of a city really appeals to me.
W: Really? I find it all a bit twee, if I'm honest. A few tomatoes on a rooftop isn't my idea of a good weekend.
M: Each to their own, I suppose. There's a more serious side to it, though. Cities are going to need far more of their food produced close by than they currently get.
W: I'm not convinced by that at all. The supply chains work perfectly well as they are. The lorries arrive every morning and the shelves are full by eight.
M: Until fuel prices double, perhaps. Then everyone will suddenly be very interested in the field down the road.
W: Possibly. I'll grant you that much, but it feels an awfully long way off to me.
M: Well, what I think we'd both happily accept is that a scheme like this creates work locally. Growers, deliveries, little shops selling the produce on the corner.
W: Yes, I'll agree with you there without any argument. Any project on that scale brings jobs and money into the area, whatever I happen to think of the vegetables themselves.
M: Exactly. Even a sceptic can see the economics stacking up nicely.
W: Quite. Just don't ask me to dig anything.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
Key: Không gian nhà ở quan trọng hơn không gian trồng trọt = Woman · Nông nghiệp đô thị hấp dẫn = Man · Thành phố cần nhiều thực phẩm hơn = Man · Nông nghiệp đô thị có lợi cho kinh tế đô thị = Both

1. Housing space is more important than farming space. → Woman: người phụ nữ nêu "In a city this crowded, putting up flats has to come before growing vegetables. Homes win every single time." Người đàn ông phản đối: "I don't see it that way, I'm afraid. We've got acres of derelict land sitting empty, and it doesn't all have to become housing."

2. Urban farming is appealing. → Man: người đàn ông nêu "the whole idea of growing food in the middle of a city really appeals to me." Người phụ nữ phản đối: "Really? I find it all a bit twee, if I'm honest."

3. Cities need more food. → Man: người đàn ông nêu "Cities are going to need far more of their food produced close by than they currently get." Người phụ nữ phản đối: "I'm not convinced by that at all. The supply chains work perfectly well as they are."

4. Urban farming will benefit the urban economy. → Both: người đàn ông nêu "a scheme like this creates work locally", người phụ nữ đồng ý rõ: "Yes, I'll agree with you there without any argument. Any project on that scale brings jobs and money into the area, whatever I happen to think of the vegetables themselves."

👉 Mẹo: Bẫy ở ý 3 — câu "Possibly. I'll grant you that much" của người phụ nữ là nhượng bộ lịch sự về giá nhiên liệu, không phải đồng ý rằng thành phố cần thêm thực phẩm, nên vẫn là Man.

questions.prompt: Children are interested in tech-based learning
questions.explanation:
Man: I've been considering the way children and teenagers use technology these days. Many of them seem eager to learn through devices such as computers, tablets, and various educational applications.
Woman: I think so too. Digital learning activities often make lessons more engaging, and students are generally enthusiastic about using technological tools in the classroom.
Man: On the other hand, technology may have a negative impact on communication skills. Because some children spend a great deal of time online, they can struggle to interact with others in person.
Woman: That's a good point. Although they may be comfortable communicating through texts or online messages, they sometimes lack confidence when having face-to-face conversations.
Man: Another concern is that a lot of parents are unsure how to control or monitor their children's use of technology. Families may need more guidance to establish suitable boundaries and rules at home.
Woman: I understand that concern, but I also think children are capable of managing their own online behaviour. If they receive the right education and support, they can learn when to limit their screen time and how to communicate appropriately and responsibly on the internet.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
1. Người nam nói trẻ em "seem eager to learn through devices such as computers, tablets, and various educational applications." Người phụ nữ đồng tình: "I think so too. Digital learning activities often make lessons more engaging."
2. Người nam nêu: "they can struggle to interact with others in person." Người phụ nữ đồng ý: "That's a good point... they sometimes lack confidence when having face-to-face conversations."
3. Người nam lo ngại: "a lot of parents are unsure how to control or monitor their children's use of technology. Families may need more guidance..."
4. Người phụ nữ phản biện: "I also think children are capable of managing their own online behaviour. If they receive the right education and support, they can learn when to limit their screen time."

questions.prompt: Cultural Exchange
questions.explanation:
1. Heading: Redefining Global Cultural Understanding Why this answer: Chọn tiêu đề này vì đoạn văn cho thấy quá trình giao thoa văn hóa trong bối cảnh toàn cầu hóa đang thay đổi cách con người hiểu về văn hóa trên toàn thế giới. Vietnamese translation: Toàn cầu hóa đã thay đổi cách con người hiểu về văn hóa trên khắp thế giới. Ngày nay, giao lưu văn hóa cho phép mỗi cá nhân khám phá phong tục, niềm tin và giá trị vượt ra ngoài xã hội của chính mình. Quá trình này giúp định hình lại cách hiểu văn hóa toàn cầu bằng cách khuyến khích sự cởi mở, tính hiếu kỳ và nhận thức sâu sắc hơn về sự đa dạng trong đời sống hiện đại.
2. Heading: Encouraging Cross-Cultural Festivals Why this answer: Chọn tiêu đề này vì đoạn văn nói về các sự kiện quốc tế kết hợp âm nhạc, ẩm thực, nghệ thuật và truyền thống từ nhiều quốc gia để tôn vinh sự đa dạng và kết nối. Vietnamese translation: Nhiều cộng đồng hiện nay tổ chức các sự kiện quốc tế để tôn vinh sự đa dạng và sự kết nối. Những buổi gặp gỡ này quy tụ âm nhạc, ẩm thực, nghệ thuật và truyền thống từ nhiều quốc gia khác nhau. Bằng cách khuyến khích các lễ hội giao thoa văn hóa, xã hội tạo ra cơ hội để mọi người trân trọng sự khác biệt, tăng cường quan hệ và thúc đẩy sự hòa hợp giữa các nhóm văn hóa.
3. Heading: Promoting Language Exchange Programs Why this answer: Chọn tiêu đề này vì đoạn văn nhấn mạnh rằng ngôn ngữ là công cụ mạnh mẽ để kết nối văn hóa và các chương trình trao đổi ngôn ngữ giúp người học vừa luyện giao tiếp vừa mở rộng hiểu biết văn hóa. Vietnamese translation: Ngôn ngữ là một trong những công cụ mạnh mẽ nhất để kết nối văn hóa. Trường học và các tổ chức thường tạo cơ hội để học sinh, sinh viên luyện nói với người đến từ các quốc gia khác. Bằng cách thúc đẩy các chương trình trao đổi ngôn ngữ, cộng đồng giúp người học cải thiện kỹ năng giao tiếp, đồng thời phát triển nhận thức văn hóa sâu sắc hơn và tình bạn quốc tế.
4. Heading: Overemphasis on Commercial Tourism Why this answer: Chọn tiêu đề này vì đoạn văn cảnh báo rằng truyền thống đôi khi bị điều chỉnh để thu hút khách du lịch và tăng lợi nhuận, từ đó làm giảm tính chân thực của văn hóa. Vietnamese translation: Mặc dù du lịch có thể hỗ trợ giao lưu văn hóa, nó đôi khi cũng tạo ra những tác động tiêu cực. Ở nhiều nơi, các truyền thống bị thay đổi để thu hút du khách và tăng lợi nhuận thay vì giữ lại ý nghĩa nguyên gốc. Sự nhấn mạnh quá mức vào du lịch thương mại có thể làm giảm tính chân thực và khiến các thực hành văn hóa trở thành màn trình diễn hơn là sự biểu đạt bản sắc thực sự.
5. Heading: Concerns About Cultural Preservation Why this answer: Chọn tiêu đề này vì đoạn văn nêu rõ nỗi lo rằng những phong tục truyền thống có thể mai một dần và thế hệ trẻ có thể mất liên kết với di sản địa phương. Vietnamese translation: Khi các nền văn hóa tương tác với nhau thường xuyên hơn, một số người lo sợ các phong tục truyền thống sẽ dần biến mất. Thế hệ trẻ có thể tiếp nhận lối sống nước ngoài và mất đi sự gắn kết với di sản địa phương. Những lo ngại về bảo tồn văn hóa này đã khiến nhiều cộng đồng chủ động bảo vệ ngôn ngữ, nghi lễ và các giá trị lịch sử của mình cẩn thận hơn trước đây.
6. Heading: Building Mutual Respect Among Communities Why this answer: Chọn tiêu đề này vì đoạn văn cho thấy khi con người tìm hiểu truyền thống và niềm tin của nhau, họ thường thông cảm hơn và bớt phán xét hơn, từ đó xây dựng sự tôn trọng lẫn nhau. Vietnamese translation: Giao lưu văn hóa có thể đóng vai trò quan trọng trong việc tạo ra những mối quan hệ hòa bình giữa các nhóm khác nhau. Khi con người tìm hiểu về truyền thống và niềm tin của nhau, họ thường trở nên thấu hiểu hơn và bớt phán xét hơn. Theo cách đó, các hoạt động văn hóa góp phần xây dựng sự tôn trọng lẫn nhau giữa các cộng đồng và khuyến khích sự hợp tác lâu dài.
7. Heading: Focusing on Authentic Cultural Experiences Why this answer: Chọn tiêu đề này vì đoạn văn nói rằng du khách hiện nay muốn trải nghiệm kết nối sâu hơn, tiếp cận đời sống và truyền thống địa phương thật hơn thay vì chỉ đi ngắm cảnh. Vietnamese translation: Du khách hiện đại ngày càng tìm kiếm những kết nối sâu sắc hơn thay vì chỉ tham quan đơn thuần. Thay vì đến những điểm đông đúc, họ muốn trải nghiệm đời sống hàng ngày, truyền thống địa phương và sự tương tác có ý nghĩa với người dân bản địa. Khi tập trung vào các trải nghiệm văn hóa chân thực, du lịch có thể trở nên tôn trọng hơn, mang tính giáo dục hơn và có giá trị hơn cho cả du khách lẫn cộng đồng sở tại.

questions.prompt: Media exaggerates the benefits of the programme
questions.explanation:
M: There have been so many volunteer events recently that it's almost impossible not to talk about them on my podcast.
W: Fair enough.
M: First of all, these volunteer groups have become incredibly popular — the media everywhere is covering them. But honestly, I think what these events actually achieve is being blown out of proportion.
W: I agree with you there. The press keeps saying these groups are going to change the whole world and fix the environment, when in fact they only deal with a tiny part of the problem. There are plenty of other issues going on.
M: Like littering — for me that's one of the biggest problems in society today. People assume dropping one wrapper has a tiny effect, but it all adds up until it becomes a huge issue.
W: Hmm, I'm not sure it's as serious as you make out — there are far bigger things to worry about. But let's leave that to one side. What I want to say is that these volunteers are getting a lot of publicity — interviews, posts, articles — and I think that's a good thing. Whether they do it for fame, for personal reasons or for the community, it makes no difference to the result: it still draws more people into volunteering.
M: I don't see it that way. If people who volunteer for their own benefit get all that publicity, it doesn't just attract more volunteers — it can backfire. You end up with people volunteering to boost their ego rather than to help the community, and that does change what the programme achieves.
W: OK, let's go back to the litter problem, since you feel so strongly about it. What do you think should be done?
M: The best approach is to introduce penalties. Other countries have very tough punishments — heavy fines, even prison — and the figures show those countries have far lower rates of littering.
W: I'll accept the figures, but I don't think punishment is the most appropriate answer here. A fine changes behaviour for a week and then people forget. What actually works is education and making it easy to do the right thing — more bins, clearer signs, campaigns in schools. Change the habit, not just the price of breaking it.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
Key theo đề thật 16/9: Media exaggerates = Both · Littering main problem = Man · Volunteers' motivations don't affect the outcome = Woman · Punishment most effective = Man.
1. Media exaggerates the benefits → Both: anh nói "blown out of proportion", cô "I agree with you there".
2. Littering is a major problem → The man: "one of the biggest problems in society today". Cô không đồng ý: "I'm not sure it's as serious as you make out".
3. Motivations do not affect the outcome → The woman: "Whether they do it for fame, for personal reasons or for the community, it makes no difference to the result". Anh phản bác: "it can backfire... that does change what the programme achieves".
4. Punishment is the most effective way → The man: "The best approach is to introduce penalties". Cô: "I don't think punishment is the most appropriate answer".
👉 Mẹo: câu 2 và 3 là bẫy — người nói đồng ý với SỐ LIỆU nhưng không đồng ý với KẾT LUẬN thì vẫn không phải Both.

Exhibitions should be different and diverse
questions.explanation:
M: So the new cultural centre opens next month. Has anyone told you what's actually going in it?
W: Only scraps. But if I had any say, I'd want the exhibitions changing all the time. Folk art one month, photography the next, then something borrowed from abroad. A proper mixture.
M: I'm not so sure about that, honestly. A place like that needs one clear identity. If you chop and change every few weeks, nobody ever works out what the building is for.
W: Oh, I'd find that deadly dull. Same cases, same labels, year after year.
M: Well, we see it differently. What does genuinely worry me is that the old customs are quietly fading away. Hardly anyone under thirty knows the words to anything any more.
W: I agree with you there, completely. My grandmother could name every single step of the harvest dance. My sister's children have never even heard of it.
M: Exactly. It slips away in one generation and then it's gone.
W: It really does.
M: Which is why I'd say the village festivals themselves will have vanished within ten or fifteen years. Finished.
W: Hang on, that's far too gloomy. I'll grant you the crowds are smaller than they were, but disappear? No. They shrink, they change shape, and then somebody's daughter revives them. I don't see it that way at all. Ours died out in the eighties and it's back now, bigger than ever.
M: And the other thing is the classroom. It's the schools that will decide what the next lot grow up caring about. Put it on the timetable and you've saved it.
W: I really don't think so. Children take their values from home, not from a lesson on a wet Tuesday afternoon. A school can tick a box; it can't make anybody care.
M: I'd still back the teachers over the parents, every time. Give me one hour a week on that timetable and I'd change a whole generation.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
Key: Triển lãm nên đa dạng, luôn đổi mới = Woman · Phong tục truyền thống đang mất dần ý nghĩa = Both · Lễ hội địa phương sẽ biến mất = Man · Trường học quan trọng với thế hệ sau = Man
1. Exhibitions should be different and diverse → Woman: Nữ nêu "I'd want the exhibitions changing all the time. Folk art one month, photography the next". Nam phản đối: "I'm not so sure about that, honestly. A place like that needs one clear identity."
2. Traditional customs are gradually losing their significance → Both: Nam nêu "the old customs are quietly fading away". Nữ tán thành: "I agree with you there, completely."
3. Local festivals will disappear in the near future → Man: Nam nêu "the village festivals themselves will have vanished within ten or fifteen years". Nữ phản đối: "I'll grant you the crowds are smaller than they were, but disappear? No."
4. Schools are important in shaping future generations → Man: Nam nêu "It's the schools that will decide what the next lot grow up caring about." Nữ phản đối: "I really don't think so. Children take their values from home, not from a lesson on a wet Tuesday afternoon."
👉 Mẹo: Ở ý 3 nữ nhượng bộ một nửa ("I'll grant you the crowds are smaller") rồi mới bác bỏ — nghe thấy "I'll grant you" đừng vội chọn Both, hãy nghe hết câu sau chữ "but".

Four people are talking about their exercise preferences. Match each person to the correct information.
questions.explanation:
Speaker A: I've always been drawn to outdoor activities, especially those that get my heart racing. While some of my friends prefer running or hiking, I find nothing more exciting than mountain biking. I love the challenge of rough terrains and feeling the wind rush by as I go downhill. It's also a great way to explore nature and stay fit. I try to hit the trails at least a few times a month because it's such a thrilling experience for me. It's become my go-to form of exercise whenever I have the time. Speaker B: When it comes to staying active, I've tried lots of different things, but I've found that I get the most out of a good jog. It's a great way to keep my energy levels up, and I enjoy how it clears my mind. I usually jog around the park or along the river near my home. It's not too fast, but it still gets my heart pumping and helps me unwind. I try to fit it into my routine as often as I can, even if it's just for twenty minutes. Speaker C: I prefer something more low-key and calming when it comes to exercise. I'm not really into intense activities like running or biking. Instead, I find walking to be the perfect balance for me. It allows me to relax while still staying active. Whether it's in the park or just around my neighborhood, I try to get my steps in every day. It's also a nice way to clear my head after a long day at work. Speaker D: I've been involved in different sports over the years, but one thing that stands out for me is horse riding. There's something about being with horses that feels both calming and exciting. Riding through open fields or along forest paths is an amazing way to stay active. It's not just a workout, but also a chance to connect with animals and nature. I try to go riding whenever I have a free weekend. It's definitely my favorite way to keep fit.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ---
• Going for a run → Speaker B: "I get the most out of a good jog", chạy quanh công viên hoặc dọc bờ sông.
• Mountain biking → Speaker A: "nothing more exciting than mountain biking", thích địa hình gồ ghề và lao xuống dốc.
• Walking → Speaker C: "I find walking to be the perfect balance", thích vận động nhẹ nhàng, đi bộ mỗi ngày.
• Horse riding → Speaker D: "one thing that stands out for me is horse riding", cưỡi ngựa qua đồng và đường rừng.
• Hiking và Swimming là 2 phương án nhiễu — hiking chỉ được A nhắc để LOẠI ("some of my friends prefer running or hiking"), còn swimming không ai nói.

questions.prompt: Housing space is more important than farming space.
questions.explanation:
M: Did you see they're turning that old multi-storey car park into growing plots?
W: I did, and I think it's a shocking waste, frankly. In a city this crammed, putting up somewhere for people to live matters far more than finding room for rows of lettuce.
M: I don't see it that way at all. I'll grant you that housing is desperately tight, but you're talking about a rooftop nobody could put flats on anyway. It isn't one or the other.
W: In practice it usually is, though. Somebody always has to choose.
M: Well, I'll be honest with you, I find the whole idea rather lovely. Tomatoes on a warehouse roof, herbs growing over a bus depot — there's something genuinely charming about the whole business.
W: It leaves me completely cold, I'm afraid. To me it looks like a hobby for people with plenty of spare time and very little to worry about.
M: That's a bit harsh. Anyway, charm aside, there's a hard practical case as well. Towns are simply going to need far more food than they can currently lay their hands on, and it has to come from somewhere.
W: I'm not convinced that's the real problem, though. We already produce more than enough — a third of it ends up in the bin. Growing a few extra courgettes on a roof doesn't fix any of that.
M: Fair enough, but the supply lines into cities are terribly fragile.
W: Maybe so. There is one thing I'll happily give it, mind you — a proper network of city farms would put real money back into the area. Jobs, shops buying produce grown half a mile away, that sort of thing.
M: Exactly, I agree with you entirely there. Every pound stays in the neighbourhood instead of disappearing off to some enormous distributor two hundred miles away.
W: That's the bit I'd put funding behind, then. Just not at the expense of somebody's flat.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
Key: Không gian ở quan trọng hơn không gian canh tác = Woman · Nông nghiệp đô thị hấp dẫn = Man · Thành phố cần thêm thực phẩm = Man · Nông nghiệp đô thị có lợi cho kinh tế đô thị = Both

1. Housing space is more important than farming space. → Woman: người phụ nữ nêu "putting up somewhere for people to live matters far more than finding room for rows of lettuce". Người đàn ông phản đối: "I don't see it that way at all."

2. Urban farming is appealing. → Man: người đàn ông nêu "I find the whole idea rather lovely". Người phụ nữ phản đối: "It leaves me completely cold, I'm afraid."

3. Cities need more food. → Man: người đàn ông nêu "Towns are simply going to need far more food than they can currently lay their hands on". Người phụ nữ phản đối: "I'm not convinced that's the real problem, though."

4. Urban farming will benefit the urban economy. → Both: người phụ nữ nêu "a proper network of city farms would put real money back into the area", người đàn ông tán thành: "Exactly, I agree with you entirely there."

👉 Mẹo: Chỗ dễ sập bẫy nhất là "I'll grant you that housing is desperately tight" (ý 1) — nghe như đồng ý nhưng là nhượng bộ một nửa rồi bác kết luận, nên ý 1 vẫn là Woman. Ý 3 cũng vậy: người đàn ông nêu, người phụ nữ chỉ công nhận một phần rồi phản đối.

Young people are more into politics
questions.explanation:
Woman: Politics have been a very common topic lately. I've noticed that young people are becoming much more interested in politics lately. It's great to see them engaging in discussions and activism.
Man: I completely agree! It's refreshing to see younger generations taking a stand on important issues.
Woman: I also think social media plays a big role in this. Platforms like Twitter and Instagram help spread political information quickly and connect people with similar interests.
Man: Actually I believe people are becoming better informed about politics not because of social media but through traditional news sources. Many are actively seeking information to understand the issues better.
Woman: I see your point, but I think social media has a unique impact. It allows for diverse voices to be heard that might not be represented in mainstream media.
Man: It's also encouraging to see more women pursuing careers in politics. It brings different perspectives to the table, which is essential for a balanced approach to governance.
Woman: Absolutely! More representation is always a positive step forward.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
1. Người phụ nữ nhận xét: "I've noticed that young people are becoming much more interested in politics lately." Người nam hoàn toàn đồng ý: "I completely agree!"
2. Người phụ nữ cho rằng mạng xã hội có tác động: "I also think social media plays a big role in this. Platforms like Twitter and Instagram help spread political information..."
3. Người nam không nghĩ đó là do MXH mà do tin tức truyền thống: "Actually I believe people are becoming better informed about politics not because of social media but through traditional news sources."
4. Người nam nói: "It's also encouraging to see more women pursuing careers in politics." Người phụ nữ đồng tình mạnh mẽ: "Absolutely! More representation is always a positive step forward."

Auditions are most important for an actor's career.
questions.explanation:
Man: You know, I've always believed that auditions are the most important part of an actor's career. I mean, that's where the magic happens. It doesn't matter how great you are in rehearsals or even in the final performance, if you can't nail that audition, you're not getting anywhere.
Woman: Yeah, but it's not just about the audition. I've seen actors who can absolutely shine when they're given the right material to work with. Strong scripts really bring out the best in them. If the writing's weak, even a talented actor might struggle to connect. I think actors respond best when they feel inspired by what's on the page.
Man: That's true, but whether it's a strong script or a weak one, they still have to nail that first audition to even get the chance to perform, right?
Woman: Sure, the audition is key, but once they're in, the script can make or break their performance. It's kind of a balance between both.
Man: I agree with that. But I also think there's a huge difference between theater acting and screen acting. The two require completely different skill sets. In theater, you've got to project and be larger than life, whereas on screen, it's all about subtlety, keeping everything smaller and more contained.
Woman: Absolutely! They're such different worlds. The way you use your body, your voice, even how you interact with your fellow actors-it's all completely different depending on whether you're on stage or in front of a camera.
Man: Right, and that's why actors deserve as much praise as possible. They're constantly shifting between styles and adapting to new roles. It's tough!
Woman: Couldn't agree more. I mean, whether it's theater or film, acting is such an emotional and demanding job. Encouragement and praise go a long way. They need to feel appreciated for all the work they put in.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
1. Người nam đánh giá cao tầm quan trọng của vòng thử vai: "I've always believed that auditions are the most important part of an actor's career."
2. Người phụ nữ cho rằng kịch bản mới quan trọng: "I think actors respond best when they feel inspired by what's on the page." (Strong scripts really bring out the best in them).
3. Người nam so sánh sự khác nhau: "...huge difference between theater acting and screen acting." Người phụ nữ hoàn toàn đồng ý: "Absolutely! They're such different worlds."
4. Người nam nói: "actors deserve as much praise as possible." Người phụ nữ đồng tình: "Couldn't agree more. ... Encouragement and praise go a long way."

Singers can be good role models for young people.
questions.explanation:
W: You took your daughter to that concert on Saturday, didn't you? How did it go?
M: Brilliant, thanks. And I came away thinking the singer was actually rather a good influence on her. People up on that stage can set a genuinely positive example for teenagers.
W: I'm not so sure about that, to be honest. They're performers, not teachers. Handing them that kind of responsibility seems risky to me.
M: Some of them handle it rather well, though, in fairness.
W: One or two, maybe. Anyway, she and I could never agree on what to put on in the car. I've always thought what you like in music is completely your own business. Nobody can argue you out of it.
M: Oh, I agree with you entirely there. I gave up trying to convert anybody to my records years ago.
W: Quite right too. Although I do think there's something that goes beyond all that. Put a piece of music on anywhere in the world and people respond the same way. It speaks across everything.
M: Hmm, I don't see it that way. I'll accept that a good tune travels, certainly, but the meaning doesn't travel with it. What sounds joyful to me might well be a funeral song somewhere else.
W: That's rather a bleak way of looking at it, if you ask me.
M: Realistic, I'd say. Sensible, even.
W: Well, here's one you might come round to. I'm convinced music gets used quite deliberately to push us about emotionally. Think of adverts, or the soundtrack in any film.
M: No, you're absolutely right there. Supermarkets do it, adverts do it, everybody does it. Slow the tempo right down and people apparently wander round the aisles and spend more.
W: Frightening, really, when you stop and think about it.
M: It works, though. That's precisely why they keep on doing it.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
Key: Ca sĩ có thể là hình mẫu tốt cho giới trẻ = Man · Gu âm nhạc là chuyện rất cá nhân = Both · Âm nhạc là ngôn ngữ toàn cầu = Woman · Âm nhạc có thể thao túng cảm xúc = Both

1. Singers can be good role models for young people. → Man: người đàn ông nêu "People up on that stage can set a genuinely positive example for teenagers." Người phụ nữ phản đối: "I'm not so sure about that, to be honest. They're performers, not teachers."

2. Taste in music is a highly personal thing. → Both: người phụ nữ nêu "what you like in music is completely your own business. Nobody can argue you out of it." Người đàn ông tán thành: "Oh, I agree with you entirely there."

3. Music is a universal language → Woman: người phụ nữ nêu "Put a piece of music on anywhere in the world and people respond the same way. It speaks across everything." Người đàn ông phản đối: "Hmm, I don't see it that way... the meaning doesn't travel with it."

4. Music can be used to manipulate people's feelings → Both: người phụ nữ nêu "music gets used quite deliberately to push us about emotionally", người đàn ông đồng ý rõ: "No, you're absolutely right there. Supermarkets do it, adverts do it, everybody does it."

👉 Mẹo: Bẫy ở ý 3 — người đàn ông nói "I'll accept that a good tune travels" nghe rất giống đồng ý, nhưng ngay sau đó bác bỏ phần cốt lõi (ý nghĩa không đi theo), nên đáp án là Woman chứ không phải Both.

questions.prompt: Four people are talking about doing exercise. Match each person to the correct information.
questions.explanation:
Speaker A: Exercise has become essential in my life, especially with my demanding and stressful job. The workload can be overwhelming at times, leaving me feeling exhausted and overwhelmed. That's why I turn to exercise as a way to unwind and rejuvenate. Whether it's going for a run, practicing yoga, or even just taking a brisk walk, exercise helps me release stress and clear my mind. I've noticed that after exercising, I feel more focused, energized, and ready to tackle my work with renewed vigor. It's incredible how something as simple as exercise can greatly improve my work performance and overall well-being. Speaker B: Honestly? Exercise wears me out. The idea of getting all sweaty and sore doesn't excite me at all. Every time I try to work out, it feels like I'm running on empty within minutes. And people say it gives them energy? Are we talking about the same thing? I feel more tired just thinking about the treadmill. I know it's supposed to be good for me, and I try to do it for my health, but I don't get that rush people talk about. Exercise for me is just exhausting. Why do something that makes me want to lie down for three days afterward? Speaker C: Exercising is a blast when you're with the right people. I've joined a few group classes, and they're like a party every time. The music is pumping, everyone's in sync, and it feels like we're all in this together. Working out alone can get boring, but with friends, you laugh, you encourage each other, and suddenly, an hour has flown by. We push each other, you know? It's kind of amazing half the time, I forget I'm even working out. I actually look forward to it. The camaraderie makes it worth every minute. Speaker D: Exercise? Ugh, I can't stand it. I know it's supposed to be good for you and all that, but I find it completely miserable. The sweat, the strain, the way my muscles burn afterward, it's like a punishment. People say it'll get better or that I'll start to like it eventually, but I've tried, and I still hate it. Honestly, life's too short to spend it doing something you can't stand. There are other ways to be healthy that don't involve torturing myself. I'd rather read a book than jog any day.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ---
• Improve work performance → Speaker A: tập xong "I feel more focused, energized, and ready to tackle my work" — tập để làm việc tốt hơn.
• Hate exercising → Speaker D: "I can't stand it... it's like a punishment", đã thử nhưng vẫn ghét.
• Find exercise tiring → Speaker B: "Exercise wears me out... it feels like I'm running on empty within minutes" — thấy mệt chứ không thấy khỏe ra.
• Have fun exercising with others → Speaker C: "Exercising is a blast when you're with the right people", tập nhóm vui như đi tiệc.
• Enjoy exercising alone và Exercise to lose weight là 2 phương án nhiễu — C còn nói ngược lại ("Working out alone can get boring"), và không ai nhắc tới giảm cân.

⚠️ Phân biệt B và D: cả hai đều KHÔNG thích tập, nhưng B nhấn vào cảm giác KIỆT SỨC (tiring), còn D nói thẳng là GHÉT (hate).

What does she say about working at home?
options: Video calls are superior to face-to-face conversation
questions.explanation:
Before I began working from home, I imagined paradise: no commute, no meetings that could have been emails, and above all, silence. I truly believed there would be no distractions once the chatting colleagues were gone. Reality re-educated me within a week. The distractions did not disappear; they changed uniform. The washing machine calls, the doorbell rings, the fridge whispers, and family members assume that being home means being available. As for video calls — useful, yes, but let nobody tell you they beat face-to-face conversation. Explaining a complicated problem through a frozen screen and a delayed microphone cured me of that idea permanently. So when friends ask for my honest verdict after a full year, I give them three words: not as expected. There are real advantages, but the dream and the reality live at different addresses.
Let me pass on what I have actually learned. First, forget the magazine photos — you do not need a big home office. My best work happens at a small desk in the corner of the bedroom. Second, do not believe anyone who says this lifestyle requires no self-motivation; with nobody watching, discipline is the entire game. And the biggest lesson: there is no universal answer. How well working from home goes depends on your situation and your personality. My neighbour thrives alone; I miss the noise of other humans. Learn which kind of worker you are — preferably before you sign anything.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
(Bản variant của Đề 02 bài 2.)
1. Đáp án: Not good as expected. Bẫy: "no distractions" ("changed uniform") và "video calls superior" ("cured me of that idea").
2. Đáp án: It depends on your situation and personality. Bẫy: "big home office" và "no self-motivation" đều bị phủ định.

questions.prompt: What is the speaker's opinion about security cameras at work?
options: People are unnecessarily worried about them
Most people don't even realize cameras are present
Cameras should be placed to ensure complete coverage
questions.explanation:
When the security cameras appeared in our office last spring, the reaction was immediate. Colleagues whispered about being watched, and a few genuinely believed management had stopped trusting us. Months later, I can offer a calmer view: people are unnecessarily worried about these cameras. And let me correct two claims I keep hearing. First, the idea that most staff do not even notice the cameras — untrue in our building, where everyone noticed within an hour and discussed nothing else for a week. Second, one colleague's campaign for cameras covering every single corner of every room — an overreaction in the opposite direction that would help nobody. The cameras sit in shared spaces: entrances, corridors, the storage area. They are there for safety, not surveillance, and no one reviews footage without a reason.
Think practically about what the cameras actually do for us. If equipment disappears or an accident happens near the loading door, there is finally a record instead of a guessing game. Their quiet presence also discourages trouble before it starts. I know some people still find them intimidating, and others repeat that cameras only matter after something bad has already happened. I would ask both groups to reconsider. We should feel reassured by their presence, not threatened. A company that installs safety equipment is not accusing its staff — it is protecting them. Once that idea settles in, the little lens above the doorway stops feeling like an eye and starts feeling like a seatbelt.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
(Bản variant của Đề 08 bài 2.)
1. Đáp án: People are unnecessarily worried about them. Bẫy: "don't realize cameras are present" ("untrue in our building") và "complete coverage" ("overreaction").
2. Đáp án: People should feel reassured about their presence. Bẫy: "intimidating" và "only useful after incidents" — "I would ask both groups to reconsider".

questions.prompt: Why did the new podcast fail?
options: The creators did not promote their show effectively
questions.explanation:
Let us talk about the podcast that everyone predicted would succeed — and did not. The interviews were thoughtful, the sound was clean, and the episodes were a reasonable length; anyone claiming the content ran too long has not checked, because most episodes finished under forty minutes and listeners who started them stayed to the end. Nor was the market to blame. Yes, podcasting is crowded, but during those same months several smaller shows in noisier categories found their audiences and grew. The failure had one address: promotion. The creators uploaded each episode and simply waited, assuming discovery would happen by itself. No clips shared online, no visits to neighbouring shows, no message to the communities who would have loved the topic. In podcasting, the microphone is only half the work; the megaphone is the other half, and they never picked it up.
Does one quiet failure say anything bad about podcasting itself? I think not, and I will go further. Dismissing the medium as a waste of time — as some critics still do — misses what actually happens between a host and a loyal audience. Calling it mere entertainment for the commute sells it equally short. A good podcast is one of the great community builders of our age. Strangers gather around a shared curiosity, week after week, write in with their stories, and meet in comment threads and live events. Radio spoke to millions; podcasts gather thousands into rooms — and the rooms are what matter.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
(Bản variant podcast #3. Phương án "too many listeners" đã thay bằng "It faced too much competition".)
1. Đáp án: The creators did not promote their show effectively. Bẫy: "content too long" ("has not checked") và "competition" ("several smaller shows... grew").
2. Đáp án: It is a great way to build a community. Bẫy: "waste of time" và "only entertainment" — "misses what actually happens... sells it equally short".

questions.prompt: What does the expert say being professional is all about?
options: To create a good working environment
questions.explanation:
Good morning, and thank you for inviting me to speak about professionalism. When I ask audiences what the word means, I hear the same two answers everywhere. Creating a good working environment, say the managers. Making a good impression, say the juniors. Fine answers — but notice that both describe outcomes, not causes. In my view, professionalism is, at its centre, about maintaining a positive attitude. The colleague who stays constructive on a bad day, who greets the difficult client with patience, who offers help before being asked — that attitude is the seed. The pleasant environment and the strong impression are simply what grows from it. Get the attitude right and the rest arrives on its own; fake the rest without the attitude and everyone notices within a month.
The second thing I want to say is about time. Some people in this room may believe professionalism means today what it meant forty years ago — the suit, the firm handshake, the strict hierarchy. It does not. Others may hope that once they learn today's rules, the definition will finally hold still. It will not. Our definition of professionalism is changing, and it keeps changing. Flexibility now sits where formality sat; cultural understanding matters as much as punctuality; using new tools well counts as basic manners. The professionals who flourish are not the ones who memorised one era's rulebook — they are the ones who notice when the rulebook is being rewritten. Thank you.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
(Bản variant của Đề 01 bài 2.)
1. Đáp án: To maintain a positive attitude. Bẫy: "good working environment" và "good impression" — "both describe outcomes, not causes".
2. Đáp án: Our definition of it is changing. Bẫy: "same as 40 years ago" ("It does not") và "will not change anymore" ("It will not").

questions.prompt: What does the speaker say is one major strength of successful television series?
options: They focus mainly on famous actors
They are usually shorter than films
questions.explanation:
Every year my students ask me to name the secret of a successful television series, hoping for a shortcut. Here is the honest lecture. The shortcuts people believe in are famous actors — and yet the graveyard of cancelled shows is full of A-list faces — and shorter running times, the idea that episodes beat films simply by asking less of your evening. Neither survives contact with the ratings data. The quality that actually predicts long life is consistency. The series that run for years maintain their standard from first episode to last: the writing stays sharp in season six, the acting stays committed, the production never visibly saves money. Audiences are generous with a single weak hour, but they are merciless with decline. The moment a show feels like it has stopped trying, the loyalty it spent years building evaporates in weeks.
As for how series are made today, ignore two fashionable complaints. Streaming did not make production cheap — budgets have climbed to historic highs. And television is not growing less creative; by any honest measure this is a bold era. The real transformation is quieter and more interesting: viewer habits now shape production itself. Platforms watch us watching — where we pause, what we skip, when we abandon — and that data flows back into the writers' rooms, adjusting episode lengths, pacing, even storylines. For the first time since the medium was born, the audience is not just receiving television. It is quietly co-writing it.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
(Bản variant TV series #3.)
1. Đáp án: They maintain consistent quality throughout. Bẫy: "famous actors" và "shorter than films" — "Neither survives contact with the ratings data".
2. Đáp án: Viewer habits influence the way that series are made. Bẫy: "reduced production costs" và "less creative" đều bị bác.

questions.prompt: Why hasn't he gone to college?
options: He couldn't afford the tuition fees.
He wasn't ready to start higher education.
He didn't get good enough grades.
questions.explanation:
On today's education programme, a story I often share with worried parents: the young man who did not go to college with his classmates. Why not? The neighbourhood had theories. Money troubles, whispered some — wrong; the family had saved carefully and could afford the fees. Poor grades, assumed others — wrong again; his results were comfortably good enough. The real reason was the one nobody guessed because it sounds so simple: he was not ready for higher education. He told his parents that his mind felt like a full cup — pour in more, and everything would spill. Rather than waste the most expensive years of his education arriving empty, he asked for time. To their credit, they gave it.
What did the break actually give him back? He spent months working part-time in a bakery, but he laughs when people assume the job was the lesson — it mostly taught him to wake at four. He returned valuing education more than ever, yet even that, he insists, was not the point. The real lesson of his break was independence. He learned to run his own timetable, answer for his own mistakes, and make decisions without a teacher's rubric or a parent's reminder. When he finally began university a year later, tutors described him as the most self-directed student in the room. The year everyone called lost, he now calls the most efficient year of his education.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
(Bản variant gap year #3 — góc người dẫn chương trình.)
1. Đáp án: He wasn't ready to start higher education. Bẫy: "tuition fees" và "grades" là "theories" bị bác.
2. Đáp án: How to be more independent. Bẫy: "working part-time" ("mostly taught him to wake at four") và "importance of education" ("not the point").

Throughout the presentation, we used images to explain our ideas.
After the presentation, other students asked questions.
questions.explanation:
--- GIẢI THÍCH ---
Dạng sắp xếp câu: tìm câu mở đầu (không trỏ ngược), rồi bám vào đại từ, từ chỉ định và từ nối để nối dần.

▸ Wellness fair — thứ tự đúng:
  0. "Last weekend, the community organised a special event to inspire people to live healthier lives." → câu cho sẵn, giới thiệu sự kiện.
  1. "The wellness fair took place on Saturday afternoon, promoting healthy habits and lifestyles." → gọi tên sự kiện đã nhắc ở câu cho sẵn và cho mốc thời gian.
  2. "Over sixty participants joined the event, with Dr Patel leading an exciting fitness workshop." → "the event" trỏ về hội chợ, thêm số người và hoạt động đầu tiên.
  3. "The fair also featured activities such as cooking demonstrations, mindfulness sessions and a fun run." → "also" nối thêm hoạt động sau workshop.
  4. "After the workshops, prizes were given to those with the most creative health posters." → "After the workshops" nối tiếp ngay sau các workshop/hoạt động vừa nêu, kể phần trao giải.
  5. "Families had a great time sampling healthy snacks and learning useful tips about overall wellness." → câu kết: tổng kết cảm nhận chung của người tham dự về cả sự kiện.

▸ A group presentation — thứ tự đúng:
  1. “First, we prepared the materials for our group presentation.” → câu mở đầu: nêu chủ thể và bối cảnh, không trỏ ngược về câu nào.
  2. “Then, we presented our topic for 10 minutes.” → mốc thời gian “Then” — kể tiếp sự việc vừa xảy ra.
  3. “Throughout the presentation, we used images to explain our ideas.” → nối tiếp mạch nội dung của câu ngay trước.
  4. “After the presentation, other students asked questions.” → mốc thời gian “After” — kể tiếp sự việc vừa xảy ra.
  5. “Finally, each group member took turns answering the questions.” → mốc thời gian “Finally” — kể tiếp sự việc vừa xảy ra.

title: Đề 34 - Family sports day + The first American woman in space

questions.prompt: Put the sentences in the correct order.
options: They were all hungry after all of this, so the children had tasty food and drinks with their parents.
These included football, swimming and jumping, and the children had lots of fun.
Sixty men and women ran in this, and Ms Kamur won with a very fast time.
It started early on Saturday morning with a ten-mile race for adults.
After she had received her prize, the children's activities and competitions began.
As a member of the team, she traveled into space and carried out numerous experiments.
Encouraged by her parents, Mae decided to study science at university.
Some of these experiments involved growing plants and observing animals aboard the spacecraft.
Her passion for space led Mae to join a dedicated research team.

questions.explanation:
--- GIẢI THÍCH ---
Dạng sắp xếp câu: tìm câu mở đầu (không trỏ ngược), rồi bám vào đại từ, từ chỉ định và từ nối để nối dần.

▸ Family sports day — thứ tự đúng:
  0. "Last weekend the weather was good, so the town held a family sports day in the park." → câu cho sẵn, giới thiệu sự kiện.
  1. "It started early on Saturday morning with a ten-mile race for adults." → "It" trỏ về "a family sports day".
  2. "Sixty men and women ran in this, and Ms Kamur won with a very fast time." → "ran in this" trỏ về "a ten-mile race".
  3. "After she had received her prize, the children's activities and competitions began." → "she" trỏ về Ms Kamur ở câu trước.
  4. "These included football, swimming and jumping, and the children had lots of fun." → "These" trỏ về "the children's activities and competitions".
  5. "They were all hungry after all of this, so the children had tasty food and drinks with their parents." → "after all of this" gom lại toàn bộ hoạt động, chốt bằng bữa ăn.

▸ The first American woman in space — thứ tự đúng:
  1. “Encouraged by her parents, Mae decided to study science at university.” → câu mở đầu: nêu chủ thể và bối cảnh, không trỏ ngược về câu nào.
  2. “Her strong academic record earned her a place in a training program in the United States.” → bắt đầu bằng đại từ “Her” — bắt buộc phải có câu giới thiệu đứng trước.
  3. “Her passion for space led Mae to join a dedicated research team.” → bắt đầu bằng đại từ “Her” — bắt buộc phải có câu giới thiệu đứng trước.
  4. “As a member of the team, she traveled into space and carried out numerous experiments.” → nối tiếp mạch nội dung của câu ngay trước.
  5. “Some of these experiments involved growing plants and observing animals aboard the spacecraft.” → mở bằng “Some of these” — từ nối bám thẳng vào ý câu trước.
