Let's talk about clothes. What are you wearing today?
questions.explanation: Today I am wearing a plain white shirt and dark blue jeans. I also have simple black shoes that I bought last year. The shirt is cotton, so it feels cool in hot weather. I chose these clothes because I had a meeting at my office this morning. I like clothes that are comfortable and easy to wear every day.

questions.prompt: Where do you usually buy your clothes?
questions.explanation: I usually buy my clothes at a shopping mall near my house. There are several shops there that sell simple clothes at fair prices. Sometimes I order online when there is a sale, but I worry about the size. I prefer going to a real shop because I can try things on first. I do not buy new clothes very often.

questions.prompt: Do people in your country dress differently at work and at home?
questions.explanation: Yes, most people in my country dress quite differently at work and at home. At work they wear shirts, trousers, or a uniform that the company provides. At home they change into shorts and a T-shirt because the weather is hot. Older people often wear very simple clothes at home. I think comfort matters more than style inside the house.

questions.prompt: Describe these two pictures.
questions.explanation: In the first picture, five friends are standing close together and taking a photo of themselves. One of them is holding the phone up high, and everyone is smiling. They look like a group that is on holiday somewhere warm. In the second picture, a man is alone on a hillside with a camera. He is pointing it at the mountains in front of him. Both people are taking photos, but the first picture is about the group and the second one is about the view.

questions.prompt: Which way of taking photos do you prefer, and why?
questions.explanation: I prefer taking photos with my friends, like the first picture. When I look at those photos later, I remember the day and the people clearly. Photos of scenery are beautiful, but they often look the same as pictures that I can find online. My friends make each photo different. I still take some landscape photos when I travel, especially in the mountains near Sa Pa. I have kept every one of them since school. Group photos are the ones that I actually open again.

questions.prompt: Why do some people like sharing photos with their friends?
questions.explanation: I think people take photographs because they want to keep their memories. Life moves quickly, and we forget small details after only a few months. A photo brings the moment back. People also like sharing photos with family and friends who live far away. Some people take photos simply because it is fun and creative. Phones have made this very easy, so almost everyone takes pictures every single day. My mother still keeps printed photos in a box that she has had for years.

questions.prompt: How often do you drink coffee, and when do you usually drink it?
questions.explanation: I drink coffee almost every day, usually one cup in the morning. I make it at home with a small filter that my mother gave me. I drink it at about seven o'clock, before I leave for work. Sometimes I buy an iced milk coffee near my office in the afternoon. I try not to drink coffee after four o'clock, because then I sleep badly. On Sunday I drink it slowly with my family at home. That is my favourite cup of the week.

questions.prompt: Why do you think coffee shops are so popular in your country?
questions.explanation: Coffee shops are very popular in Vietnam because they are cheap and they are everywhere. Many people meet their friends there instead of at home. Students also go there to study, because the air conditioning is good and the wifi is free. I have friends who work in coffee shops all Saturday afternoon. Houses in the city are small, so a coffee shop is a comfortable second living room. A drink costs only about thirty thousand dong. That price is easy for most young people.

questions.prompt: Describe the picture.
questions.explanation: This is a line of people inside a small bakery. About eight customers are waiting to pay at the counter. A young man at the front is talking to the woman behind the till. Two people in the middle of the line are looking at their phones. One older woman is holding a paper bag with bread in it. The floor is clean and the shelves behind the counter are full of bread. Everybody looks patient, so the line has not stopped moving.

questions.prompt: Tell me about a time you had to wait in a long queue.
questions.explanation: Last year I waited two hours at the passport office in Hanoi. I arrived at seven in the morning, but there were already forty people in front of me. I needed a new passport for a work trip. I took a paper number and sat on a plastic chair that faced the door. I read the news on my phone and drank a bottle of water. The staff called my number at half past nine. After that everything was finished in ten minutes.

questions.prompt: Do you think people in your country are patient when they have to wait? Why?
questions.explanation: I think it depends on the situation. In a bank or a hospital, most people wait quietly and follow the numbers. But on the road, drivers are not patient at all. At a red light in Hanoi, people start pressing the horn after two seconds. Young people are also less patient than my parents, because they are used to fast apps. My father has waited an hour for a bowl of pho. I usually give up after twenty minutes and go home.

questions.prompt: Describe the picture.
questions.explanation: This is a living room in the evening. A father and his son are sitting close together on a grey sofa. Both of them are holding game controllers that have long black cables. The television in front of them shows a car racing game. The boy is about ten years old and he is leaning forward. His father is laughing and looking at the screen. There are two glasses of water on the small table. The room is warm and the curtains are closed.

questions.prompt: When was the last time you played games?
questions.explanation: I do not play much now, but I played a lot at university. My favourite one was a football game on the PlayStation console. My roommate and I played it almost every night after dinner. We made a small tournament with four friends who lived on our floor. Now I only play simple games on my phone while I wait for the bus. I have not touched a console for about three years. Sometimes I miss those noisy evenings in the dormitory.

questions.prompt: Why do some people like playing games with their friends?
questions.explanation: I think it can be very good, if the family chooses the right game. Children often find it hard to talk to their parents about school. But playing a game together is easy and there is no pressure. My uncle has played a racing game with his daughter every Saturday evening. He says they laugh more in one hour than in a whole week. The problem is time, because most parents come home late from work. One hour together is still better than nothing.

questions.prompt: Tell me about a time when you had to give a presentation.
questions.explanation: The one I remember most clearly was last November. My manager asked me to present the results of a customer survey to about fifteen colleagues. I had never spoken to a group that size before. I had a week, which sounds generous until you try to turn four hundred responses into twelve slides. I cut the charts down twice, because my first version looked like a spreadsheet on a wall. My friend Nam sat through a rehearsal and told me, quite bluntly, that I was speaking far too fast. Beforehand I was worse than I expected. My hands were cold and I drank two glasses of water in the corridor. The first minute was rough, and I heard myself racing through the introduction. Then somebody in the second row started taking notes, and that small thing settled me down. By the middle I was actually enjoying it. Afterwards came a strange mix of pride and exhaustion, and I remember not wanting to talk to anybody for an hour. On the wider question, I think these skills matter enormously for young people here. Students spend years learning theory which they are never asked to explain out loud. Then they start a job where every meeting demands exactly that. Someone who can make a complicated idea simple gets noticed quickly, whereas a brilliant person who cannot be understood stays invisible. It is a skill you learn by doing it badly a few times.

title: Đề 29 - Working on a laptop vs travelling

questions.prompt: Describe the picture.
questions.explanation: In the first picture, a young woman is working at a desk. She has a laptop in front of her, with papers and a cup of coffee beside it. The room looks quiet and tidy. In the second picture, a man who is carrying a backpack stands beside a mountain lake. He is holding a paper map and looking at the water. Both pictures show how people spend a day, but one day is spent indoors and the other outdoors. The mood of each picture is completely different.

questions.prompt: Would you prefer to work at a desk or to travel for work? Why?
questions.explanation: I would prefer to travel, at least for part of the year. Sitting at a desk every day makes me tired, and I have noticed that my ideas get weaker after long hours indoors. Travelling gives me fresh air, new places and new people to talk to. However, I still need a steady income, so a job that mixes both would suit me best. A few weeks away, then quiet office work at home. That balance has worked well for two friends of mine, and I would copy it.

questions.prompt: Do you think technology has made it easier for people to work while travelling?
questions.explanation: Yes, technology has changed this completely. People can now send emails from a train, join a meeting from a hotel room, or share files from an airport. My cousin, who works for a travel company, does most of her job from her phone. Ten years ago this was much harder for her. However, working everywhere also means that people never really stop. So technology helps us travel, but it brings the office along with us. Most of us have accepted that trade without really choosing it.

title: Đề 30 - Writing by hand vs on a tablet

questions.prompt: Describe the picture.
questions.explanation: The first picture shows a student writing in a notebook with a pen. Her handwriting fills half the page, and an open textbook lies next to her elbow. The desk is wooden and a little untidy. In the second picture, a young man is writing on a tablet with a digital pen. His notes appear on the bright screen as he moves his hand. Both people are taking notes, but one uses paper and the other uses a device. The tools that they have chosen are the only real difference.

questions.prompt: Do you prefer writing by hand or typing on a device? Why?
questions.explanation: I prefer writing by hand when I am studying. Words that I write slowly seem to stay in my memory longer, and I remember where they sat on the page. For long documents, though, a keyboard is much faster and easier to correct. I have used a tablet for university notes, and it was convenient, but I still keep a paper notebook for revision. So my honest answer depends on what I am writing. Speed matters at work, but memory matters more when I study.

questions.prompt: Do you think children should still learn to write by hand at school?
questions.explanation: Yes, I think handwriting is still important for children. Writing by hand helps them control small movements and learn how letters are formed. Teachers who I have spoken to say children remember spelling better when they write words themselves. Of course, students need computer skills too, because most work today is done on screens. So schools should teach both, with handwriting in the early years and typing added later. Neither skill should replace the other completely. The two skills belong to different parts of a child's education.

title: Đề 31 - Planting trees vs caring for older people

questions.prompt: Describe the two pictures.
questions.explanation: In the first picture, a group of young volunteers is planting a small tree in a park. Two of them hold the trunk while another fills the hole with soil. They are wearing gloves and green shirts. In the second picture, a young woman is sitting with an elderly lady in a care home. They are holding hands and talking. Both pictures show people who are helping others, but one group helps nature and the other helps a person. The two scenes feel calm in different ways.

questions.prompt: Which activity do you think is more useful for the local community?
questions.explanation: I would prefer to spend time with older people. Planting trees is useful, but I enjoy conversation, and many elderly people who live alone rarely have visitors. My grandmother was very lonely in her last years, so I understand how much a short visit means. Tree planting is good too, and it is easier to organise for large groups. Still, if I had one free afternoon, I would choose to sit and listen to someone. Trees can wait, but a lonely afternoon cannot wait at all.

questions.prompt: Do you think it's important to do volunteer work in your local area?
questions.explanation: Volunteering teaches young people skills that school cannot easily give. They learn to work in a team, to speak with strangers, and to solve small problems by themselves. It also shows them how other people live, which can change their opinions about society. Many employers like to see volunteer work on an application, because it shows responsibility. Most importantly, helping others makes young people feel useful, and that feeling stays with them for years. Schools that build volunteering into the timetable are doing the right thing.

title: Đề 32 - Picking up litter vs planting trees

questions.prompt: Describe the picture.
questions.explanation: In the first picture, a group of volunteers in bright yellow vests is collecting litter in a park. A man at the front is using a long picker to grab a plastic bottle, and the others are putting rubbish into green bags. In the second picture, five young people in white T-shirts are planting a small tree together. A girl is holding the tree straight while her friends dig, rake the soil and pour water from a green watering can. Both pictures show people helping the environment as a team.

questions.prompt: Do you think it is important to do volunteer work? Why?
questions.explanation: I would rather join a litter clean-up in the park. The change is immediate, and at the end of the morning you can look back and see a clean park. That feeling keeps people coming again. Planting trees is important too, but you have to wait a long time for any result. I have also noticed that clean-ups are easier to organise in a city, because you do not need any land. So I would start with the rubbish. A visible result is what keeps volunteers coming back.

questions.prompt: Which project is more beneficial to the environment? Why?
questions.explanation: Local governments can do many practical things. They can put more bins and recycling points in public places, so people are not tempted to drop rubbish. They can also fine companies that pour waste into rivers. Improving buses and building cycle lanes reduces the number of cars in the centre. Schools can be given money for environment clubs, which teaches good habits early. Small local rules often work faster than big national promises. People usually follow the rules that make good behaviour easy and cheap for them.

questions.prompt: Describe the picture.
questions.explanation: The first picture shows a busy beach in summer. Families are lying under coloured umbrellas, two boys are playing volleyball, and a child is eating ice cream near the water. In the second picture, a town square is covered in snow. People in thick coats are skating on an outdoor rink, and children are building a snowman. Both pictures show people who are enjoying free time outside, but the activities depend completely on the season. One crowd is dressed for heat and the other for snow.

questions.prompt: Which season do you prefer for your free time activities? Why?
questions.explanation: I prefer summer for activities, because the days are long and almost everything happens outside. I can swim, play football in the evening, or travel with friends without worrying about the weather. Winter activities are more limited in my country, since we have no snow, so people stay at home. I have spent whole winters indoors, which was very boring. Summer simply gives me more choices, even if the middle of the day is too hot. A long summer evening is worth more to me than anything winter offers.

questions.prompt: How do the seasons change the activities that families do together?
questions.explanation: Seasons change family life a lot. In summer, families go to the beach, have picnics, or travel during the school holidays, and children play outside until late. In winter, activities move indoors, so families cook together, watch films, or visit relatives. In countries that have snow, winter brings skiing and skating instead. Festivals also follow the calendar, which gives each season its own routine. So the weather quietly decides how families spend their weekends. Children remember those routines long after they have forgotten the details.

title: Đề 34 - Healthy food vs fast food

questions.prompt: Describe the picture.
questions.explanation: In the first picture, there is a plate of healthy food on a kitchen table. I can see a green salad, a piece of grilled fish, and a glass of water. Everything looks fresh and simple. In the second picture, a tray of fast food is sitting on a counter. It holds a burger, a large box of chips and a soft drink. Both pictures show a meal, but the food that they offer is very different. One meal was cooked slowly and the other was not.

questions.prompt: Which of these two meals would you choose? Why?
questions.explanation: Most days I would choose the healthy meal. I feel much better in the afternoon after fish and vegetables, and a heavy burger makes me sleepy at my desk. Cooking at home is also cheaper for my family. However, I will not pretend that I never eat fast food. I have burgers with friends perhaps twice a month, usually late at night. So I choose the healthy plate normally and the tray occasionally. The problem only starts when the exception has quietly turned into a daily routine.

questions.prompt: Why do so many young people eat fast food?
questions.explanation: Fast food is popular with young people for simple reasons. It is quick, cheap, and available almost everywhere, including near schools and universities. Many students who live away from home cannot cook well, so ordering is easier than shopping. Fast-food restaurants are also social places where friends can sit for hours. Advertising and delivery apps make it even more tempting. Young people know it is not healthy, but convenience usually wins in the end. Habits that start at university often last for many more years.

questions.prompt: Describe the picture.
questions.explanation: The first picture was taken inside a museum. A group of school children is standing in front of a large dinosaur skeleton, and their teacher is explaining something. Some children are writing in small notebooks. The second picture shows a playground in a park, where children are running, climbing and going down a slide. Both pictures show children who are learning and enjoying themselves, but one group is quiet indoors and the other is loud outside. The teacher has planned one visit, while the park needs no plan.

questions.prompt: Where would you rather take a group of children? Why?
questions.explanation: I would take them to the park first. Young children need to move, and after twenty minutes in a museum many of them stop listening. In a playground they run, share equipment and make friends quickly. Museums are valuable, but they work better for older students who can read the information. I have helped with a school trip before, and the children who enjoyed it most were over eleven. So age really decides my answer. A short walk in a park has never made a child unhappy.

questions.prompt: How should schools balance classroom learning and outdoor activities?
questions.explanation: Schools should treat outdoor time as part of learning, not as a reward. Children who move during the day concentrate better afterwards, so breaks and sport are not wasted hours. A good balance might be short breaks every hour, one sports lesson a week, and a few trips each term. Museums, farms and parks all teach different things. Exams are important, but a school that only sits children at desks will lose their attention. A day that mixes both kinds of learning usually produces the calmest classroom.

title: Đề 36 - Sunny weather vs cold weather

questions.prompt: Describe the picture.
questions.explanation: In the first picture, a woman is walking along a street in strong sunshine. She wears a wide hat and sunglasses, and she is wiping her face because of the heat. In the second picture, a man is standing outside on a grey winter day. He has put on a thick coat, a scarf and a wool hat, and his breath is white in the cold air. Both people are dressed for the weather that they are facing. The seasons that they are living in look completely opposite.

questions.prompt: In which kind of weather do you feel better? Why?
questions.explanation: I feel better in cool weather than in heat. When the temperature rises above thirty-five degrees, I lose my appetite, sleep badly and get headaches. In cold weather I can put on more clothes and keep moving, and I have always slept better under a blanket. Of course, very cold air is bad for people who have chest problems. But for my own body, a cold morning feels much healthier than a burning afternoon. A thick jacket solves a problem that no fan can solve.

questions.prompt: How does the weather affect people's mood and health?
questions.explanation: Weather affects us more than we think. Sunlight helps the body produce vitamin D, and many people feel happier and more active on bright days. In long grey winters, some people become tired and sad, which doctors call seasonal depression. Extreme heat is also dangerous, because older people lose water quickly and their hearts suffer. Cold weather brings colds and flu. So both extremes affect health, and the mild days between them suit us best. Doctors say that the body works best in the middle range.

title: Đề 37 - Pushing a shopping trolley vs driving a car

questions.prompt: Describe the picture.
questions.explanation: In the first picture, a woman is pushing a shopping trolley across a car park. The trolley is full of bags, and she is holding the handle with both hands. She looks tired but not unhappy. In the second picture, a man is driving a car through a busy street. His hands are on the wheel and he is watching the road ahead. Both pictures show a person who is on the way home after an ordinary trip. The bags and the traffic show two very ordinary afternoons.

questions.prompt: Do you prefer to walk to local shops or to drive to a big supermarket? Why?
questions.explanation: I usually prefer to walk to the small shops near my house. I can buy what I need for one day, and the walk gives me a little exercise. Driving to a big supermarket is better once a month, when we buy heavy things like rice and water. My mother, who does not drive, shops on foot every single morning. So I use both, but walking suits my normal week much better than driving does. The small shops near me have also become part of my routine.

questions.prompt: Do you think cities should reduce the number of cars in the centre?
questions.explanation: Yes, I think city centres would be better with fewer cars. Traffic causes air pollution, noise and accidents, and drivers waste a lot of time looking for parking. If cities build good buses, trains and cycle lanes, many people will happily leave the car at home. Streets that have no traffic are also safer for children and better for small shops. However, transport must improve first, or people will simply be stuck. Cities that have done this well are much nicer places to walk in.

questions.prompt: Describe the picture.
questions.explanation: In this picture, I can see four or five people in an office. Two of them are looking at some papers together. A woman in a checked jacket is standing and pointing at a document, and a man in a black shirt is sitting at a computer and listening to her. Behind them, two other colleagues are standing and talking. The office is bright and modern, with big screens on the desk. Everyone looks busy but relaxed.

questions.prompt: What do you think about working in an office with other people?
questions.explanation: I think working in an office with other people has good and bad points. The main advantage is that you can ask your colleagues for help immediately, so problems get solved faster. You also feel less lonely during the day. However, an office can be noisy, and it is hard to concentrate when people are talking around you. For me, the teamwork is worth it, but I still need somewhere quiet sometimes.

questions.prompt: Why do some people prefer to work from home?
questions.explanation: I think there are several reasons why some people prefer working from home. First, they save a lot of time because they do not have to travel to the office. Second, the house is usually quieter, so it is easier to focus on difficult tasks. They can also decide their own schedule and take breaks when they want. For parents, working at home makes it easier to look after their children.

questions.prompt: Describe the picture.
questions.explanation: In this picture, I can see two young women inside a train. One of them is standing and holding a camera, and she has a backpack on her shoulder. The other one is sitting near the window and smiling at her friend. The inside of the train is painted light green, and there are large windows on both sides. They look like tourists who are travelling together and enjoying the journey.

questions.prompt: What do you think about travelling by train?
questions.explanation: I think travelling by train is a very comfortable way to move around. You have much more space than on a bus, so you can stand up and walk when you feel tired. Trains are also safer, and you can look at the view through the big windows. The main problem is that trains do not go everywhere, and sometimes they are late. Still, for a long journey I would always choose the train.

questions.prompt: Why do some people prefer trains to other kinds of transport?
questions.explanation: I think people prefer trains for several reasons. First, there is a lot of legroom, so long journeys feel less tiring. Second, you can move around, buy food, or sleep during the trip. Trains are also better for the environment than planes or cars. Many people also say the journey itself is part of the holiday, because you can sit back and watch the countryside pass by through the window.

questions.prompt: Let's talk about school. Please tell me about the first school you went to.
questions.explanation: My first school was a small primary school in my neighbourhood. It was about ten minutes from my house, so I walked there with my sister every morning. The building was old and painted yellow, and there was a big tree in the playground. My favourite teacher was Mrs Lan, who taught us how to read.

questions.prompt: Let's talk about films. Please tell me about your favourite film star.
questions.explanation: My favourite film star is Tom Holland. I first saw him in a superhero film and I liked him immediately. He seems friendly and funny in interviews, not like a famous person at all. He is also quite young, so I feel he is close to my age. I think he is a good actor and a kind person.

questions.prompt: Let's talk about films. When was the last time you watched a film, and what was it?
questions.explanation: The last film I watched was about two weeks ago at home. It was an action film that my brother chose. We watched it on the television after dinner and ate some snacks. I did not know the story before, but it was easy to follow and quite exciting. I enjoyed it, although I usually prefer comedies to action films.

questions.prompt: Describe the picture.
questions.explanation: In this picture, I can see an older man playing music on the street. He has grey hair and a beard, and he is sitting in a wheelchair. He is holding a guitar and singing into a microphone in front of him. Behind him there is a yellow taxi and a black metal fence. He looks calm and he is clearly enjoying the music. It seems to be a normal day in a busy city.

questions.prompt: What do you think about street musicians?
questions.explanation: I think street musicians make a city more interesting. When I walk past someone playing music, the street feels friendlier and less stressful. It is also a chance for musicians to practise and earn some money. However, some people say the music is too loud, especially near shops or offices. In my opinion, as long as they are not disturbing anyone, street musicians are a good thing. I always stop for a minute if the music is good.

questions.prompt: Why do some people enjoy listening to live music?
questions.explanation: I think people enjoy live music because it feels more real than a recording. You can see the musician playing, and you can feel the sound all around you. The atmosphere is also different when you are with other people who like the same music. Many people say they remember a live concert for years, but they forget the songs they hear at home. For me, live music is simply more exciting than anything on my phone.

questions.prompt: Describe the picture.
questions.explanation: In this picture, I can see a young man sitting at a wooden desk. He is wearing a white shirt and a tie, so he is probably at work. He is looking at his laptop and laughing, with one hand touching his face. There is a video call on the screen and some papers and photographs on the desk. The room is bright and simple. He looks relaxed and in a very good mood.

questions.prompt: What do you think about using video calls for work?
questions.explanation: I think video calls are very useful for work. They save a lot of time because you do not have to travel to another office or another city. You can also see the other person's face, so it is easier to understand each other than on the phone. The problem is that the internet is not always stable, and long online meetings make people tired. Overall, I think video calls are a good tool if we use them carefully.

questions.prompt: Why do some people prefer meeting face to face?
questions.explanation: I think some people prefer meeting face to face because it feels more natural. When you sit in the same room, you can see body language and understand the mood better. Conversations also flow more easily, because nobody has to wait for the sound. Meeting in person helps to build trust, especially with new clients or new colleagues. For important decisions, most people still want to be in the same room.

questions.prompt: Describe the picture.
questions.explanation: In the first picture, I can see two people walking through a forest in winter. The ground is covered with snow and the trees are tall pine trees. They are wearing thick coats and warm hats. In the second picture, two people are walking along a beach. The sand is wet and the sea is on their right. Both pictures show people walking outdoors, but the weather is completely different.

questions.prompt: Which place would you rather spend a day in?
questions.explanation: If I had to choose, I would spend the day on the beach. I grew up in a hot country, so I feel more comfortable near the sea than in the snow. Walking on the sand is relaxing, and I like the sound of the waves. The forest looks beautiful, but I think I would feel cold very quickly. However, I understand why some people love winter, because the snow is quiet and peaceful.

questions.prompt: Why do many people travel to a different climate on holiday?
questions.explanation: I think many people travel to a different climate because they want something new. If you live in a cold country, a warm beach feels like a real escape, and if you live somewhere hot, snow is exciting because you never see it. A different climate also changes what you can do, such as swimming or skiing. For most people, a holiday should feel completely different from ordinary life at home.

questions.prompt: Describe the picture.
questions.explanation: In the first picture, I can see four colleagues sitting around a table in an office. They are looking at charts and papers, and one of them is pointing at a document. In the second picture, two people are sitting on the grass in a park. They have a laptop and a phone, and they are working outside in the sunshine. Both pictures show people working, but the places are completely different.

questions.prompt: Which type of work do you prefer to do?
questions.explanation: I would prefer working in the office, at least for a meeting like the one in the first picture. When everyone is around one table it is easier to discuss and to point at the same document. Working on the grass looks lovely, but I think the sun on the screen would be a problem, and my back would hurt after an hour. For quiet work alone, though, I would happily sit outside.

questions.prompt: Why do some people like working outdoors?
questions.explanation: I think more people work outside the office now because technology makes it possible. With a laptop and a phone, you can work almost anywhere. Many companies also allow flexible working, so staff choose cafes, parks or their own homes. People say they feel less stressed and more creative outside. After the pandemic, a lot of businesses realised that staff can do good work without sitting in an office all day.

title: Đề 40 - Learning outdoors vs in a classroom

questions.prompt: Describe the picture.
questions.explanation: In the first picture, I can see a teacher sitting on the grass with three young children. They are wearing red hats and there are papers on a rug in front of them. In the second picture, a teacher is standing in front of a blackboard in a classroom, and the children are sitting at desks with their hands up. Both pictures show a lesson, but one is outside and one is indoors.

questions.prompt: Which kind of lesson do you think children enjoy more?
questions.explanation: I think children enjoy the outdoor lesson more. When they sit on the grass, they can move around and the lesson feels like play rather than study. Being outside is also good for their health. However, the classroom is better for learning to read and write, because the room is quiet and everyone can see the board clearly. In my opinion, a school should use both kinds of lesson, depending on the subject.

questions.prompt: Why do some schools take lessons outside the classroom?
questions.explanation: I think schools take lessons outside for several reasons. Children get fresh air and sunshine, which is good for their health. They also remember things better when they can see and touch real examples, such as plants or insects. Being outside makes the lesson feel new and exciting, so the children pay more attention. Many teachers also say that behaviour improves when children are not sitting still all morning.

questions.prompt: Tell me about a time when you received an important phone call or email.
How did you feel when you received it?
Why do some people prefer a phone call to a written message?

title: Đề 47 - Learning to ride a bicycle

questions.prompt: Describe the picture.
questions.explanation: In this picture, I can see a woman and a young boy outside in a park. The boy is wearing a blue helmet and an orange top, and he is sitting on a bicycle. The woman is standing behind him with her hands on the bike to keep it steady. She is smiling and looking down at him. Behind them there are green trees and grass everywhere, so it must be a warm summer day.

questions.prompt: What do you think about children learning to ride a bicycle?
questions.explanation: I think learning to ride a bicycle is very good for children. It teaches them balance and gives them confidence, because at first they are afraid of falling. It is also good exercise and it lets them play outside instead of sitting at home. Of course, parents worry about traffic, so children need a safe place to practise. In my opinion, every child should learn, and the earlier they start, the easier it is.

questions.prompt: Why do fewer children play outside these days?
questions.explanation: I think fewer children play outside now for several reasons. The main one is that they have phones and computers, so they can play games at home. Traffic is also much heavier than before, and parents do not feel safe letting children out alone. In many cities there are fewer parks and open spaces than there used to be. Children are also much busier with extra classes in the evening, so they simply have far less free time than before.

questions.prompt: Describe the picture.
questions.explanation: In this picture, I can see a young girl sitting on a small horse. She is wearing a black riding helmet and a pink top. A woman is standing next to the horse, holding its head and smiling at the girl. They are outside on a farm, and behind them I can see a white fence and bare trees. It looks like a cold but sunny day.

questions.prompt: What do you think about children learning to ride horses?
questions.explanation: I think riding a horse is a very good activity for children. It teaches them to be patient and gentle, because a horse will not do anything if you are rough with it. It also builds confidence, since sitting on a big animal is frightening at first. The main problem is that riding is expensive and there are not many places to learn. Still, I think children who try it learn something they cannot learn in a classroom.

questions.prompt: Why do some people enjoy spending time with animals?
questions.explanation: I think people enjoy being with animals for several reasons. Animals are honest, and they do not judge you or argue with you. Looking after a pet also gives people something to care about, especially if they live alone. Many studies say that spending time with animals reduces stress and helps people relax. For children, it is also a good way to learn responsibility from an early age.

questions.prompt: Describe the picture.
questions.explanation: In this picture, I can see a man and a woman carrying a sofa together. The sofa is dark green and it looks heavy. They are both holding one end and walking slowly across the room. The room is empty and very bright, with three tall windows and a wooden floor. I think they have just moved into this flat, because there is no other furniture yet.

questions.prompt: What do you think about moving to a new home?
questions.explanation: I think moving to a new home is exciting but also very stressful. It is exciting because you can start again and arrange everything the way you want. However, packing takes a long time, and you always find things you forgot. Moving is also expensive once you add the transport and the new furniture. In my opinion, the first week in a new place is difficult, but after that it starts to feel like home.

questions.prompt: Why do people ask friends to help them move?
questions.explanation: I think people ask friends to help because moving is simply too much for one person. Furniture like a sofa or a bed cannot be carried alone, so you need at least two people. Hiring a company is also expensive, and many young people cannot afford it. Having friends there makes a boring job much more enjoyable, and people usually thank them with food or drinks afterwards.

questions.prompt: Describe the picture.
questions.explanation: In this picture, I can see four young people running together on the sand. Two of them are men and two are women, and they are all wearing sports clothes. They are holding each other's arms as they run, and everybody is smiling. Behind them there is a low sandy hill covered with some green plants. It looks like a bright, warm morning somewhere by the sea.

questions.prompt: Do you prefer exercising alone or with other people?
questions.explanation: I prefer exercising with other people, because it keeps me going. When I run alone, I stop as soon as I feel tired, but with a friend I am too embarrassed to give up. Talking also makes the time pass faster. However, exercising alone has its advantages, since you can choose your own speed and go whenever you want. For me, the best answer is a mixture of both.

questions.prompt: Why do some people find it hard to exercise regularly?
questions.explanation: I think many people find it hard to exercise regularly because they are busy. After a long day at work, most people are too tired to go to the gym. The weather is also a problem, especially when it is very hot or raining. Some people start with a plan that is too difficult and then give up quickly. In my opinion, the main reason is that people expect results too soon.

title: Đề 41 - Living in a cold city vs a warm city

questions.prompt: Describe the picture.
questions.explanation: In the first picture, I can see three people walking across a bridge in winter. Everything is white with snow, and they are wearing thick coats, hats and scarves. In the second picture, people are walking along the seaside in a sunny city. There are tall palm trees, small boats and a church tower behind them. The two pictures show the same thing, people walking outside, in completely different weather.

questions.prompt: Which of these places would you rather live in?
questions.explanation: I would rather live in the warm city. I grew up in a hot country, so I am used to the sun, and I think I would find the snow difficult after a few weeks. In the warm place you can be outside all year, and life happens in the street rather than indoors. However, I understand why people love winter, because the snow is quiet and beautiful, and the summer heat can be exhausting.

questions.prompt: Why do some people move to a country with a different climate?
questions.explanation: I think people move to a different climate for several reasons. Many of them move for work or study, and the weather is simply part of the package. Others move because the climate at home makes them uncomfortable, for example people who cannot stand the cold. Some retired people move somewhere warm for their health. Family is also a common reason, because people follow their children or their partner.

title: Đề 51 - Security cameras & Professionalism at work

questions.prompt: What is the speaker's opinion about security cameras at work?
options: People are unnecessarily worried about them
Most people don't even realize cameras are present.
Cameras should be placed to ensure complete coverage.
questions.explanation:
Our workplace wellbeing session today begins with the topic that filled the suggestion box: the security cameras installed last month. I have read every note, and I want to respond honestly. Many of you wrote that you feel watched, even judged. My view, after sitting with the facts, is that people are worrying more than the situation deserves. Two claims from the notes need correcting. Somebody argued that most staff do not even realise the cameras exist — clearly untrue, given that they filled our suggestion box. Somebody else demanded the opposite: cameras extended into every corner of every room for what they called complete coverage. That would be excessive and will not happen. The cameras cover entrances, corridors and the equipment store. Nobody watches live feeds, and recordings are opened only when an incident requires them.
Let me offer a different frame for the anxious among us. When a package vanished from reception last year, we spent three unpleasant weeks in suspicion — a camera would have ended it in an hour. When the fire door was propped open all summer, nobody could say by whom. These little lenses answer questions that otherwise poison a workplace. I know they can feel intimidating, and I have heard the argument that they only matter after trouble has already struck. I would put it the other way: their presence should reassure us. The company is not doubting the people in this room. It is standing guard for them.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
(Bản variant camera #3 — bối cảnh buổi wellbeing.)
1. Đáp án: People are unnecessarily worried about them. Bẫy: "don't realize cameras are present" ("clearly untrue") và "complete coverage" ("excessive and will not happen").
2. Đáp án: People should feel reassured about their presence. Bẫy: "intimidating" và "only useful after incidents" đều được nhắc rồi lật lại.

questions.prompt: How does the speaker suggest people should feel about security cameras at work?
options: People often find them intimidating and invasive.
Many believe they are only useful after incidents have occurred.
People should feel reassured about their presence

questions.prompt: What does the expert say being professional is all about?
options: To create a good working environment.
questions.explanation:
For the second half of our session, an expert takes the floor on professionalism — what it truly is, and where it is heading. People decorate this word with many meanings. Ask around the office and you will hear that being professional is about building a good working environment; ask the sales floor and you will hear it is about making a good impression on clients. Pleasant ideas, but they confuse the fruit with the tree. Professionalism is all about maintaining a positive attitude. Friendliness under pressure, openness to other views, the willingness to help without being asked — that attitude is what colleagues and clients actually experience. Impressions and environments are not built; they are grown, and positive attitude is the soil they grow from.
Now, the question of definition. There are veterans who insist professionalism means exactly what it meant forty years ago: the pressed suit, the formal letter, the unquestioned hierarchy. There are also younger colleagues hoping the modern definition is final, ready to be memorised once and used forever. Both are mistaken, and in the same way: our definition of professionalism is changing, and it has never stopped changing. Globalisation added cultural fluency to the job description; technology added digital competence; remote work is adding new rules as we speak. Treat professionalism as a moving target and you will always be aiming correctly. Treat it as a monument, and you will be photographing something that has already walked away.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
(Bản variant professionalism #3.)
1. Đáp án: To maintain a positive attitude. Bẫy: "working environment" và "good impression" — "confuse the fruit with the tree".
2. Đáp án: Our definition of it is changing. Bẫy: "same as 40 years ago" và "will not change anymore" — "Both are mistaken".

questions.prompt: What does the expert say about the definition of professionalism?
options: It is the same as 40 years ago.
Our definition of it is changing.

title: Đề 35 - Making films + A famous singer

questions.prompt: Put the sentences in the correct order.
options: This is because they were all in black and white, and they had no sound.
In addition to these technical limitations, the film producers also had a limited budget.
Things have changed over time, and some of them now earn millions of dollars for appearing in films.
Films from that period were very different from films of today.
This lack of money mainly affected the actors, and they did not earn a lot of money.
During this education, he learned to be creative and to practise singing on stage.
Before becoming famous at this young age, he studied art and music at high school.
They started to follow him on social media, and now he is very popular.
In these performances, he liked to wear bright clothes and paint his face.
This strange way of dressing and his songs have attracted people's attention.
questions.explanation:
--- GIẢI THÍCH ---
Dạng sắp xếp câu: tìm câu mở đầu (không trỏ ngược), rồi bám vào đại từ, từ chỉ định và từ nối để nối dần.

▸ Making films — thứ tự đúng:
  0. "In 1895, the Grand Café in France showed the first ever commercial film." → câu cho sẵn, nêu mốc thời gian và sự kiện đầu tiên.
  1. "Films from that period were very different from films of today." → "that period" trỏ thẳng về năm 1895 ở câu cho sẵn.
  2. "This is because they were all in black and white, and they had no sound." → "This is because" giải thích cho ý "very different" ở câu trước.
  3. "In addition to these technical limitations, the film producers also had a limited budget." → "these technical limitations" gom lại ý đen trắng và không có tiếng.
  4. "This lack of money mainly affected the actors, and they did not earn a lot of money." → "This lack of money" trỏ về "a limited budget".
  5. "Things have changed over time, and some of them now earn millions of dollars for appearing in films." → "some of them" trỏ về "the actors", chốt bằng tương phản quá khứ với hiện tại.

▸ The famous singer — thứ tự đúng:
  0. "Jade Nobelton is only 18 years old, and he is a famous singer." → câu cho sẵn, giới thiệu nhân vật.
  1. "Before becoming famous at this young age, he studied art and music at high school." → "this young age" trỏ về "18 years old".
  2. "During this education, he learned to be creative and to practise singing on stage." → "this education" trỏ về việc học ở high school.
  3. "In these performances, he liked to wear bright clothes and paint his face." → "these performances" trỏ về "singing on stage".
  4. "This strange way of dressing and his songs have attracted people's attention." → "This strange way of dressing" trỏ về quần áo sặc sỡ và vẽ mặt.
  5. "They started to follow him on social media, and now he is very popular." → "They" trỏ về "people" ở câu trước, chốt bằng kết quả hiện tại.

questions.prompt: Let's talk about school. Can you tell me about the first school you went to?
questions.explanation: My first school was a small primary school about ten minutes from my house. The building was old and painted yellow, with a large tree in the middle of the yard. I started there when I was six years old. I still remember my first teacher, who was very patient with us. I walked there with my older sister every morning.

questions.prompt: What did you enjoy most about being at school?
questions.explanation: What I enjoyed most was break time with my friends. We played football in the yard or just talked about cartoons. I also liked art lessons because I could draw whatever I wanted. Lessons were sometimes difficult, especially maths, but the atmosphere was friendly. Looking back, I think I enjoyed the people more than the subjects.

questions.prompt: Do you still keep in touch with anyone from school?
questions.explanation: Yes, I still keep in touch with two or three close friends from school. We do not meet often because we all work in different cities now, but we chat in a group on social media. Sometimes we meet for coffee during holidays and talk about our old teachers. It is nice to have friends who knew me when I was young.

questions.prompt: Let's talk about animals. What is your favourite animal?
questions.explanation: My favourite animal is the dog because dogs are loyal and friendly. They are always happy to see you when you come home, even after a bad day. I also like that dogs are easy to train and enjoy being outside. When I was a child, my neighbour had a brown dog that followed me everywhere. I have liked dogs ever since.

questions.prompt: Have you ever had a pet?
questions.explanation: Yes, my family had a cat when I was in secondary school. Her name was Mia and she was grey and white. She slept on my bed almost every night and woke me up when she was hungry. Taking care of her taught me to be responsible. She lived with us for about eight years. I still miss her sometimes.

questions.prompt: Do you think people in your country like keeping pets?
questions.explanation: Yes, I think keeping pets is quite popular in Vietnam, especially in the cities. Many young people keep small dogs or cats in their apartments. In the countryside, families often keep dogs to guard the house rather than as pets. I have noticed more pet shops and pet cafes opening recently, so the habit seems to be growing.

title: Đề 42 - Cooking alone vs cooking together

questions.prompt: Describe the two pictures.
questions.explanation: These two pictures both show people cooking, but in very different places. In the first picture a woman is standing alone on a hillside. She is cooking something on a small camping stove that is placed on a rock. Next to it I can see a flask and a cup. The second picture shows a man and a woman in a modern kitchen. They are both wearing black aprons and the woman is cutting a red pepper. So one person is cooking alone outdoors and two people are cooking together indoors.

questions.prompt: Which way of cooking would you prefer? Why?
questions.explanation: If I had to choose, I would prefer cooking with another person. I am not a very confident cook, so having someone next to me makes it easier. Cooking together is also a good way to talk while you work. The first picture looks peaceful, but I think I would feel lonely out there. Having said that, I sometimes enjoy cooking alone at the weekend. It depends on my mood, but usually I choose company.

questions.prompt: Why do you think cooking with other people is becoming popular?
questions.explanation: I think cooking together is becoming popular because people have less time to meet. Making a meal gives friends a reason to spend two or three hours together. It is also cheaper than going to a restaurant every week. For example, my friends and I have cooked at each other's houses once a month for years. Of course, a small kitchen can get crowded and noisy. Still, I think people enjoy making something with their hands together.

title: Đề 43 - Video games vs board games

questions.prompt: Describe the two pictures.
questions.explanation: Both pictures show families playing games at home, but with different equipment. In the first picture a mother and her young son, who looks about six, are sitting on a grey sofa. Each of them is holding a game controller and they are both laughing. The second picture shows three people on the floor of a bedroom. A father, a mother and a small girl are playing a word game with wooden letters. So one family is playing a video game and the other is playing a board game.

questions.prompt: Which kind of game do you think is better for families? Why?
questions.explanation: I think board games are better for families, like in the second picture. When you play a board game everyone sits together and looks at each other. You have to talk, wait for your turn and explain the rules to children. Video games are exciting, but people often stare at the screen and say nothing. Having said that, playing a video game together is still better than watching television. So I would choose the board game for family time.

questions.prompt: Why do you think many families still play board games today?
questions.explanation: I think families still play board games because they are simple and cheap. You do not need electricity or a good internet connection. They are also easy for different ages, so grandparents and children can play together. For example, my family has played the same card game every Tet for years. Of course, some board games take a very long time to finish. Still, they give families a reason to sit in the same room.

title: Đề 45 - Walking in the countryside vs walking in a park

questions.prompt: Describe the two pictures.
questions.explanation: Both pictures show people going for a walk together. In the first picture I can see a family of four who are walking away from the camera. The two parents and two girls are holding hands. They are walking along a dirt road between fields of wheat. The second picture shows a mother and her small child in a park. They are walking towards the camera and both of them are smiling. Behind them there is a lake. So one walk is in the countryside and the other is in a park.

questions.prompt: Where do you prefer to go walking? Why?
questions.explanation: I prefer walking in the countryside, like the family in the first picture. The air is cleaner and there is much less noise from traffic. You can walk for an hour without meeting anyone, which I find relaxing. Parks are convenient, but they are often crowded at the weekend. Having said that, I only reach the countryside two or three times a year. So in practice I walk in the park near my house almost every day.

questions.prompt: Why do you think walking is such a popular activity?
questions.explanation: I think walking is popular because anyone can do it. You do not need equipment, a gym membership or any special skill. It is also free, which makes it suitable for every age and income. For example, my parents have walked around the lake every evening for ten years. Of course, it is not enough exercise if you want to get really fit. Still, it is the easiest way for most people to stay healthy.

title: Đề 44 - An old house vs a modern home

questions.prompt: Describe the two pictures.
questions.explanation: Both pictures show homes, but they are completely different. In the first picture a man who is wearing a red patterned shirt stands in front of an old house. The walls are yellow and the paint is cracked in places. The second picture shows the inside of a modern home. A man is sitting at a long table and reading a newspaper. A woman is standing near the window, looking outside. So one is an old house and the other is a new one.

questions.prompt: Which of these two homes would you prefer to live in? Why?
questions.explanation: I would prefer to live in the modern home in the second picture. It looks comfortable and there is a lot of space and light. The kitchen and dining room are large, so a family could eat together easily. The old house in the first picture has character, but it looks small and difficult to repair. Having said that, I would not want a home that feels cold or unfriendly. So I would choose the modern house, but I would try to make it warm.

questions.prompt: Why do you think some people prefer old houses to new ones?
questions.explanation: I think some people prefer old houses because they have character. Every old house has a history and looks different from the others. New buildings often look exactly the same, especially in big cities. Old houses are also usually in older neighbourhoods, where people know each other. For example, my grandparents have lived in the same old house for forty years. Of course, they need a lot of repair, which many people cannot afford.

title: Đề 46 - A garden in the country vs a balcony in the city

questions.prompt: Describe the two pictures.
questions.explanation: Both pictures show people outdoors, but in very different places. In the first picture two people who are working in a vegetable garden. An older man with white hair is digging with a long tool. A young woman in a straw hat is pulling out weeds. The second picture shows a young woman standing on a balcony. She is wearing a pink cap and leaning on the railing. Behind her there are tall apartment buildings. So one place is green and the other is full of concrete.

questions.prompt: Which of these two places would you rather spend your free time in? Why?
questions.explanation: I would rather spend my free time in the garden in the first picture. I like being outside and I find gardening relaxing after a week at work. You can also see the result of what you have done, which is satisfying. The balcony in the second picture is quiet, but the view is only buildings. Having said that, a balcony is much easier to reach than a garden. So I would choose the garden, even though it is more work.

questions.prompt: Why do you think many people in cities want a garden or some plants?
questions.explanation: I think city people want plants because they miss nature. Cities are full of concrete, traffic and noise, so anything green feels calming. Growing something is also a way to relax after work. For example, my aunt has grown herbs on her balcony for years. Of course, most apartments have very little space or sunlight. Still, even a few small pots can make a flat feel more alive.

title: Đề 51 - Taking photos of a view

questions.prompt: Describe the picture.
questions.explanation: This photo was taken high up on a green hill. Two young people are standing in the long grass. The man has his back to us and is holding a camera up to his face. He is taking a picture of the woman, who is smiling at him. She has a camera around her neck as well. Behind them I can see rows of green mountains. The weather looks cool and slightly cloudy.

questions.prompt: Do you like taking photographs when you travel? Why or why not?
questions.explanation: Yes, I always take photographs when I travel. I like having something to look at later, because I forget details very quickly. I usually take pictures of food and of the streets that I walk through, rather than of myself. Last summer I filled my whole phone in about four days. Sometimes I take too many and never look at them again, and my friends laugh at how often I stop. Even so, I would feel strange going somewhere new without my camera.

questions.prompt: Why do you think people enjoy looking at beautiful scenery?
questions.explanation: I think people enjoy beautiful scenery because it helps them relax. When you look at mountains or the sea, your mind becomes quiet for a while. It is also a change from the city, where everything is crowded and noisy. Most of us spend the whole week indoors looking at a screen. For example, my family drives to the countryside when we feel tired, and we always come back calmer. A wide view makes daily problems feel smaller.

questions.prompt: Describe the picture.
questions.explanation: This photo was taken in a bright living room with a large white sofa. I can see three young women who are looking at the same phone. One of them is sitting on the sofa and leaning forward. The other two are sitting on the floor. The woman in the middle is holding the phone so everyone can see the screen. All three of them are laughing. Behind them there is a big window with a garden outside.

questions.prompt: How often do you use social media?
questions.explanation: I usually use social media in the evening, after I finish work. I check messages from my friends and look at photos they have posted. I also use it during my lunch break if I have some free time. In the morning I try not to open it, because it makes me late. I would say I spend about an hour a day on it in total.

questions.prompt: Why do people love sharing their photos on social media?
questions.explanation: I think people share happy moments because they want to keep in touch with friends. It is faster than telling the same story ten times. Sharing good news also makes the moment feel more real and more important. For example, my cousin posted her graduation photos and got hundreds of messages. Of course, some people only show the perfect side of their lives. Still, most of us just enjoy being seen by people who care about us.

questions.prompt: Describe the picture.
questions.explanation: This photo was taken in a small office with white walls and a red curtain. A woman who is wearing a black dress is sitting at a wooden desk. She is holding a phone to her ear with one hand and a pen in the other hand. On the desk in front of her there are papers with colourful charts. There is also a computer screen on the right. She looks serious and is thinking carefully about the call.

questions.prompt: Tell me about a time when you had to make a difficult decision.
questions.explanation: Last year I had to decide whether to change my job. I had worked at the same company for four years and I felt comfortable there. Then a smaller company offered me a better salary but a longer journey to work. I made a list of good and bad points and talked to my family. In the end I accepted the offer. It was difficult at first, but I do not regret it.

questions.prompt: Why do you think some people find it hard to make decisions?
questions.explanation: I think some people find decisions hard because they are afraid of choosing wrongly. They worry about what will happen if the choice turns out badly. Having too many options also makes it more difficult. For example, I have a friend who spent a month choosing a phone and was still unsure. Some people also care too much about what others will think. In my opinion, it is often better to decide quickly and then adjust.

questions.prompt: Describe the picture.
questions.explanation: This photo was taken in a living room with white brick walls. I can see five friends who are watching a football match on television. Three of them are sitting on a grey sofa and one is sitting on the floor. They are waving small flags and cheering loudly. One man is holding a football and another one is blowing a horn. On the wooden table in front of them there is pizza and some drinks. Everyone looks excited.

questions.prompt: Do you enjoy watching sports? Why or why not?
questions.explanation: Yes, I enjoy watching sports, especially football. I like the excitement of not knowing who will win until the last minute. I usually watch matches with my brother at home on Saturday evenings. I do not play football very well myself, but I enjoy following my favourite team. The only problem is that some matches finish very late at night. Even so, I would not want to miss an important game.

questions.prompt: Why do you think people prefer watching sports with other people?
questions.explanation: I think people prefer watching sports together because it is more exciting. When your team scores, you want to celebrate with someone. Watching alone at home feels quiet and a bit boring. Being in a group also means you can argue about the referee afterwards. For example, my friends and I have met at the same coffee shop for every big match. Sport is really a reason to spend time together.

questions.prompt: Describe the picture.
questions.explanation: This photo was taken inside a library. I can see five students who are sitting at a long table. They are all young, and they look about twenty years old. Each of them is looking down at a book or a notebook. One student on the right is turning the page of a large book. There is also a laptop open in front of them. Behind them I can see shelves full of books. The room is quiet and everyone is concentrating.

questions.prompt: Do you prefer studying alone or with other people? Why?
questions.explanation: I prefer studying alone, especially when the work is difficult. When I am on my own I can go at my own speed and stop when I want. With other people I often start talking and forget the work. However, I do like studying with a friend who is taking the same exam, because explaining something to someone else helps me understand it. So it really depends on what I have to do that day.

questions.prompt: Why do you think many students choose to study in libraries?
questions.explanation: I think students go to libraries because it is easier to concentrate there. At home there are many distractions, such as the television or family members. In a library everyone else is working, so you feel you should work too. Libraries are also free and have books that you cannot buy anywhere else. For example, I finished my whole thesis in the library near my house. It is simply a better environment for studying.

questions.prompt: Tell me about a time when you were responsible for something important.
questions.explanation: I want to tell you about the time I was responsible for my class's charity sale at school. It turned out to be much harder than I expected. It was in my final year, about three years ago. My teacher asked me to plan the stalls, collect the money and keep it safe. The part I remember most is that I carried the cash box home every evening and counted it twice. At that moment I felt proud but also quite worried, because the money was not mine. Later, we gave everything to a children's hospital, and the total was higher than anyone expected. These days, I still think about that week whenever somebody gives me an important task. About the feeling, the honest answer is that I was nervous first and proud second. This is mainly because everyone was watching me, and one mistake would have spoiled the whole event. For example, I checked the numbers every night because I was afraid of losing money. On the other hand, that pressure taught me to be careful and organised. On the last question, I think responsibility is good for young people because it helps them grow up. One reason is that when something depends on you, you stop making excuses and start solving problems.

questions.prompt: How did you feel about having that responsibility?
Why is it good for young people to take on responsibility?
Tell me about a time when you received some bad news.
questions.explanation: I want to tell you about the day I heard that I had failed my driving test. It turned out to be a smaller disaster than it felt at the time. It was last spring, after two months of lessons and practice. The examiner told me politely that I had made one serious mistake at a junction. The part I remember most is the quiet drive back with my father, who had come to celebrate. At that moment I felt embarrassed more than sad, because I had told my friends I would pass. Later, I booked another test for the next month and passed it easily. These days, I actually drive better because of that first failure. About dealing with it, I gave myself one evening to feel bad, and then I made a plan. This is mainly because sitting with bad news changes nothing, but a plan changes everything. For example, I wrote down the mistake I had made and practised that exact junction ten times. On the other hand, some people need more time, and that is fine. On the last question, I think people hide bad news because they want to protect others. One reason is that saying a thing out loud makes it real, and many people are not ready.
